title: With Troy Aikman possibly exiting broadcasting, he extends an olive branch to Jerry Jones
summary: Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman has talked openly for years about wanting to work in an NFL front office.
full_text: Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman has talked openly for years about wanting to work in an NFL front office. He took a half-step in that direction last year, becoming a consultant to the Dolphins and continuing to work for the team while also working for Monday Night Football . In March, Aikman spoke openly about the Cowboys’ historical lack of interest in pursuing his services. Now that Aikman's time with ESPN is by all appearances moving toward a conclusion, Aikman seems to be extending an olive branch toward Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones. Asked by Mike Fisher whether Aikman would break bread with Jerry Jones, Aikman said this: "I would have lunch, breakfast, or dinner with Jerry any time he wants it. And it wouldn't necessarily have to be because it's a job interview. Just because, you know, we go back a long way. . . . I came in, I was 22 years old. I was his very first draft pick. There's a lot within that relationship, both from the beginning, when he began as the owner, when I began my NFL career as a quarterback for 12 years of my life, playing for him, and then, even in the years that have followed, you know, we've been through a lot. We've been through the highest of highs, we've been through some pretty tough moments as well. Our relationship is complicated. I think he would agree with that, but it is one that's built, I believe, on respect. This week, he said some really kind things, which meant a lot to me, quite honestly. So, yeah, I would welcome any conversation with Jerry, and quite honestly I don't know if there would be, or if there ever would be an opportunity. But if Jerry came to me and felt that, in his heart, I could lend some services that would help make them better, I would — I’d have a hard time not taking a good look at that ." Jones did indeed speak glowingly about Aikman during this week's quarterly NFL ownership meetings. " Troy is very capable , and he's so, really relatively speaking, he's in his youth as careers go," Jones said. "And he's very capable of doing any one of a number of things, certainly anything to do with football. I don't know of any area short of getting that kind of feeling, I don't know of any area that Troy Aikman wouldn't be qualified and competent to go into." Aikman's current role with the Dolphins remains fluid and undefined, but it was enough to prompt the NFL to place Tom Brady-style restrictions on his ability to enter the facilities of other teams or to attend practices before Monday night games. Despite Aikman's unfulfilled aspiration to work in a front office, he seems to be realizing that his time as a broadcaster could be ending — and he's apparently feeling some regret over that. “As I’m into my last year at ESPN, I’m realizing that this is something that could very well be taken away from me ,” Aikman told Fisher, via Tyler Lauletta of Awful Announcing . “For the first time, I’m realizing how much I really do — I’ve always enjoyed it. I’ve always known that. But until you risk having something taken away from you, I think sometimes you tend to maybe take things for granted. “And so, for the first time probably in my career, I’m realizing, you know, this is a great profession. It’s been a great ride for me, and I hope it’s not over. Time will tell. But, yeah. So, we’ll see. I’m excited about what the rest of this year holds, and I’m excited to finally get back into the booth for a Super Bowl.” With CBS already deciding to make J.J. Watt the full-time replacement for Tony Romo, there may not be a high-profile (and high-paying) seat for Aikman in 2027. If he truly wants to continue to call games, the best spot could be Greg Olsen's current slot as the No. 2 NFL announcer on Fox. And the money that goes with that assignment. It's still not clear why ESPN has apparently soured on Aikman. Maybe he overplayed his hand, by reportedly asking for $30 million per year . Maybe ESPN wasn't thrilled by his Miami moonlighting, especially since it has complicated his ability to be as prepared to call games as he could be. (It's also possible that Aikman took the position with the Dolphins before running it by anyone at ESPN, which if accurate would tend to impair the relationship between ESPN and Aikman.) Regardless, Aikman is now making it known that his upcoming free agency sweeps more broadly than broadcasting. He's also officially in play for the Cowboys or any other team that may choose to consider hiring him.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saints elevate WR Cedric Tillman, OT Easton Kilty
summary: The Saints announced that they have elevated a pair of players from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
full_text: The Saints announced that they have elevated a pair of players from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Steelers. Wide receiver Cedric Tillman and offensive tackle Easton Kilty have been summoned to the active roster for the matchup in Paris. Both players will revert back after the game. Tillman has been elevated for two other games, so the Saints will need to sign him to the active roster if they want him back for another game. He has played five offensive snaps and one special teams snap so far this year. Kilty played on special teams in the Saints' Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
author: Josh Alper

title: CeeDee Lamb: We feel we have best roster in NFC East, so why not us?
summary: The first six weeks of the season have not gone as hoped for the Cowboys, but they head into Week 7 with the NFC East well within their grasp.
full_text: The first six weeks of the season have not gone as hoped for the Cowboys, but they head into Week 7 with the NFC East well within their grasp. The Giants lead the division with a 3-2-1 record while the Cowboys and Eagles are 2-4 ahead of their Monday night matchup. Should the Texans beat the Giants on Sunday, the winner of the Dallas-Philadelphia game will likely be feeling pretty good about their chances of navigating the final 10 games well enough to wind up hosting a playoff game in the first round of the postseason. On Friday, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb acknowledged that the Cowboys are "very fortunate that everybody else is playing pretty bad" because it has kept things within their reach and he shared his feeling that the team's talent will wind up winning out. "We think about it just like that ," Lamb said, via the team's website. "Anybody can win his division, so why not us? Every opportunity that we can get, we know what we're messing up, and what are our areas of improvement — like playing complementary ball. I feel like, at the end of the day, we feel like we have the best roster, top down, and we've got to be able to play like that on Sundays or Mondays." That last part has been the trickiest part for the Cowboys, but a couple of wins would make for a very different outlook in Dallas heading into the second half of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: The NFL should relocate the Steelers-Saints game in Paris to London
summary: NFL scraps multiple Saturday events due to ongoing protests.
full_text: '' With one day more to go until the Steelers and Saints play in Paris, the NFL shouldn't wait one hour more to relocate the game. No matter how safe and secure Stade de France will be for the game, it's not safe for NFL fans to be in Paris due to protests that from time to time morph into full-blown riots. Consider the latest moves made by the league as to the collateral activities. Via the Associated Press, the NFL announced on Saturday the closure of its "NFL House" event, due to "potential accessibility issues." Previously, the Steelers Fan House event was scrapped . The "Saints House" has been postponed until Sunday. Meanwhile, the U.S. State Department issued a security alert cautioning "Americans in Paris for the NFL game" to "exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings." Why would the NFL insist on pressing forward? The risk, however big or small it may be, isn't worth it. The league has said security at the game will be enhanced. Which necessarily means security resources that could be utilized elsewhere in the city are being devoted to something that is far from a necessity. Also, no matter how secure the stadium is, the fans who have bought tickets to the game will need to get to the perimeter where the NFL's security plan activates. A soccer match between PSG and Lyon recently was moved from Sunday to Monday , at the direction of French authorities. If the NFL won't do the prudent thing and move the game to London, the powers-that-be in Paris should direct the NFL to bump Steelers-Saints to Monday, too. (That would shift the game broadcast to Monday morning or afternoon, New York time. Which could inadvertently unlock a new standalone window for future NFL games.) It's surprising that it's gotten to this point. The warning signs have been obvious for weeks. On Friday, even the President chimed in . And the league's determination (or, more accurately, stubbornness) to proceed has led to a situation in which the NFL may still be forced to make an eleventh-hour-and-fifty-seventh-minute decision to do something other than play the game as scheduled. Which, for the teams, will only add to the overall in-season inconvenience of traveling to another country to play a football game. There's no reason to wait. They should make the move now. We're not privy to all of the specifics. The generalities continue to suggest that the league absolutely should pivot from the plan to play in Paris at 3:30 p.m. local time on Sunday. Why assume the risk that any fan will be endangered as they try to get to the game? Why take any risks that the enhanced security will be overrun by an event that the protester-rioters could see as a perfect opportunity to make their message resonate internationally? It seems to be increasingly obvious that relocation of the game is the right call. Even if nothing happens, there's already a cloud over the league's first-ever Paris game. And if there's even one incident in connection with playing the game as planned, the NFL will risk being dubbed what the French call les incompétents .
author: Mike Florio

title: Rhamondre Stevenson says Bears' defensive alignment helped with 48-yard TD
summary: Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson made one of the most stunning plays of this NFL season when he turned a short pass at the end of the first half and ran for a 48-yard touchdown against the Bears.
full_text: Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson made one of the most stunning plays of this NFL season when he turned a short pass at the end of the first half and ran for a 48-yard touchdown against the Bears. Stevenson said the Bears' defensive alignment made it possible. The Bears were so concerned about giving up a Hail Mary on the last play of the half that they put two defensive backs near the goal line, almost 50 yards downfield. The Bears also rushed six to try to prevent Patriots quarterback Drake Maye from having time to set up for a Hail Mary. But that meant the middle of the field was wide open. "It's kind of how they lined up pre-snap that got us into that play," Stevenson said. The Bears' defense seemed to be caught off-guard, not expecting Maye to dump it off to Stevenson only a yard past the line of scrimmage. And it's not surprising the Bears weren't expecting it, as scoring a touchdown in that situation is almost unheard of: According to Doug Clawson of CBS Sports, there have been 1,006 plays in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, starting more than 40 yards from the end zone, in which the ball was thrown less than 10 yards downfield, and Stevenson's catch was the only one of those 1,006 plays that turned into a touchdown. "I was just trying to make a play, put my team in a position to swing the game a little bit, as much as we can," Stevenson said. "We've been working on that play for a long time and it came in handy today. Executed on that play so it felt good to do that." Asked what his mindset was when Maye threw him the Ball, Stevenson answered, "Score." He did that, producing one of the best touchdowns of this NFL season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bears lead NFL in time of possession, but Ben Johnson would prefer one-play TD drives
summary: ""I've never been one for the time of possession stat. I don't know that that really equates to winning and losing," Johnson said.
full_text: '' The Bears lead the NFL in time of possession, but that doesn't matter to coach Ben Johnson. "I've never been one for the time of possession stat. I don't know that that really equates to winning and losing, necessarily. And yet when you look up, we were possessing the ball more than our opponent more often than not," Johnson said. The Bears' average time of possession of 35:30 per 60-minute game is the highest in the NFL, they've run 505 offensive plays this season, which is by far the most of any team, and they're the only team averaging more than 70 offensive plays per game. Johnson said he thinks about how long drives affect players, both on offense and defense, but that he's ultimately happier when his offense scores quickly than slowly. "It's not something that we stress," Johnson said. "We really talk more about getting explosive plays. I would rather have a one-play drive for a touchdown than a 10-play drive for a touchdown. But the ability to stay efficient, stay on schedule, I think that's something that good offenses show that they can do." The Bears have shown they're a good offense, even if sometimes it takes them longer to get into the end zone than Johnson would like.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lions' Sam LaPorta clarifies contract comments: "I want to play for this team"
summary: The Lions' tight end is hoping to get a contract extension from the Lions.
full_text: Lions tight end Sam LaPorta said this week that if he doesn't get a new contract from the Lions, he’ll go get paid somewhere else . LaPorta spoke to the media on Friday to clarify that "somewhere else" would not be his first choice. "I feel bad if there was any sort of distraction to the team or my teammates or the coaches, but I think there was maybe a bit of a misconception with, I guess — my intentions are I want to play for this team," LaPorta said. "I give everything I have. My teammates do, as well. They all love me, respect me and support me, and they want to see me be happy and be compensated." LaPorta has been disappointed with the offers the Lions have given him on a long-term extension, but he said he and his pregnant wife are still hoping to stay in Detroit for years. "I guess I wouldn't expect anybody else to really even care, but emotionally for me and my family, it's an important thing for us," LaPorta said. "We want to have stability. We're excited, in the coming months, we're gonna have our first kid, me and my wife. We're gonna welcome our baby girl into the world in Metro Detroit. We want to be here with the Lions. I guess I'm getting emotional about it, but in the grand scheme of things, it's really a business. And you have to respect what the front office is doing because they're the ones calling the shots. They're the ones that brought me in. This is my first team. They've been nothing but supportive of me and my career." LaPorta is in the fourth and final year of his rookie contract, and his base salary this year is $5.675 million. He knows he's lucky to make the money he's already making, but his contract is still a far cry from what the highest-paid tight ends in the NFL are making. "We're very blessed. I'm getting paid millions of dollars this year," LaPorta said. "But also, when I reflect on other people in the league, I feel like I'm doing just as good a job if not better, and I want to be paid like those guys."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Seahawks sent mixed signals about whether Zach Charbonnet would play on Sunday
summary: The Seahawks sent plenty of mixed signals this week regarding the question of whether running back Zach Charbonnet would play on Sunday.
full_text: The Seahawks sent plenty of mixed signals this week regarding the question of whether running back Zach Charbonnet would play on Sunday. On Friday, the decision came. He will not play. Charbonnet, who suffered a torn ACL in the divisional-round win over the 49ers in January, returned to practice on October 1. He was moved to the active roster this week, and he fully participated in practice on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. “Zach is going to have a full week’s worth of reps, so that’s exciting," coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Monday. "There is a possibility that you can see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that is exciting.” Speaking to reporters on Friday, Macdonald's explanation created the impression that Charbonnet not playing on Sunday was the plan all along. "We’re going along with the plan," Macdonald said. "Plan was to get a great week’s worth of work and see where we’re at. We’re going to take it into next week. It’s part of the plan. Zach’s doing great and we’ll go into next week and see how it goes.” The situation doesn't violate the injury-reporting rules, even if the Seahawks arguably created the impression Charbonnet would play. Actually, the Seahawks could have milked the uncertainty for two more days. Charbonnet could have been listed as questionable on Friday, with the decision announced on Sunday that he won't be among the active players. Still, it feels odd. Especially since Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL said on Friday's Pat McAfee Show that Rapoport expects Charbonnet to "play and play a lot" on Sunday night. (The clip apparently was deleted from Twitter, but it's still in the YouTube version of the episode.) At a time when more and more fans are skeptical of the impact of gambling and prediction-market influences on the flow of information (and/or misinformation), this is another tangible piece of grist for the tinfoil-hat mill.
author: Mike Florio

title: President Trump on Sunday's game in Paris: "The NFL probably could have postponed"
summary: The NFL plans to press forward with Sunday's game between the Steelers and Saints in Paris.
full_text: The NFL plans to press forward with Sunday's game between the Steelers and Saints in Paris. Asked about the situation by reporters on Friday, President Trump expressed misgivings about the decision. “ Well, you worry about it ," he said. "It's not — I think maybe it’s looking like tomorrow's gonna be a bad day in France. So you worry about it. I would have said the NFL could have probably postponed that match, if you want to know the truth. Because France is really in trouble." Postponement isn't really possible, given the NFL's schedule. Relocation would make the most sense, with the game moving to one of the two NFL-ready stadiums in London. (As best we can tell, both Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and Wembley Stadium are available.) For now, the NFL's attitude is "the show must go on." Even if the show could end up being something far different than what the NFL has envisioned.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kenneth Walker III, who had blood clots in high school, says Jalen Hurts flying is "crazy"
summary: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III dealt with blood clots in his lungs in high school.
full_text: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III dealt with blood clots in his lungs in high school. He thought his football career would be over, before it even got started. During his Friday press conference, he was asked about Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is currently dealing with blood clots in his lungs. "Yeah, honestly, just stay positive ," Walker said. "You know, obviously, I guess you know about what happened in high school, like, with the blood clots and everything. And he went on the flight, huh, and everything? Yeah, that's crazy. "You know, honestly, just stay positive, and, you know, do all the things necessary that he need to do, like, to get his body back right. But, yeah, I'll be praying for him, because that's not something, you know, we should take lightly." Walker's reaction to the fact that Hurts flew to London and back again isn't uncommon. And with neither the Eagles nor the league providing any real clarity on how that came to be, everyone will have to wait for the results of the investigation requested by the NFL Players Association. If, of course, the results of that investigation are shared with the public.
author: Mike Florio

title: Three teams could be undefeated through seven weeks, which is a rarity
summary: Entering Week 7, three teams are undefeated.
full_text: Entering Week 7, three teams are undefeated. If three teams exit Week 7 undefeated, it will be a rarity. The 49ers take their 6-0 record to Atlanta. The 5-0 Chiefs face the Seahawks in Seattle. The 5-0 Vikings play the Colts in Minneapolis. Via NBC Sports research, only twice since the merger have three or more teams been undefeated through seven weeks of a season (with the exception of the 1982 strike year). In 2009, three teams were unbeaten through seven weeks: the Saints, Colts, and Broncos. In 2015, five teams were perfect through seven weeks: the Panthers, Packers, Broncos, Patriots, and Bengals. On both occasions, two of the unbeaten teams through seven weeks made it to the Super Bowl. In 2009, it was the Colts and the Saints. In 2015, the Panthers and the Broncos played in the Super Bowl. The 49ers last went 7-0 in 2019. That year, they made it to the Super Bowl, losing to the Chiefs. The Chiefs last went 6-0 in 2024, when they made it to the Super Bowl for the third straight year, losing to the Eagles. The Vikings last went 6-0 in 2009. They lost to the Saints in the NFC Championship.
author: Mike Florio

title: George Pickens: "I'm doing what they tell me to do"
summary: On Thursday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer had some things to say about receiver George Pickens.
full_text: '' On Thursday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer had some things to say about receiver George Pickens. The message was that Pickens needs to do more during the plays in which he doesn't get the ball. That's not how Pickens heard it. “Well, I’m doing what they tell me to do ," Pickens told reporters on Friday, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . "So, do what they tell me to do.” As to the specific message from Schottenheimer that Pickens needs to do a better job of blocking, Pickens didn't take it as something that was intended only for him. “I feel like if you narrow the comments down, you’re talking about the team," Pickens said. "Most definitely, I feel like as a team, just keep improving.” Pickens can take it however he wants. And he's right; improvement across the board is needed. Still, it sure seemed like Schottenheimer was singling out Pickens. If Pickens doesn't want to take it that way, that's his prerogative.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley remained limited in Friday's practice
summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) remained a limited practice participant on Friday.
full_text: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) remained a limited practice participant on Friday. He is hoping to return for Monday night's game against the Cowboys. The Eagles had five changes to their injury report, including downgrading outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard (ankle) to out of practice. Greenard was limited on Thursday. The Eagles added offensive tackle Fred Johnson (illness) as a limited participant. Offensive lineman Drew Kendall (knee) and linebacker AJ Epenesa (back) were full participants Friday after limited work on Thursday, and offensive lineman Willie Lampkin (illness) had limited participation after missing Thursday's session. Defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were out of practice again. Guard Landon Dickerson (knee, pectoral), linebacker Jonathan Greenard (ankle), linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee, ankle), defensive tackle Moro Ojomo (abdomen) and guard Tyler Steen (shoulder) joined Barkley as limited participants.
author: Charean Williams

title: Broncos CB Patrick Surtain II is questionable
summary: The Broncos could get cornerback Patrick Surtain II back this week.
full_text: The Broncos could get cornerback Patrick Surtain II back this week. Surtain is questionable with his ankle injury. He has not played since Week 4 when he was injured against the 49ers. Surtain had a third consecutive limited practice on Friday after returning to practice this week. Running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) also could return. Coleman, who went on injured reserve after Week 2, had his 21-day return-to-practice window opened Wednesday. He has had three consecutive full practices. The Broncos ruled out running back Tyler Badie (thumb), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). None practiced this week. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) improved to a full participant on Friday after being limited in Denver's first two practices of the week. Waddle was not assigned a game status. Cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) was also a full participant on Friday and not given an injury designation.
author: Charean Williams

title: Former Rams RB Lawrence McCutcheon dies at 76
summary: Former Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon died Friday, the team announced.
full_text: Former Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon died Friday, the team announced. He was 76. McCutcheon played eight seasons with the Rams (1972-79) and was a five-time Pro Bowl selection and second-team All-Pro honoree. "It is with great sadness that we share the passing of our husband, brother, father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, Lawrence McCutcheon," the McCutcheon family said in a statement. "Clutch passed away on Oct. 23 with family at his bedside following a long, courageous battle with Parkinson's disease. "Through a decade-long playing career and another 32 years in the Rams' front office, Clutch earned the respect and admiration of teammates, opposing players, colleagues and fans alike. Clutch will be missed and remembered forever. "We are thankful to those in our community who have reached out with love and support. In lieu of flowers, we ask that those wishing to honor Clutch please donate to the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's research." McCutcheon also played for Denver, Seattle and Buffalo, retiring after the 1981 season. He finished his career with 1,521 carries for 6,578 yards and 26 touchdowns, adding 198 catches for 1,799 yards and 13 touchdowns. McCutcheon played 109 games with 82 starts. “The Los Angeles Rams are deeply saddened by the passing of Lawrence McCutcheon," the team said in a statement. "His impact on this organization spanned generations, and he embodied what it means to be a Ram. A five-time Pro Bowl running back and once the franchise’s all-time leading rusher, he later served in our front office as a scout and director of player personnel. His legacy is woven into the fabric of our team. "We extend our heartfelt condolences to the McCutcheon family as we celebrate a life that gave so much to the Rams and to our game.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Vikings release RB Deejay Dallas
summary: The Vikings released running back Deejay Dallas on Friday, according to the NFL's personnel notice.
full_text: The Vikings released running back Deejay Dallas on Friday, according to the NFL's personnel notice. The move makes room for running back Jordan Mason's return to the active roster. Mason fractured his thumb in the season opener against the Packers, and the Vikings placed him on injured reserve Sept. 16. He has a questionable designation for Sunday's game, but Dallas' release signals that Mason will play. Dallas is not subject to waivers and could sign back to the team's practice squad on Saturday and be activated for Sunday's game, if the Vikings so choose. Dallas has played 40 offensive snaps and 92 on special teams in five games this season. He has seven touches for 44 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jordan Love, Christian Watson among Packers off injury report and set to play vs. Lions
summary: Earlier this week, Packers quarterback Jordan Love told reporters he would be available to play on Sunday, despite being listed as limited on Wednesday with a back issue.
full_text: ' Earlier this week, Packers quarterback Jordan Love told reporters he would be available to play on Sunday, despite being listed as limited on Wednesday with a back issue. Now that has become official. Love has no injury designation on Green Bay's final practice report of the week and is set to play against Detroit. Receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Savion Williams (ankle), and Matthew Golden (shoulder) are also off the injury report and are all set to play, despite being listed as limited all week. Guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), receiver Bo Melton (back), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackle Jordan Riley (Achilles) are all questionable. Defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), and edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness) are also off the injury report and are set to play. Head coach Matt LaFleur noted earlier on Friday that linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) is out after suffering an injury on Thursday .
author: Myles Simmons

title: NFL admits a penalty by the Cowboys in Week 5 was assessed against the Bucs
summary: The NFL has admitted a rather embarrassing officiating mistake from Week 5: When Buccaneers defensive lineman Calijah Kancey was called for illegal hands to the face, it was actually a Cowboys player who put his hands in Kancey's face, and somehow the wrong team got assessed the penalty when it was time to step off the yardage.
full_text: '' The NFL has admitted a rather embarrassing officiating mistake from Week 5: When Buccaneers defensive lineman Calijah Kancey was called for illegal hands to the face, it was actually a Cowboys player who put his hands in Kancey's face, and somehow the wrong team got assessed the penalty when it was time to step off the yardage. In the weekly officiating video , NFL officiating and rules analyst Walt Anderson said Cowboys guard Tyler Booker put his hands in Kancey's face but somehow that was miscommunicated as Kancey committing the penalty. Anderson said when the on-field officials make a mistake that blatant, the league officiating office should correct it immediately. "Were going to have a foul called on No. 94 on the defensive team for illegal hands to the face," Anderson said. "The only action relative to any hands is really by the offensive player here. So this is the type of play that the Competition Committee has instructed officiating that if objective information in terms of just asking the officials, 'Are we sure we have the right number of the player here?' that we can end up assisting with this. Because it's clearly not a foul by No. 94. If there is illegal use of hands, it's obviously by No. 52 of the offense." Kancey made clear in the moment that he knew it was a bad call, but there's nothing a player can do to fix a bad call against him. The New York officiating office could have fixed it, but didn't.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Injuries could increase Aaron Donald's playing time
summary: Aaron Donald may be privately thinking, "I'm too old for this shit."
full_text: Aaron Donald may be privately thinking, "I'm too old for this shit." Regardless, the rash of injuries along the Rams' defensive line could result in the 35-year-old defensive tackle, who returned last month from a two-year retirement, taking more reps than he has. “I'm going to just be out there playing," Donald told reporters on Friday. "However that rotation is going to be, it's going to be. We never have to set a snap — we just go as the game goes and have what that is. If it's 30 plays, 40 plays, 50 plays, 60 plays, that's what it's going to be.” This week, the Rams placed both nose tackle Poona Ford and defensive end Kobie Turner on injured reserve. Linebacker Myles Garrett has been on IR since the days following Week 1. Also on Thursday, defensive coordinator Chris Shula was asked whether the injuries would result in more reps for Donald. “That's hard to say," Shula said. "I think it definitely depends on the flow of the game and a lot of things like that. A lot of things go into it. We have a general snap count that he's always going to have going into the game. I don't think we would go crazily past that, but it's going to be hard if it's a tight game and he's at that number. Just like one of those pitchers in the ninth inning, you're probably going to leave him in for a few extra snaps.” In four games this season, Donald has played 33 snaps in Week 2 (56.9 percent), 35 snaps in Week 3 (52.2 percent), 43 snaps in Week 5 (67.2 percent), and 42 snaps in Week 6 (58.3 percent). Donald, whose interest in returning was sparked by the trade for Garrett, has yet to play in a game with the 2025 NFL Defensive Player of the Year. On Sunday against the 3-3 Raiders, the Rams may need Donald to turn back the clock to his pre-retirement form — and workload — in order to avoid falling to 2-5 through seven games.
author: Mike Florio

title: RB David Montgomery, DB Jalen Pitre among Texans out for Sunday
summary: The Texans will be short-handed on Sunday, without four key players.
full_text: The Texans will be short-handed on Sunday, without four key players. Running back David Montgomery (groin), safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder), offensive tackle Blake Fisher (thumb) and safety Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) will not play. The Texans list wide receiver Tank Dell (knee) as questionable, but he is expected to play. title: Ben Johnson on Cole Kmet: He's going to be sorely missed
summary: Bears coach Ben Johnson confirmed that tight end Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season on injured reserve after a right knee injury Thursday night.
full_text: '' Bears coach Ben Johnson confirmed that tight end Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season on injured reserve after a right knee injury Thursday night. The Bears made the move official Friday. In seven games, Kmet made 10 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown. Johnson said the Bears will miss Kmet, who has missed only one game in seven seasons. " He’s one of my favorites for a number of reasons," Johnson said, via Adam Jahns of CHGO_Sports. "I still remember him at the combine coming out and how much I loved him in that slight interaction we had there. To be able to be in the same room with him for the last year and a half, I've got so much respect for the player that he is, but also the person, the leader. He's everything we want to be about here. He's one of the glue guys. He's one of the guys that I can count on, whether it's a messaging standpoint or getting the pulse of the team. He's going to be sorely missed. Really, he's Chicago. He's been here his whole life, and he's a big part of our heartbeat. So, it stinks. It does. I hate it for him. I hate it for his teammates as well. And yet the train keeps rolling along. Someone else has to step up. Fortunately, we talked about this last week: Just our practice squad, the way we've been developing, the way they've been working, I think we've got some good options here on this roster. So, yeah, we're going to miss him."

title: A.J. Brown: I've got to put my best foot forward, try to make plays and keep going
summary: Patriots wide receiver A.J.
full_text: '' Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown expects more of himself, but he is trying to be patient and not frustrated. The Patriots played two games in four days in Brown's return from a right high ankle sprain, and he made only six catches on 16 targets for 75 yards. He dropped four passes, including three in Sunday's win over the Jets. “ I’m a vet . I understand how the game goes,” Brown said, via Eric Edholm of yahoo!sports. “It’s just how the game is. I know what type of player I am, and I know that that’s always the case, every time I line up I get a lot of attention. Teams try to take me away and it gives a lot of opportunities to other guys to make plays and soften that up for me. And then whenever I get my shots, I have to make them.” The Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder for Brown, who requested the trade from the Eagles. He was frustrated with the offense and quarterback Jalen Hurts in Philadelphia last season. Now, he's with Drake Maye and is trying to find his way back to being a No. 1 wide receiver. He was asked after Thursday night's loss to the Bears whether he needed an adjustment period with a new team. "I guess you could say that," Brown said. "But there's no time for that. . . . I just gotta try to put my best foot forward and try to make plays and keep going."

title: Lamar Jackson officially questionable for Ravens-Bengals
summary: Jackson told reporters on Friday he's heading in the right direction to play on Sunday.
full_text: After a week of limited practices, Baltimore quarterback Lamar Jackson is officially questionable for Sunday’s game against Cincinnati. The Ravens made the designation official with their final injury report of the week on Friday afternoon. Jackson has been sidelined for the last two games by a sprained ankle. Though it’s been reported that Jackson did not have a high-ankle sprain, he said after practice that is, in fact, what he’s been dealing with. “Ian Rapoport said that? [Is] he part of the training staff?" Jackson said, eliciting laughter, via transcript from the team. ”We can’t go off Ian Rapoport. He [is] just reporting. Somebody probably told him that too though, so [I] can’t blame him. “But my staff told me it was a high ankle sprain, so we [are] going with what [head certified athletic trainer] Adrian [Dixon] told me. I’m going with what Adrian told me.” Jackson also noted that he’s “heading in the right direction.” “I can’t call it right now,” Jackson said. “I still [have] got a grace period, so we’ll see, but hopefully. I feel like I”m heading in the right direction right now. “I don’t have a number, but I don’t feel like I have to be 100,” Jackson added. “If I can just be out there and tolerate the pain in my ankle, [then] that’s it. If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But [if] I’m restricted and I can't do what I do, [then] I’m not helping [anybody]. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that’s not helping my team at all. That’s just me. I feel like I’m being selfish, because it’s about me at that point, for me to go out there and be hurt.” Tyler Huntley would start if Jackson is not available. Elsewhere on the injury report, safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) and outside linebacker Tavius Robinson (pectoral) are out. Robinson’s pectoral injury will keep him out for the rest of the season. title: Revisiting the 2026 NFL Draft: Jonah Coleman is all Broncos have to show for their efforts
summary: Fourth-round running back Jonah Coleman is the only draft pick to see the field this year, as Denver gets virtually zero production from its first-year players through six games
full_text:
The Denver Broncos likely expected to get very little contributions from their rookie class after trading away significant draft capital, but even they may be surprised by just how little. Through six games, the sum of Denver's 2026 rookie class snap count is just 46, and the majority of those came on special teams.
Who did the Broncos draft, and how have they fared? CBS Sports revisits the 2026 NFL Draft .
Denver traded its first-round pick to Miami in exchange for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle . Waddle has 22 receptions for 228 yards and one touchdown through six games. With the selection acquired from the Broncos, the Dolphins moved up slightly and chose San Diego State cornerback Chris Johnson , who has played the lion's share of defensive snaps for the franchise.
Onyedim has not yet played for the Broncos. The defensive line had been a position of strength for the team so far this season, but generally, players taken in the top 100 overall are expected to at least be part of the rotation. However, few players taken after Onyedim in the third round could have helped Denver right now. Perhaps Cowboys linebacker Jaishawn Barham or Patriots tight end Eli Raridon , but the options were limited so far.
Coleman is the only draft pick who has played this season. He played 28 offensive snaps and nine special teams snaps over two games before succumbing to an injury. Prior to said injury, he offered glimpses of being able to handle the feature role: standing tall in pass protection, catching passes out of the backfield and showing patience in the run game. The Washington product could soon return from the injured reserve.
Casey has served as depth along the offensive line and was never expected to be an immediate starter. Joly was left on the cutting room floor as Denver trimmed its roster to the 53-man limit. Miami claimed him on waivers, but he has played just five special teams snaps.
Northern Arizona wide receiver Kolbe Katsis has been on the practice squad for the Broncos, but he was called into action and contributed on special teams against the Rams .
author: Josh Edwards

title: Cowboys' George Pickens brushes off Brian Schottenheimer's critique, says team needs to improve
summary: Schottenheimer challenged Pro Bowl WR George Pickens on his effort in the run game, Pickens talked about the team
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (2-4) are in a rut offensively .
After their last two primetime losses against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (24-16) and the Green Bay Packers (23-13) in Weeks 5 and 6, the Cowboys have now scored fewer than 20 points in consecutive Dak Prescott starts for the first time since 2019, Jason Garrett's last year as the team's head coach.
One of the issues plaguing current Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer's offense is Dallas' 31st-ranked rushing offense (76.0 rushing yards per game). The Cowboys have run the football on a league-low 32.5% of their plays, and on Thursday, Schottenheimer criticized Pro Bowl wide receiver George Pickens for his effort as run blocker and how hard he runs when Dallas is trying to run the ball. Dallas' head coach and offensive play-caller feels it is harder to succeed in selling the run to set up play-action passes, with Pickens showing what Schottenheimer perceives as effort that needs improvement on run plays.
After practice on Friday, Pickens chose to deflect from directly addressing his head coach's comments and to focus on what the entire Cowboys offense needs to do to fix their lagging run game. His 1,429 receiving yards in 2025 ranked third in the NFL , and his 428 this season sit outside of the top 10 at No. 12 in the league.
"I feel like, like I said, as a team, I feel like run, pass, a lot of stuff, you know what I mean? One week, it was you guys [the media] were saying defense [needs improvement]; one week you're saying this," Pickens said. "I feel like if you narrow the comments down, you're talking about the team. So most definitely, I feel like as a team, just keep improving."
Since the Cowboys acquired Pickens in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers in May of 2025, he and fellow Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb have become fast friends. Lamb hasn't seen any dip from Pickens despite comments made by people inside or outside the Cowboys' facility about Dallas' explosive wideout.
"I don't think about it [the criticism]. I hang around GP more than pretty much anyone in this building, and I'm always going to be on his side. To answer your question [Lamb shrugged, tilted his head and gave a wry grin]. We're cool man," Lamb said Friday. "He [Pickens] comes in ready to work every opportunity. It doesn't seem to bother him. It's not like we sit around and talk about the bad things people say. As far as his approach, coming to work and being the same guy every single day, he still does it."
Generating explosive plays in both the run and pass games could also help bring the run game back to life. The Cowboys' 34 explosive plays, which TruMedia defines as catches of 16 or more yards and runs of 12 or more yards, rank 22nd in the NFL entering Week 7. Last season, Dallas had 127 explosive plays, the seventh most in the NFL. Just over 73% of those explosives in 2025 were on pass plays (93), with Pickens accounting for over a third of those explosive catches with 34 in 2025, the fourth most in the NFL. Entering Week 7 this season, Pickens' 10 explosive receptions rank 17th in the league.
So what does Pickens need to do to get involved early in games? In his mind, he's already doing it.
"I'm doing what they're telling me to do," Pickens said. "So, [keep] doing what they tell me to do."
He also feels that having a more balanced offense could help create the explosives and the big plays to himself and others. The 25-year-old mentioned how, when playing college football video games, some teams will have their offenses listed as "Air Raid" or "Ground and Pound." Pickens' preferred offense would be one that is labeled "balanced." He also disputed the need to have the ball in his hands right away on game day to get in the flow of the action.
"I wouldn't really say that because ... [if] you can run the ball, [if] you can pass it, it's more about balance. It's not really about me or anyone else," Pickens said. "As a team, how would you run your offense or how you run your defense even if you're playing a video game?"
Execution, just making plays plain and simple, could also be a quick fix. The Cowboys have been blitzed more often as of late, and they haven't been able to set up quarterback Dak Prescott to succeed nearly as well on those plays when it comes to blocking and being on the same page when the pressure comes. In 2025, Prescott's passer rating when blitzed was 103.8. This year, it's down to 89.1.
"Execute properly. We leave explosives out there on the field just about every week. I hate to say that, but you look at it on film, and it's all over the tape," Lamb said. "Just being able to execute and being on the same page with sight adjustments. We feel like everybody else feels like if they blitz us, they're going to have a better chance of winning the game. I don't believe that, but they've [opponents] been having a lot of success at doing that. Being on the same page and executing properly."
Tempo (average time between snaps in seconds)
Having the explosives back in the Cowboys' offense could help Dallas rediscover the spark and offensive rhythm it had in Year 1 under Schottenheimer last season. Pickens getting the football is a big part of that.
"I think it would help my teammates tremendously. As far as me, Javonte [Williams], Turp [KaVontae Turpin], Flo [Ryan Flournoy], Cee [CeeDee Lamb], Ferg [Jake Ferguson], anybody we can get going early, I feel like we'll spark off of it. That's why I'm saying more balance, you know what I mean?"
Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams agreed, saying he can feel the edge and excitement when Pickens makes a big play and begins to trash talk the defense despite being all the way up in the coach's box on game day.
"I think the intention has certainly been there. It's been part of the discussion when you're putting together plays early," Adams said on Friday. "One of the things that we started seeing at the end of last season is that we're seeing a little bit, or a lot a bit, we're getting played differently than what we're seeing on tape. So there have been games this year where the first quarter has been like 'alright, that's not what we were planning on seeing, we need to get to X,Y,Z.' Sometimes a lot of coaching on game day gets you out of your planned openers, or there are times where he is drawing a double early, and putting him and CeeDee on the same side where you're going to get three coverage pieces, sometimes it's difficult to get him the ball in those scenarios."
"The best way to answer that is I have to do a better job of making sure he gets it [the ball] because he is a bright spot for us when he has the ball in his hands," Adams continued. "And for a lack of a better term, talking shit to the defense. I know that I get excited."
Prescott called Pickens' edge "infectious" and something that gives the Cowboys key momentum.
"We just have to get him the ball early, I definitely think that would help," Prescott said Friday. ... "He's a guy who is infectious to the team when he catches the ball. Whether it be a celebration or run after catch, it's good momentum we can build off of."
So how can Dallas scheme up early looks to Pickens? One option is putting him and Lamb on the same side of the formation, and then freeing Pickens up off a route that pulls him away from the gravity Lamb draws. Another way would be getting him the football early underneath on a screen, something Adams acknowledged as a legitimate option.
"If you know you're going to put those two guys [Lamb and Pickens] on the same side and get a certain coverage, that's a way to do it," Adams said. "Guys like CeeDee, we sometimes give him the sweep [run play], that's an easy way to do it. I think just kind of brainstorming through the easiest vision that you can get a guy is sometimes the best one. Sometimes if you think you can ensure they're not getting coverage over the top, those guys like when you throw the fade ball toward them."
Regardless, the Cowboys need to rediscover…

G Cesar Ruiz is officially questionable and was able to practice on a limited basis after not participating earlier in the week. If he is unable to play, rookie Jeremiah Wright could be put in his place. DT Nathan Shepherd has missed the last two games. Head coach Kellen Moore would not give details on Shepherd, who didn't practice Friday after practicing all week. RB Alvin Kamara , who was limited all week with a back injury, has no game designation.
San Francisco is looking to stay perfect this week, but once again has the weight of significant injuries hindering it. The offense will be without two top wide receivers, with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) both ruled out ahead of the matchup. This is the second straight missed game for Samuel. As expected DE Nick Bosa (knee, calf) is also out. DL Mykel Williams (knee), who was sidelined to start the year, did not have a game designation this week after being upgraded from a non-participant on Wednesday to a full participant on Friday.
The Falcons have a lengthy injury report this week, ruling out four players, including RB Brian Robinson (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo (forearm). With Deablo out, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels, who is questionable, could get the nod. CB A.J. Terrell (groin) and CB C.J. Henderson (groin) could make their return this week. Terrell spent the last four weeks on IR.
Only four Bengals players landed on the injury report this week. The three players who did not practice on Friday, DT Jonathan Allen , DT B.J. Hill and DT Dexter Lawrence , were all listed as "not injury related, rest."
QB Lamar Jackson, who has missed the last two games with an ankle injury, says he is trending in the right direction to make his return against the Bengals. He is officially questionable after being limited all week. DT Broderick Washington (ankle) is also questionable and was limited all week. CB T.J. Tampa (knee) was limited all week and is their one doubtful player.
The biggest takeaway from the Buccaneers injury report is the possibility of a return from starting QB Baker Mayfield, who has been dealing with a right thumb injury. He's missed the last three games, and in his place, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has led the offense. If he does come back, he will be without WR Emeka Egbuka, who currently leads the team in receiving yards (240). On the other side of the ball, S Antoine Winfield will miss his second straight game.
Panthers QB Bryce Young (knee) was listed on the injury report, but doesn't get a game designation and was a full participant all week. OT Monroe Freeling (knee) and LB Bam Martin-Scott were full participants all week, but get the questionable stamp.
Giants LB Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) is reportedly out for the year, but at minimum is sidelined for this week. CB Greg Newsome (concussion) joins him as the only other Giant ruled out ahead of the matchup. TE Theo Johnson is doubtful after not practicing on Friday. S Jevon Holland (concussion) and OT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) were limited the last two days after both not participating on Wednesday.
The Texans could get WR Tank Dell (knee), who hasn't played since 2024, back this week. He is questionable after being a full participant on Wednesday and Thursday. Among those already ruled out are S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) and RB David Montgomery (groin).
The Colts injury report was lengthy this week. CB Sauce Gardner (calf) is out after suffering the injury in last week's loss. He did not practice all week. Tyler Warren (groin), who leads the team in receptions among TEs, is also out. CB Justin Walley (knee) didn't practice Wednesday and was limited the rest of the week. LB CJ Allen (ankle) and LB Bryce Boettcher (groin) were both non-participants on Friday.
Minnesota's injury report is very short this week, with just one player carrying a game designation. RB Jordan Mason (thumb) was a full participant all week. WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited to start the week, but after two full practices, is cleared to play. WR Jordan Addison (hamstring) will make his return after missing one week and getting extra time to rest during last week's bye. TE T.J. Hockenson is another who took full advantage of the rest, passing the concussion protocol and ruled good to go for this week.
Miami has one player ruled out ahead of the divisional matchup, as they look to get their first win of the year. LB Willie Gay (illness) is questionable and was limited in practice on Friday. S Kyle Louis (knee) was a full participant on Friday after being limited the rest of the week.
Jets RB Breece Hall, who has missed multiple weeks with a quad injury, could return to the offense this week. He was limited in practice over the last two days, an improvement over Wednesday's practice, when he was sidelined. The RB is officially questionable. EDGE Joseph Ossai remains out, missing his third straught game.
The Browns have a lengthy injury report this week with three players out, including DT Khalil Davis (quad) and G Teven Jenkins (back). CB Denzel Ward (hand) popped up in the injury report as limited on Friday and officially questionable. S Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) was limited the last two days after not participating on Wednesday.
The Titans did not rule out any players ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, and five players are listed as questionable. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) went from limited Wednesday to not practicing the next two days. RB Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited on Friday. Safties Tony Adams (ankle) and Kevin Winston (quad) were both limited the first two days of the week and ended as full participants.
The Broncos will once again be without S Talanoa Hufanga, who suffered an ankle injury in Week 5. Denver has a few players who could return after missing multiple games. CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) is questionable and was limited in practice this week, after missing the last two games. RB Jonah Coleman could make his return from IR and was a full participant all week.
The Cardinals are dealing with numerous injuries this week. S Budda Baker played through injury in their Week 6 matchup but missed two days of practice before he was upgraded to limited on Friday. Another questionable player is CB Max Melton (knee), who did not practice the last two weeks. RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle), who leads the team in rushing, will be out this week.
Packers LB Zaire Franklin is out for only the second time in his nine-year career. Franklin suffered the injury during Thursday's practice. DT Jordon Riley (Achilles) is on the PUP list and could make his return this week, after being limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday.
