author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Lamar Jackson says he's 'heading in the right direction' for potential return vs. Bengals
summary: Baltimore's offense could be back at full strength soon as Jackson progresses toward a possible return against Cincinnati
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens could be on the verge of getting their starting quarterback back in the lineup. Lamar Jackson , who has missed the last two-and-a-half games due to an ankle injury, said on Friday that he is hopeful to play on Sunday against the division rival Cincinnati Bengals .
"Right now, I'm heading in the right direction," Jackson said . "I can't call it right now. I've still got a little grace period. So, we'll see man. Hopefully, but I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now."
Ravens coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson got a "pretty good amount of work in" during Friday's practice after he was limited on Wednesday and Thursday, but stated that the team is "still working through" whether or not Jackson will play on Sunday.
For his part, Jackson said the Ravens' medical staff told him he is dealing with a high ankle sprain, per The Athletic , which he seemingly sustained on the final play of the first half of the Ravens' victory over the Tennessee Titans back in Week 4. Jackson has been described as "day-to-day" since the injury, but this week was the first time he has participated in practice since going down.
He said on Friday that he doesn't have to be 100% healthy to play, but he doesn't want to be a "statue" on the field, via The Athletic . Jackson also relayed that the decision to play through multiple injuries that limited his mobility last season was "dumb, a little bit."
Jackson's rushing ability was severely limited last year, as he averaged a career-low 5.2 rushing attempts and 26.8 rushing yards per game. He had previously averaged at least 51.3 yards per game in every full season as a starter. He's averaging 36.0 yards per game so far this year, but he did leave one of those games at halftime.
If Jackson is again unable to start against Cincinnati, Tyler Huntley would once again take his place under center. Huntley has gone 1-1 in his two starts, and he's 51 of 72 for 429 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions so far. He's also run 15 times for 64 yards and a touchdown. The Ravens managed 30 points in their overtime victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, but slumped to just 10 points in their loss to the Cleveland Browns last week.
The offense has looked electric with Jackson under center in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's scheme, but we have rarely seen it at full strength so far this year. Not only has Jackson missed two-plus games, but Zay Flowers also missed a game-and-a-half and was limited to just 33% of the snaps in another. If they can get fully healthy, the Ravens could take off offensively. But that all depends on Jackson's ankle.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Giants RB Cam Skattebo says he 'got taught a lesson' after surprise benching
summary: After being effectively benched and watching New York release Najee Harris days later, Skattebo acknowledged his situation
full_text:
The New York Giants running back room has everyone's attention following an essential benching of their star player and cutting another after he criticized the run game.
Cam Skattebo leads the Giants in rushing yards with 294 yards on 81 carries, but in last week's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints , he wasn't given a single rushing attempt. It marked the first time in his two-year NFL career that he didn't touch the ball once in a game he played in. His limited snaps and lack of opportunities were a response to his costly fumble during overtime in the team's Week 5 27-27 tie against the Washington Commanders .
The running back room also saw the departure of Najee Harris, whom the Giants cut days after he started in place of Skattebo . Harris drew headlines for his criticism of the New York run game, expressing confusion over the game plan. Harris finished his short Giants tenure with 31 rushing attempts for 99 yards in five games.
"Nobody's safe, it's as simple as that," Skattebo said on Friday. "And I think when we go on the field, and we perform, if we're not performing, we understand there's a possibility of not being here. And if I don't perform, I know there's a possibility of me not being here."
Skattebo seemed to take what was essentially a soft benching well, saying he can learn from it.
"I got taught a lesson," he said . "I don't know if that's from them or from myself. I had to kind of step back and look at it and figure out why. Why I was doing the things I was doing, what was happening. Came to practice, worked on those things, corrected them. Ready to go back out there and play ball."
This was similar to his locker-room commentary after Sunday's game.
"I got punished for what I did [in last week's tie]," Skattebo said. "I understand it. I gotta be ready when coach calls my name and that wasn't today... I didn't expect to have zero [touches], but I was expecting to not play as much like I did."
The Giants are in Houston to face the Texans on Sunday.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Should Seahawks trade for Jonathan Taylor? Pros, cons for reigning champions to add Colts superstar
summary: The Colts could fetch a pretty penny for Taylor, but is it worth it for Seattle?
full_text:
Less than nine months ago, Kenneth Walker III powered the Seahawks to a Super Bowl LX victory with 161 yards from scrimmage, won Super Bowl MVP ... and then left Seattle, becoming the first Super Bowl MVP to change teams the ensuing offseason in over two decades.
Walker took Seattle's entire running game with him. While he leads the NFL in rushing yards and yards per carry in Kansas City, the Seattle running game is wallowing among the league's worst. With Zach Charbonnet missing the first six weeks of the season, Seattle has rotated through runners -- first-round rookie Jadarian Price leading the way at first before landing on IR with a chest injury, then Emanuel Wilson after Price's injury, with a sprinkling of George Holani as a change-of-pace/third-down/pass-catching option.
None have produced. Not only that, but all three have committed the cardinal sin: turning the ball over. Price lost fumbles in Week 2 and Week 3. Wilson and Holani both lost fumbles in Week 5, gifting the 49ers 14 points. Holani's, with Seattle simply trying to run out the first-half clock, was particularly awful, and Mike Macdonald could hardly believe his eyes.
#Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald’s reaction after Gracen Halton’s TD in the end-zone is CLASSIC! "Oh my God. What are we doing?" 💀 pic.twitter.com/qGZ5l9UqBS
The Seahawks rank last in rushing expected points added, largely due to an enormous number of fumbles. But even excluding fumbles, Seattle ranks 27th in rushing success rate, a measure of down-to-down efficiency. Seattle's 34 runs of 0 or negative yards are tied for eighth-most.
Charbonnet will help -- he has zero fumbles in his NFL career,  he is a good pass catcher and protector, and he has 21 touchdowns over the past two seasons -- but to lean on him heavily would be unwise. It's not just because of the injury, but also because he's never been a bell cow. He split backfield duties with Walker each of the last three years. His career high in touches per game is 12.8, set last year. Furthermore, Charbonnet simply doesn't provide the explosive element Walker did.
Someone who does provide an explosive element and bell cow capability is Colts running back Jonathan Taylor . He has topped 1,500 yards from scrimmage each of his last three healthy years, and last year he had 1,963, as well as 20 total touchdowns. With the Colts firing GM Chris Ballard earlier this week, Indianapolis could be looking to sell.
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said if Taylor is available, he'll 1) have many potential suitors and 2) have a high price. Rapoport also pointed out the Colts' interim GM, Ed Dodds, came up through Seattle (he was with the team from 2007-16) and has strong connections there.
Does the shoe fit for Taylor and the Seahawks? Does it even make sense to see if it does? Here are the reasons for and against Seattle making the move.
Taylor, 27, is still a stud. He's maybe not quite as studly this year -- many of his rate numbers are down -- but there might be reasons for that.
The Colts' offense is a mess. Like the Seahawks, they are turning the ball over a ton. Unlike the Seahawks, they have no answer outside the run game. Alec Pierce has appeared in two games due to an ankle injury that required surgery this offseason and then got re-aggravated. This was a thin receiver group before Pierce, but now it has no deep threat. Tyler Warren has also missed time.
All of this is to say things are stacked against Taylor. He is currently averaging 1.25 yards before contact per rush, which would be the lowest number of his career. Taylor's 2.79 yards per attempt are down from last year, but not a career-worst. His tackle avoidance rate is also down, but it's harder to make people miss when there aren't as many clear running lanes to the second level.
Taylor showed he can still be a major factor. He has had 120+ yards from scrimmage in three of six games this season. He has also scored multiple touchdowns in three of those six games. His numbers may be down -- 4.0 yards per carry -- but this is a certified bell cow. He'd take the pressure off the turnover-prone Sam Darnold and would be able to carry the offense by himself for stretches if needed. A relentless run game plus a relentless, dominant defense sounds like a pretty good combination.
If the Seahawks want to put their best foot forward in defending their title, they have to find answers in the run game. First-year offensive coordinator Brian Fleury was in San Francisco when the 49ers acquired Christian McCaffrey and elevated him into superstar status. He'd know how to elevate Taylor.
Plus, the Seahawks have crushed their in-season trades recently: Rashid Shaheed last year, Ernest Jones the year before, and Leonard Williams the year before that. Taylor could be the next game changer.
At 3-3, Seattle is far from out of it, especially in an NFC that doesn't look very deep beyond the loaded NFC North. Charbonnet's return will provide far more stability to a running game that needs it, and Macdonald anticipates a "sooner rather than later return" for Price after the Week 7 game against the Chiefs .
Seattle just invested a first-round pick in Price, too. He looked very good in the season opener against the Patriots and was solid against the Cardinals in Week 2, aside from the fumble. Another fumble in Week 3 against the Commanders plus an injury is a tough combination, but his return should provide a boost in the explosives department.
Taylor's dip in efficiency this year doesn't tell the whole story by itself, but it's not a good sign, either. He led the NFL in touches in 2025, his most since 2021. He has missed at least three games due to injury in three of the last four seasons. Yes, he's only 27, but the wear and tear on his body is considerable.
Through six games, Taylor doesn't have a single carry of 25+ yards; he had seven last year and eight the year before. He isn't producing big plays at the rate he was even a year ago. NFL Next Gen Stats has him averaging -0.16 yards over expected per rush, the first time ever he's been on the negative side of that metric. In fact, he's usually been one of the best. That downward trend is concerning, and he's signed with a significant salary cap hit through 2028.
He is still a very, very good player. But an elite one? Potentially not. And if he costs what an elite player costs -- not just with trade compensation, but actually payment into the future -- the Seahawks should pass. Just because they've had success in recent trades doesn't make Taylor the right one.
The Seahawks should not trade for Jonathan Taylor, and it's not just because Taylor might not be the player he once was, or because the Seahawks have two players at his position coming back.
The biggest reason to not make a trade is Seattle has bigger issues offensively. The line is a mess, ranking 23rd in PFF's pass-blocking grades, 23rd in ESPN's pass-block win rate, and 25th in ESPN's run-block win rate. Macdonald acknowledged the issues up front after a Week 6 loss to the Broncos , saying "the quarterback is getting hit way too much ... everybody sees that."
Taylor would help -- there's no doubt about that -- but what would help much more is Taylor's teammate Quenton Nelson . A stalwart guard for the last nine seasons in Indianapolis, Nelson is still playing at a very high level. Could he come in at left guard and move Grey Zabel to right guard to fortify the interior?
If it's not Nelson, it could be another guard or a center. Seattle needs more up front than it does in its backfield, and finding a cost-effective solution there will be much smarter than hoping one talented back can lift up an offensive ecosystem currently being dragged down by its blocking.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 7 picks and score predictions: Chiefs edge Seahawks, Bengals over Ravens
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks
full_text:
For anyone who has ever wondered what I do in the 24 hours before I turn my picks in, I've decided to give you a peek behind the curtain.
Last night, I spent nine hours trying to figure out who's actually good this year and I came to the conclusion that the 49ers and Chiefs might be the only good teams in the NFL. Everyone else is average. And to be honest, I almost scratched the 49ers off my list because they almost blew a 20-point lead to the Commanders on Monday night.
I was going to include the Vikings on my "good" list, but I don't trust their offense. I also thought about the Bills, but I don't trust their defense.
Outside of Buffalo, Minnesota, San Francisco and Kansas City, every other team in the NFL has at least two losses. As we all know, the NFL's ultimate goal is total parity and I think the league might have finally achieved it. Every week is unpredictable.
After spending nine hours making my list of good teams, I ate some Waffle Crisp. That took 45 minutes. I then spent four hours watching the Bears' new Hallmark movie, which is about 90 minutes long, so yes, that means I watched it 2.5 times.
Turn those TVs on because Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story is premiering RIGHT NOW on Hallmark Channel 🌟 pic.twitter.com/R8q4XtoxQ9
Since Hallmark started featuring NFL teams in their movies back in 2024, the team featured has averaged 13.5 wins per season in the year they get the Hallmark movie, so maybe I should also add the Bears to my good list. So there are now five good teams and everyone else is average.
Speaking of average, let's get to my picks.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
I don't usually pick the winner of a game based solely on the injury report, but I might have to do that here. I am fully expecting the Patriots injury report this week to look like a CVS receipt. If you've never seen a CVS receipt, they're roughly seven yards long and that's if you buy just one thing. If you buy more than one thing, your receipt will likely be as long as an entire football field. I'm pretty sure the only reason we're destroying the Amazon rainforest is so we can create more receipt paper for CVS.
Anyway, I was watching New England play the Jets on Sunday, and during the game, the Patriots lost 60% of their starting offensive line with LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), RG Ben Brown and RT Morgan Moses (ankle) all going down. As if that's not bad enough, Romeo Doubs also left the game with an injury. There have been so many injuries that I'm just going to bookmark the tweet below to keep track of who might not be playing this week.
The Patriots could be going into Thursday night against the Bears without their: FB WR2 WR3 LG RG RT RG2 RG3 CB2
The problem for the Patriots is that this is a Thursday game, so there won't be very much time for anyone to heal.
The other problem for New England is that the Bears' pass-rush has been surprisingly good this year, so this is not the game where you want 60% of your offensive line to either be hobbling around or not playing. The Bears have 17 sacks through six games, which is tied for the fifth most in the NFL, and now, they get to go up against a banged-up Patriots line.
Drake Maye has looked spectacular over the past three weeks, but he's been playing with a lead. During this current three-game winning streak, the Patriots have only trailed for about 10 total game minutes out of 180 and Maye does well when he's playing with a lead. What's going to happen if the Patriots have to play from behind? Well, just go watch film of the Patriots' 35-6 loss to Jacksonville in Week 3 and you'll get a rough idea.
I think the Bears will blitz Maye into oblivion and force him to make mistakes that we saw him make earlier in the season. He threw six interceptions through the first three weeks, but has only thrown one over the past three weeks. I think early-season Maye returns in this game.
Not only do we have a beat-up Patriots team hitting the road on a short week, but they have to face an NFC North team.
I'm not sure what the biggest mismatch is right now in the NFL, but I'm going to go ahead and say that it's the NFC North versus any team from the AFC East. Through six weeks, the NFC North has played five games against the AFC East and they've gone 4-1. Watching an AFC East team try to beat an NFC North team is like watching four baby fawns try to fend off a hungry bear.
I think what I'm trying to say here is that there's no way I'm picking against the Bears.
PICK: Bears (-3) 27-20 over Patriots
The Bengals might have just become the first NFL team ever to somehow lose on their bye week. They went into their off week tied for second place in the AFC North, and somehow, after not playing a game, they have dropped to last place. I blame the Browns. Things seem to get weird whenever the Browns are in first place and that's a world we live in right now.
This game is between two teams that I'm still trying to figure out. Are the Bengals good? Are they kind of good? Are the Ravens for real? Can either team beat anyone with a winning record?
The answers to these questions seem to be: Maybe, probably, still thinking about it and we'll find out this weekend.
These two teams both have a winning record, but they haven't really had to beat anyone to get there. The Bengals' three wins have come against three teams that have a combined record of 3-14 (.176). The Ravens' four wins have come against teams that have a combined record of 7-17 (.292). Every other AFC team with a winning record has beaten teams that have a combined winning percentage of at least .300, but not the Ravens and not the Bengals.
That being said, the Bengals are about two plays away from being 5-0, so they might be good. As for the Ravens, they had a chance to take control of the AFC North in Week 6, but they blew a 10-0 lead to the Browns. There is no team better at blowing fourth-quarter leads than the Ravens, which is definitely not something you want to be the best at in the NFL.
The Ravens have blown FIFTEEN fourth-quarter leads of at least 7 points since 2020. No other NFL team has even blown 10. At some point, you have to stop calling it bad luck. This is who they are.
The upside for the Ravens is that they might be getting Lamar Jackson (ankle) back this week, but it's impossible to say for sure, because no one seems to know when he's going to return.
Basically, Lamar might play, but he might not.
Jackson has historically played well against the Bengals, but if he also tends to play differently when he's coming off an injury. Just look at last year: After missing three games with a hamstring injury, he was never really the same after that. That doesn't mean he's going to struggle if he plays on Sunday, but it does mean that it's hard to predict how he might look.
Whether Jackson is on the field or not, this will be a huge test for the Bengals' revamped defense and I'm guessing the Ravens will be serving up a heavy load of Derrick Henry, especially if Jackson is on the field and can't quite run full speed.
If you watched the Bengals' defense play last year, then you know they couldn't stop anyone, especially Henry. Imagine someone taking a snowplow through the Smurf Village and you'll have an idea of what it looked like last year when Henry was running against Cincinnati's defense. The Bengals are definitely better this year, but I won't know how much better until I see them play against the Ravens, and that's because the Ravens have the one offense in the NFL that the Bengals can't figure out. In the last six meetings between these two teams, the Ravens have gone 5-1 while averaging 29.2 points per game.
In the battle of the two quarterbacks who have dealt with a lot of injuries over the past few years, I'm going to take the one who's actually healthy.
PICK: Bengals (+3) 27-24 over Ravens
The last time these two teams faced each other was on Thanksgiving 2025, which is almost fitting, because the Packers definitely have something to be…
author: John Breech

title: Prisco's Week 7 NFL picks: Lions edge Packers, Steelers top Saints in Paris
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 7 picks, including the Chiefs over the Seahawks in Kenneth Walker's revenge game
full_text:
What's a good Halloween costume to hide a face? I need it.
After last week's picks, I need to go into hiding. It was awful. When you can't get over .500 with the straight-up picks, you know it's a bad week.
I went 6-8 straight up and 3-11 against the spread. I could flip a coin and do better. Maybe my cats will make my picks next week.
My season records are now 54-38-1 straight up and 37-54-2 against the spread. That is vile.
Time to turn it around, so I am going to the dogs. Let them bark.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it.
Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26
The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close.
Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28
The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal.
Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16
The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset.
Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18
The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. The Jets have the better team and their defense should be able to limit the Miami offense. But the Dolphins play hard and will also play well on defense. It's close.
Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17
The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around.
Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23
The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset.
Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23
Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory.
Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23
The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close.
Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21
The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up.
Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33
This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around.
This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it.
Pick: Chiefs 23, Seahawks 17
The Eagles are a mess with all the injuries, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being out for the year. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close.
Pick: Cowboys 21, Eagles 20
This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game.
Pick: Patriots 28, Bears 27
author: Pete Prisco

title: Revisiting the 2026 NFL Draft: Can Akheem Mesidor be a building block for Chargers defense?
summary: An 0-6 start shifts the conversation in Los Angeles to the future and which first-year contributors can serve as foundational pieces
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 to start the season. They did not lose a sixth game last season until the regular season finale. Instead of making playoff plans, the conversation in Los Angeles centers on which leadership changes may be needed and which players are building blocks for the next iteration of Chargers football.
Edge rusher had been a position commonly associated with Los Angeles leading up to the draft. Aside from Tuli Tuipulotu , the Chargers have leaned on Khalil Mack and Bud Dupree recently; both of whom are 33 years or older. Miami's Akheem Mesidor was expected to be the present and the future of a defense trying to find its footing in a post-Jesse Minter world.
To this point, he has played 192 of a potential 367 defensive snaps. A trade involving Mack, who has played 71.4% of defensive snaps, would open the door for more playing time opposite Tuipulotu.
Through six games, Mesidor has 10 pressures and 2.5 sacks. Most of his pressures and production result from playing to the whistle rather than winning quickly at the line of scrimmage. The Ontario native has brought his go-to chop-and-swipe moves off the edge from college to the pros, but he lacks an overwhelming trait that would allow him to consistently win off the line of scrimmage.  However, he does a good job setting the edge in the run game and forcing the opposition to play between the tackles.
Chargers rookie edge rusher Akheem Mesidor has been credited with 10 pressures and 2.5 sacks this season. He creates a lot of opportunities for himself because he never stops working. pic.twitter.com/DrWEwbIxcF
If Tuipulotu can disrupt the pocket and move the quarterback off his spot, Mesidor could be a complementary starter who offers a solid floor in the run game and helps clean up the chaos. There is not much untapped potential, considering he is a 25-year-old who played six seasons of college football .
Could they have gone in another direction? There is a negligible difference between Mesidor and other edge rushers taken after him in the first round. They could have taken the undersized R Mason Thomas or Cashius Howell if they wanted more pass rush production. Dani Dennis Sutton (Packers) is another quality player who was taken later.
His presence allows the organization to focus on other positions of need, such as cornerback, offensive line and more. Los Angeles is realizing its defensive needs may have been masked by Minter's influence.
author: Josh Edwards

title: Bears fear season-ending injury for Cole Kmet after veteran tight end is carted off field
summary: Chicago's longest-tenured player suffered a likely season-ending knee injury against New England
full_text:
The Chicago Bears earned a 30-24 victory over the New England Patriots , but they also lost a notable player on offense, as tight end Cole Kmet was carted off the field in the fourth quarter after suffering a knee injury. He's believed to have suffered a serious, likely season-ending knee injury and will be placed on injured reserve, according to ESPN .
Kmet caught a Caleb Williams pass in the right flat before turning upfield and getting hit by Robert Spillane and Christian Gonzalez . When he went down, the veteran pass-catcher immediately grabbed at his right knee.
Kmet caught 10 passes for 87 yards and one touchdown this season. The former No. 43 overall pick out of Notre Dame is the longest-tenured Bear on the roster and one of the team's leaders. Williams told reporters he'll be there for Kmet every step of the way as he begins his recovery.
"It was tough. Obviously, I don't know exactly what it is, but getting carted off is never good. You're at least going to miss some time. I don't have the words to describe what Cole is to me, what Cole is to this team, to this organization. He's the longest-tenured Bear, I believe," Williams said. "He's been through it and it's challenging, it's tough, and I'll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. Cole's been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, through the second year, and now through this year. So I could only do the same for him."
Kmet's injury means more attention for Colston Loveland , who saw a season-high 12 targets vs. New England, catching seven of them for 69 yards and a touchdown. Loveland has now caught touchdowns in back-to-back games after failing to find the end zone through the first five games of the season.
The only other tight end currently on the active roster is rookie Sam Roush , who was selected in the third round this year out of Stanford. He's caught three passes for 33 yards so far this season, although he was projected as more of a "blocking tight end" as a prospect. Chicago has Qadir Ismail and Stephen Carlson on its practice squad as well.
Up next for the Bears are the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks in Seattle on "Monday Night Football" Nov. 2.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Baker Mayfield set to return for Buccaneers after three-game absence, will wear custom glove
summary: After a three-week absence, Mayfield is back under center for Tampa Bay
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are getting their starting quarterback back in the lineup. Bucs head coach Todd Bowles confirmed on Friday that Baker Mayfield is ready to go for the team's Week 7 game against the division rival Carolina Panthers . Bowles said Mayfield practiced in full, as if it were a normal week.
Mayfield has missed the last three games after dislocating his right (throwing) thumb back in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings . In his return to the field, he will wear a special glove with a restrictive plate on the back of his thumb so that it does not bend the wrong way, according to the Tampa Bay Times .
The Times reported that the glove was designed by Tampa Bay Rays clubhouse attendant Nick Bond. Bond ripped the thumb off a wide receiver's glove and inserted a support in its place.
"(It's) not restricting because it's on the backside," Mayfield said this week, per the Times. "For me, just getting used to it. I don't feel the difference. It's just like me wearing a glove."
Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has been filling in for Mayfield during his three-week absence, going 1-2 in his three starts while completing 60 of 95 passes for 501 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions. He rushed 19 times for 117 yards in those games. (He also went 0 of 3 with an interception and one rush for nine yards at the end of the game against Minnesota.)
Mayfield struggled during the first three games of the season, completing 63.5% of his passes at an average of 6.4 yards per attempt, with only two touchdowns and two interceptions.
He will likely not have his No. 1 wide receiver on the field this weekend, as Emeka Egbuka is listed as doubtful due to a concussion and foot injury. Mayfield will have to show considerable improvement from his early-season performance in order to get the Bucs back into the NFC South race, and that process will likely have to start without his top target on the field.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Aaron Rodgers sounds annoyed with Steelers' travel plans for Paris: Why the QB is unhappy
summary: The Steelers quarterback is set to become the first QB in NFL history to play international games in three straight seasons in three different countries
full_text:
For the first 17 years of his career, Aaron Rodgers didn't play in a single international game, but over the past three seasons, he's become one of the most traveled players in the NFL .
Rodgers and the Steelers are in France to face the Saints in what will be the NFL's first game in Paris. This week's matchup will mark the third straight year that Rodgers has played an international game, and since this one is in Paris, Rodgers will become the first QB in NFL history to play an international game in three straight seasons, with all three games being played in a different country.
In 2024, Rodgers and the Jets traveled to London to face the Vikings , a game they lost 23-17. In 2025, Rodgers and the Steelers traveled to Ireland to play in the NFL's first game in Dublin. In that game, they also faced the Vikings and the Steelers won, 24-21.
Rodgers' three international trips all have had one thing in common and that's the fact that each team decided to travel late in the week. The Steelers left on Thursday night and arrived on Friday in Paris and Rodgers seemed slightly annoyed by that travel plan when he was asked about it this week .
"I've played in three countries now," Rodgers said. "In each of them, we've left on Thursday early evening. It would have been nice one time to come over on a Monday."
The Saints decided to fly out on Monday night and land in Paris on Tuesday, and Rodgers sounds like he would have been on board with that plan.
"I think getting acclimated has its advantages," Rodgers said of adjusting to the six-hour time difference between Pittsburgh and Paris. "Obviously, there's 'science' behind coming in later in the week."
Rodgers used air quotes when he said the word "science," so it's pretty clear that he's not buying the fact that leaving later in the week gives you an advantage. Although the science is debatable, teams leaving later in the week for a game in Europe have had a lot of success this year, going 3-0.
NFL teams that have left on Thursday night and arrived on Friday for a game in Europe this year are 3-0. Texans, Colts and Jaguars (for their first London game) all went this route. #Steelers #Saints https://t.co/jtVBSpYjSv
There are riots in Paris right now, but that wasn't taken into consideration when the Steelers made their travel plans. Both teams locked down their Week 7 travel itinerary long before the season started and they stuck with those plans. The Saints could have delayed their arrival due to the civil unrest in Paris, but they decided not to make any changes. They showed up on Tuesday morning and they haven't had any issues.
The Steelers cancelled a fan event out of an abundance of caution this week, but otherwise, it's been business as usual for both teams.
The NFL started playing international games back in 2007, but Rodgers didn't get to play in one until 2022, which was his final season with the Packers . Rodgers played in zero international games from 2007 through 2021, but after this week, he'll have played in four international games over the past five seasons.
Rodgers was asked what he thinks the NFL will do next regarding the international schedule, and he gave an interesting answer.
"I think there could be 16 sites around the world at some point," Rodgers said. "Canada, Mexico, probably another South American country, multiple European countries. There was a game in Australia this year."
Rodgers is right, the NFL will likely play 16 international games at some point. That seems to be the league's endgame, and according to Rodgers, the NFL is only doing it for the money.
"The league has a pretty far reach and there's more coin to be made, they're going to look into it," Rodgers said.
With Rodgers set to retire, he won't have to worry about playing in any more international games, and if he wants to travel after his career is over, he'll be able to make his own plans instead of being stuck doing what his team wants.
author: John Breech

title: Saquon Barkley on Jalen Hurts situation: 'It sucks that people tried to make it an Eagles vs. Jalen thing'
summary: Philadelphia has faced heavy scrutiny after the quarterback was ruled out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, prompting the NFLPA to demand an investigation into his medical care
full_text:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season after doctors discovered blood clots first in his calf and then in his lungs. Hurts was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in the calf, but follow-up scans this past weekend revealed deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning several blood clots were now in his lungs.
Because the blood clot was "provoked" by Hurts being cleated in the leg during the Eagles' Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams and he then played in the team's Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London despite the initial clot reportedly being detected the night before, the Eagles have come under fire for their handling of the situation.
The NFL has already concluded that the process that led to Hurts being cleared to play in Week 5 "was handled appropriately," but the NFLPA subsequently released a statement calling for an investigation of the process nonetheless.
"The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."
The league said earlier this week that it would welcome an investigation, with Commissioner Roger Goodell stating that "I think our protocols were incredibly good there" and that the NFL has the "greatest medical advisors and people that are working on the health of our players," per NFL Network .
No matter whether there is an investigation or not, or what the results of said investigation are, Eagles running back Saquon Barkley does not like how outside observers have tried to pit Hurts and the Eagles against each other.
"It sucks that people tried to make it an Eagles vs. Jalen thing," Barkley said, via The Philadelphia Inquirer . "Jalen is a heck of a guy, heck of a leader, a guy who cares about this sport, cares about other people. Any time the game is taken away from somebody, it sucks, but especially in this situation, where we don't fully know the magnitude of it. Sometimes it's bigger than football. My prayers go out to him."
The Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, did release a joint statement about the situation when the quarterback was ruled out for the season, so it would seem that they are on the same page regarding the situation. Here is the full statement:
"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition.
"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. "blood thinners"). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.
"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.
"We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."
The situation is obviously incredibly serious, and the league and the NFLPA should probably conduct an investigation to ensure everything was handled appropriately and to determine whether any changes should be made to the protocols currently in place. Whether the Eagles and Hurts remain on the same page in the wake of such an investigation remains to be seen, but for now, it appears that they are.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Colts' Anthony Richardson facing charge for marijuana possession, per report
summary: Police cited the quarterback during an Oct. 12 traffic stop after officers discovered marijuana and THC gummies inside his vehicle
full_text:
Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. was hit with a misdemeanor charge for marijuana possession earlier this month, according to court records obtained by ESPN .
"We are aware of the situation involving Anthony Richardson and are currently gathering additional information," the Colts said in a statement. "We will have no further comment at this time."
Police pulled Richardson over on Oct. 12 after officers had questions about the car's registration. Police smelled marijuana in the car, and the quarterback admitted to smoking in the vehicle to avoid smoking marijuana at his house around his children. A search of the vehicle revealed a small amount of marijuana and THC-infused gummies that were confiscated by authorities.
The former No. 4 overall pick was not arrested and was allowed to leave. But he was issued a citation for an expired registration and a summons for the charge of marijuana possession.
Richardson, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, has not appeared in a game this season and was given permission to seek a trade in February. However, no trade partner appeared, and he returned to the fold to serve as Daniel Jones ' backup.
As a prospect, Richardson was recognized for his athletic ability. He actually became the most athletic quarterback to ever go through the NFL combine process up to that point, checking in with impressive measurements at 6-foot-4, 244 pounds, then running an official 4.43 40-yard dash, registering a 40.5-inch vertical leap, plus a 10-foot-9 broad jump. It led recently fired general manager Chris Ballard to use the Colts' top pick in the 2023 NFL Draft on the Florida product despite his lack of experience, as Richardson had made just 13 starts.
Richardson went 2-2 as a starter during his rookie season before a shoulder injury ended his year early. There was considerable excitement surrounding his entering 2024, as Richardson scored seven total touchdowns over his first three NFL games. However, an oblique injury sidelined him in Week 4, and then came the infamous incident in Week 8 against the Houston Texans , when Richardson took himself out of the game because he "needed a breather." Richardson was then benched for Joe Flacco , but returned to the starting lineup three weeks later.

title: NFL Week 7 bold predictions: Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring TD, Bijan Robinson shreds 49ers
summary: The Cardinals produce another improbable victory behind a barrage of field goals, and the Dolphins finally hold their first lead of the season
full_text:
Anything can happen in the National Football League and the kickoff to Week 7 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea.
In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research.
What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup?
The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object.
Flores' defense leads the NFL in:
The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release.
That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance.
The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game.
Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs.
San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries.
Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco.
The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals.
The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6.
How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research.
Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns.
The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league.
However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research.
The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long.
The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game.
They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets .
The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn.
Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Jaguars LT Anton Harrison done for season with torn ACL, per report: options for Jaguars at the trade deadline
summary: Walker Little will take over protecting Trevor Lawrence's blind side
full_text:
Trevor Lawrence's blind side protector, Anton Harrison , is done for the rest of the season due to a torn ACL. Harrison underwent arthroscopic surgery on Thursday, but during the surgery, doctors discovered he had torn his ACL as well, according to ESPN .
Harrison, 24, hurt his knee in Week 5 during Jacksonville's eventual win over the Eagles in London and was carted off. The Jaguars , who also played in London in Week 6, placed Harrison on IR but were hopeful he'd be able to return at some point this season. Then Thursday's surgery revealed the full scope of the injury.
The No. 27 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft , Harrison moved from right tackle to left tackle this offseason. It had been a bit of an up-and-down year for him in his new spot -- he allowed three sacks and 12 pressures in just five games -- but it's a significant loss for Jacksonville nonetheless.
Veteran swing Walker Little took over for Harrison in Week 5 and started in his stead in Week 6 against the Texans . The good news for Jacksonville is that Little has significant experience (40 career starts) and performed ably -- no sacks, two pressures allowed -- in Week 6 against a ferocious Houston front.
The bad news, outside the obvious bad news that comes with losing a left tackle, is this leaves Jacksonville paper-thin at tackle. Little was the only tackle on the roster outside Harrison and starting right tackle Cole Van Lanen . The Jaguars do have veteran offensive lineman Geron Christian Sr. on the practice squad but could look to make moves ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
A second-round pick out of Stanford in 2021, Little has spent his entire career with the Jaguars, and he started at least three games every year from 2021-25. Last year, he started 14 games, including 12 at left tackle. Overall, he allowed 2.9 pressures per game, the second-highest rate among offensive linemen, only behind Tennessee's Dan Moore Jr ., and nine sacks, tied for third-most. He also committed seven penalties. By the end of the season, the Jaguars had moved him to right guard and moved Van Lanen to left tackle.
But coach Liam Coen said last week, "I have a lot of confidence" in Little.
"I probably can't overstate how important it is because we really are fortunate to not have to play a backup in a situation when a tackle goes down," Coen said a day later. "I don't look at Walker as a backup tackle or a backup guard."
This -- plus calling up someone from the practice squad -- seems to be the clear solution for now, but if Little struggles, the Jaguars could pursue other options.
Van Lanen impressed moving over to left tackle late last season, so much so that he got a three-year, $51 million extension. Should Coen and his staff deem it worth doing again, they already have proof of concept.
The issue, though, is that it would create a hole at right tackle, where Van Lanen has worked the past several months. Little stepped in for some snaps at right tackle in two games this season, but both times were at the end of blowouts. He has never played meaningful right tackle snaps in his NFL career, though the Jaguars clearly trusted him to do so, considering he was their swing tackle prior to Harrison's injury.
Unfortunately for Jacksonville, it's not like capable left tackles are a dime a dozen. However, there are some options potentially available before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
The Commanders and the Eagles are two potential sellers in the lowly NFC East. The Eagles have already traded away Cam Jurgens amid a nightmarish season for the entire organization. Last year, the Jaguars traded Fred Johnson to Philadelphia for a 2026 seventh-round pick. Might they be interested in a reunion?
Andrew Wylie is another name that could be of interest. He has not played meaningful snaps at left tackle, but he has played a ton at right tackle, right guard and left guard. If anything, he could be the Jaguars' swing tackle, the role Little had before Harrison's injury. Wylie has played sparingly this season, though it was at left tackle.
Both Washington and Philadelphia are still in the division race (somehow), but if either decides to sell and Jacksonville decides to buy, both options could make sense. GM James Gladstone made a deal for Jakobi Meyers last year at the deadline and a blockbuster for Travis Hunter during last year's draft. If there's anyone who will go hard after making his team better, it's him.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Cowboys vs. Eagles rivalry game headlines three matchups with underrated big stakes
summary: The unpredictable NFC East supplies two of this week's most intriguing under-the-radar matchups
full_text:
There are always underrated NFL games that need to be on your radar, and we select three every week to highlight the storylines you may have missed while selecting your fantasy lineups or projecting the playoffs. This week, the underrated games are heavy on the NFC East, a division that's hard to predict this year and not necessarily for good reasons. This week's games have the potential to be season-defining, momentum-shifting, and playoff-implicating.
It can be argued that the New York Giants are worse than their record (3-1-1) suggests, and the Houston Texans (2-4) are better than theirs.
The Giants quarterback situation has been anything but stable. Starter Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury, leaving Jameis Winston to lead the offense. Winston, who is anything but consistent, was replaced by their newest acquisition J.J. McCarthy . The former Minnesota Viking immediately threw a pick, but did find the end zone.
It's hard to pinpoint where this team is going this season, and what makes it all the more confusing and unpredictable is the struggles of the rest of the NFC East. The Giants are in the lead among the Philadelphia Eagles (2-4), Washington Commanders (1-4-1) and Dallas Cowboys (2-4). Anything could happen with these four teams.
The Texans are a team on the rise, winning their last two, with a win last week against a top AFC team and division rival, the Jacksonville Jaguars . They started the season 0-4 and while a loss is a loss, these losses were close, which counts for something, right?
They came close to defeating the Buffalo Bills in Week 1, losing 26-31, lost 19-17 to the Indianapolis Colts in Week 3 and lost 34-30 to the Cowboys in Week 4. Granted, those aren't all Super Bowl contenders, but the ball bounces the other way in some of those games and the Texans would be in the "top team" conversation. Houston has never started 0-4 and ended with a winning record, but I think this could be the year.
The Los Angeles Rams and Las Vegas Raiders are each interesting studies this season, so I am intrigued at a matchup between the two.
The Raiders are looking to bounce back after losing to three strong AFC teams in the Kansas City Chiefs , New England Patriots and Buffalo Bills. The losing streak comes after a strong 3-0 start, during which they seemed poised to be this year's surprise success. They are now 3-3 and a win this week could begin to turn things back to where they started.
Unlike the Raiders, who had low expectations heading into the season, the Rams were widely considered Super Bowl favorites.
L.A.'s downfall has been one of the big surprises of the season. The once hyped NFC team now sits at 2-4, last in the NFC West. With the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers in their division, winning it seems like a huge reach. The Rams have the third-worst odds of winning the division at +1200, per DraftKings Sportsbook.
Their playoff hopes have fallen from 90.1% to 26.0% since the start of the season, according to our friends at SportsLine.
It's getting awfully close for Sean McVay's squad to panic, and it's possible for them to gain a little bit of hope against a team that is trending downward with three losses.
Both these teams need a win badly, and games between teams that need a victory are always interesting.
These divisional rivals have a lot of history, which means things could get chippy on Monday Night Football. These teams have faced off 134 times, with the Cowboys having the 75-59 edge.
If Eagles coach Nick Sirianni doesn't start winning, it could cost him his job, and players may want out if they continue to play mistake-filled, uninspired football. This is another case where I think desperation will make the game plan interesting. What they've done isn't working, and I'm interested to see what they can do to change the trajectory.
Philly has the added struggle of numerous significant injuries this season, most notably to quarterback Jalen Hurts , who is likely out for the season due to blood clots .
The Cowboys are right there with the Eagles at 2-4 as well, and while they have a strong passing game, their run game is third-worst in the league. Philadelphia's run defense is stronger than its pass defense, and it will face a challenge to even things out.
Divisional games are always there to surprise us and give us great football, and with jobs and seasons on the line, I think this one will be more interesting than people expect.

The Seahawks have three losses this season. All three have come by three points or fewer, and the Seahawks have committed three turnovers in each loss. title: Should the Chiefs trade for Garrett Wilson? Why blockbuster deal makes sense, and why it probably won't happen
summary: Pairing the dynamic Jets wideout with Patrick Mahomes could solve Kansas City's receiver concerns, but several obstacles stand in the way
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than two weeks away, and several stars could be moved prior to that Nov. 10 date. Sometimes the trade deadline is more "bark than bite," but we've already seen a team punt on their former No. 4 overall pick wide receiver in Marvin Harrison Jr . Could we be in for some fireworks?
Among the hypothetical buyers at the trade deadline are the Kansas City Chiefs . They are right back to being a contender following that 6-11 season in 2025. In fact, they are the first team since the 2019 San Francisco 49ers to start 5-0 following an 11-loss season. It's in large part due to the play of new running back Kenneth Walker III , who has rushed for more yards (665) than any other player in their first five games with a team in NFL history.
Imagine adding another playmaker to this Chiefs offense. CBS Sports' Russell Wilson has one in mind, and that's New York Jets wideout Garrett Wilson .
"If I'm the Kansas City Chiefs, I got the all-star running back in the backfield, Ken Walker, which we've never had before," Wilson said on "Set Hut." "All these years we've never had a running back like this. And guess what that does? Play action opens up. What Mahomes does better than arguably anybody in the world is throw the ball down the field. So if I'm thinking about this, who would I go get, I'm going to go get Garrett Wilson.
"If the Jets keep losing, I'm going to go get Garrett Wilson from the 'New York football Jets,' because I believe that Garrett Wilson down the field -- with his ability, he's a smart guy he learns quickly, he'd be great in an Andy Reid style of offense. Patrick Mahomes and him, how he gets in and out of his breaks, they haven't had a receiver like him. "
Garrett Wilson to Chiefs? @DangeRussWilson thinks the Chiefs should trade for Garrett Wilson pic.twitter.com/PRHRrVVLpq
So, should the Chiefs swing a massive trade for a WR1 like Wilson? Let's take a look.
The benefits of adding Wilson are easy to identify. He enters Week 7 ranked 14th in receiving yards (418) despite having average quarterback play. Well, at least not Mahomes-level quarterback play. In fact, Geno Smith is one of the best quarterbacks Wilson has ever had. Wilson had to begin his NFL career with Zach Wilson and Mike White . Yet, he found a way to cross 1,000 yards receiving in each of his first three seasons!
Wilson actually became the fifth player in NFL history to record 80 receptions and 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first three seasons, joining Ja'Marr Chase , Justin Jefferson , Michael Thomas and Odell Beckham Jr . And again, did it mostly with Zach Wilson. The Jets' quarterback situation last year with Justin Fields , Tyrod Taylor and Brady Cook was so bad, that Wilson ended up leading the Jets in receiving with 395 yards -- in SEVEN games played. It was the fewest receiving yards by a team leader since 1976, according to CBS Sports Research, excluding the 1982 strike season. Wilson has already surpassed that total in six games this year.
So, this playmaker can be productive no matter how bad his situation is. Imagine giving Wilson a three-time Super Bowl MVP and two-time NFL MVP at quarterback in an Andy Reid offense.
That brings me to my next point, which Russell Wilson brought up about play action. When the Chiefs signed Walker, the first thing I thought about was how he would open up the passing game. Granted, I didn't know he was going to come in and be Barry Sanders, but I did think he was going to be the best running back Kansas City has had in quite some time, which was really going to open up things for everyone else.
The Chiefs passing offense currently ranks in the top 10 with 254.2 yards per game, but I'm not sure it's really felt like that. No offense to a legend, but 37-year-old Travis Kelce probably shouldn't be leading your team in receiving through five games. His 299 yards receiving rank 35th in the NFL. Behind him is Tyquan Thornton with 219 yards, who is expected to miss extensive time after suffering a serious ankle injury earlier this month, then Xavier Worthy is third with 206 yards receiving. Those 206 yards are tied for 76th in the NFL. Rashee Rice has caught 13 passes for 190 yards and one touchdown through four games in what has statistically been his worst season thus far, and he's dealing with a hamstring injury.
The Chiefs have a legitimate need at wide receiver, and a legitimate need for a WR1 as well. If Kansas City added a talent like Wilson, the Chiefs would definitely be looked at as the favorites in the AFC -- and for good reason.
Are you willing to trade at least a first-round pick for Wilson? That's probably what it would cost. Another hurdle to trading for Wilson is his contract and the Chiefs' cap situation.
Some believe the salary cap is a myth, and in certain circumstances, it can feel like that. But Wilson just signed a four-year, $130 million extension that includes $90 million guaranteed 15 months ago. He's technically under contract for five more seasons, including 2026. Currently, the Chiefs have just $2.2 million in available funds, per Over The Cap , which ranks No. 29 in the NFL. Sure, you can move money around, but the Chiefs are also projected to be nearly $12 million over the cap in 2027. His cap hit goes up to $23.3 million in 2027, and then north of $35 million in 2028-2030.
While we are talking about finances, the Jets would take on a dead cap hit of $31.2 million to trade Wilson, while also losing $21.2 million in "savings." So, the Chiefs would have to REALLY sweeten the offer for the Jets to make this kind of move. I'm not really sure it makes sense.
Do the Chiefs really need to give up premium draft capital and take on a massive contract with their financial situation while already boasting what is statistically the best offense in the NFL?
Ultimately, I don't think the Jets are going to trade Wilson. They had their fire sale last year with Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams , while Wilson got paid. The dead cap hit/loss in savings don't make sense for New York, which would make a potential deal even tougher for the Chiefs.
Maybe if the Jets fall to 2-7, they could reconsider their situation?
vs. Las Vegas Raiders (3-3)
at Kansas City Chiefs (5-0)
Wilson in Kansas City would be a dream fit, but the Chiefs could use a cheaper option. Maybe that Tyreek Hill reunion is in the cards, although the NFL's investigation complicates that . The names are less sexy, but perhaps Brian Thomas Jr. , Jauan Jennings or Jerry Jeudy could be potential trade targets for the Chiefs if they want to go that route.

title: Week 7 best bets: Browns keep stacking wins, two big-name running back under props to target
summary: Cleveland should move to 5-2 with a win in Tennessee
full_text:
Well, after two straight winning weeks, we came back down to Earth in Week 6. In two tight end props I liked, Tucker Kraft fell just short of hitting 40+ receiving yards, and Juwan Johnson laid a complete goose egg. The Patriots were up 10 late, but a Jets field goal meant New England didn't cover -7.5. While D'Andre Swift found the end zone to complete one leg of the parlay, Drake London didn't score. He now has the most receptions without a touchdown across the entire NFL .
We did hit on the Texans ' money line over the Jaguars , so at least it wasn't a completely lost weekend, but it was a bad one for sure.
Somehow, the 4-2 Browns are only 1.5-point favorites at the 1-5 Titans . And how did the Titans get that win, you ask? Last week, the Colts completely melted down in every facet, including giving up a blocked punt for a touchdown and a 58-yard punt return. Indianapolis was cruising before that. The loss led to GM Chris Ballard being fired.
I just don't see the Browns doing the same. Deshaun Watson has come back down to Earth after a hot start, but this is a really good defensive team facing one of the league's worst offenses. I'll confidently take Cleveland to get to 5-2 and continue what has been the most pleasantly surprising start in football.
Daniel Jones has six interceptions in six games this year. Now he faces a ferocious Brian Flores defense that leads the NFL in pressure rate. Jones has a tendency to make poor decisions under pressure, and the Vikings have six interceptions this season, tied for the fifth-most in the league through six weeks, even though they've already had their bye.
Here are Ashton Jeanty's rushing numbers from the last two games:
That doesn't inspire a ton of confidence, even against a banged-up Rams defensive line. He also doesn't appear to inspire much confidence among his coaching staff. Jeanty's snap share has steadily declined this season. He was up around 80% Weeks 1-3, then down to 67% in Week 4, and then down again to the mid-50s last week. Mike Washington (43 yards) nearly doubled Jeanty's yardage total on one fewer carry last week, and he recorded a season-high 35% snap share. Even Dylan Laube has entered the fray in the past two weeks. Klint Kubiak notably split his backfield in Seattle last season, and it looks like it's trending that way in Las Vegas.
Josh Jacobs is back after being removed from the commissioner's exempt list. While he is expected to suit up and play this week, I don't expect a huge workload or a ton of success for him. Remember, while Jacobs was on the exempt list (which he had been since the start of the regular season), he couldn't practice with the team, either. Should we really expect him to get a ton of touches?
Furthermore, the Packers have been completely unable to run the ball. Yes, Jacobs should help that slightly, but the Packers are 28th in yards before contact per rush. Jacobs could help the yards after contact per rush (the Packers rank 32nd there), but in his first game back, I'm fading him putting up substantial numbers. This is a team that ran for just 57 yards on 26 carries against the Cowboys ' woeful defense last week.
I could see Jacobs making an impact Sunday and maybe even scoring a touchdown, something he's still really good at. But big rushing numbers? I doubt it.
I just cannot envision the Rams losing again. I know about all the Matthew Stafford problems. I know about all the injury issues. I just can't see it happening. They'll find a way.
Corum, meanwhile, has had back-to-back games with a touchdown and at least 50 yards from scrimmage. He provides more explosiveness than Kyren Williams does, and with the Rams lacking explosives through the air (and Davante Adams being out), Sean McVay could turn to more Corum.
With no Adams, the Rams will be in more 13 (one running back, three tight ends) personnel. In 13 personnel, Los Angeles has the third-highest yards per carry rate in the league, and when facing 13 personnel, the Raiders ' defense allows 5.3 yards per carry, the worst in the NFL. Furthermore, with no Adams, the running backs should be even more involved in the passing game. Corum should have a solid day in a must-win game.
Season record: 59-34 Last week: 10-4

title: Jared Goff vs. Packers' stifling secondary: How this crucial NFC North showdown will be won
summary: How aggressive Goff decides to be against Green Bay's defensive backs with tight window throws will be critical
full_text:
Thus far, there is only one division in the NFL with all four teams making the playoffs if the season ended today: the NFC North.
The Minnesota Vikings lead the way with a 5-0 record, which would make them the No. 2 overall seed in the NFC bracket at the moment. Then, the rest of the division makes up the three wild card teams, seeds five through seven in the following order: the Green Bay Packers (4-2), the Chicago Bears (4-2) and the Detroit Lions (3-2). Every inter-division game between those four squads holds high-stakes ramifications on the conference's playoff picture, with both division and conference tiebreakers up for grabs.
That makes the Packers' Week 7 trip to Ford Field to face the Lions one of the league's most important matchups of the week. So, where could this showdown between two high-flying offenses, led by Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love and Detroit quarterback Jared Goff, be decided? Let's take a closer look.
Wide receiver Christian Watson and wide receiver Matthew Golden are the first duo in Packers history with 500-plus receiving yards each in the first six games of a season. Along with Love, they wouldn't seem to have too much of an issue with the Lions' leaky defense, which is allowing the third-most points per game (29.6) this season. Detroit is also allowing the highest rate of opponent touchdowns per drive (37%), and its defensive passing expected points added (EPA) per game (-19.0) is the second worst by any team through the first five games of a season, ahead of only the 2005 San Francisco 49ers , who went 4-12.
That's why the matchup between Goff, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown , wide receiver Jameson Williams and tight Sam LaPorta against the Packers defense will likely decide Sunday afternoon's game. It's a battle that could tilt either way.
Goff is off to a historically great start to the season as just the second quarterback in NFL history with 1,400-plus passing yards (1,485) and no turnovers through the first five games of a season, along with Drew Brees in 2018. However, Goff will be challenged by a Packers defense that is allowing the sixth-fewest passing yards per game (193.3) in the entire league and is playing its best ball right now.
Green Bay's offense, hitting its stride with a patched-up offensive line, has allowed its defense to play with more energy since it doesn't have to be on the field as often, and it's paying off. The Packers lead the NFL in scoring defense (11.3) and takeaways (9) during the team's three-game winning streak since Week 4.
Where they will really pose a challenge to Goff is on tight-window throws (less than one yard of target separations). Per the NFL's Next Gen Stats, Goff is throwing into a tight window on just under a fifth of his throws, 19.4%, which is the fifth-highest rate in the league this season and his highest since his rookie year with the Rams in 2016, when he threw when an NFL-high 25.9% of his throws were into tight windows. What's interesting about Goff's willingness to squeeze the football into tight windows this season hasn't really changed when the Lions are tied or leading (19.6%) or trailing (19.2%).
Goff has completed 13 of his 37 tight-window throws for 115 yards and two touchdowns, with St. Brown making up the bulk of that production. The duo has connected on five of 16 tight-window throws for 34 yards and both of Goff's tight-window throw touchdown passes this season. Green Bay's defense is tied for the most tight-window interceptions so far, with three, so it would be more than happy for Goff to try them when a tight window opportunity arises.
There's also a chance Goff may be attempting a higher volume of tight window throws on Sunday because Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs has historically struggled against the Packers, more so than any of his other NFC North opponents. In six games against Green Bay, Gibbs is averaging 48.2 rushing yards per game with a 3.9 yards per carry average and just one touchdown. Compare that to his 12 games against the rest of the division, and his numbers look a lot different: He has a 75.3 rushing yards per game average with a 5.2 yards per carry average and 12 rushing touchdowns in NFC North division games not against the Packers.
Whoever wins the battle on Goff's tight-window throws between St. Brown and the rest of the Lions' pass catchers and the Packers' secondary will likely decide the outcome of this crucial Week 7 showdown in the NFC North.
