title: How the Cardinals can defeat the Broncos
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are not dead after all. In fact, they are showing good signs of life. But now, they have an upcoming game against AFC power Denver Broncos. After that, the schedule is just as difficult with the Dallas Cowboys, Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs. With a one-game […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Josh Wallace #30 and Poona Ford #97 of the Los Angeles Rams tackle Michael Wilson #14 of the Arizona Cardinals in the fourth quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are not dead after all. In fact, they are showing good signs of life. But now, they have an upcoming game against AFC power Denver Broncos. After that, the schedule is just as difficult with the Dallas Cowboys, Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs. With a one-game win streak, Arizona has the opportunity to salvage what looked like another dismal season. RELATED: OPENING LINE FOR WEEK 7 Next up, the Broncos in a home game. Last year, Denver was the #1 seed in the AFC with a 14-3-0 record and at one time had an 11-game win streak. After missing the Wild Card round, in the divisional game they defeated the Buffalo Bills 33-30 in overtime, and then lost a heartbreaker 10-7 to the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship Game. So, they are a very good team. After six games this year, they sit at 4-2-0 and are in second place in the AFC West Division. How can the Cardinals beat this exceptional AFC powerhouse? Broncos are not a good road team Oftentimes, the home crowd is the twelfth man. The Cardinals wish their home field were a safe haven, but unfortunately this year they are 0-2. The Broncos are 3-0 at home but 1-2 while traveling to games. Denver has struggled mightily on the road. They were beaten badly by the undefeated Chiefs 31-10 in Kansas City, and 24-14 by another undefeated team, the San Francisco 49ers. At one time against San Fran, they had built a 17-6 lead while Denver had punted five times. Their offense was stymied repeatedly without any run game. QB Bo Nix only had the short passing game to stand on, while the intermediate passing zones were minimal. In the end, the Broncos only had 82 rushing yards. In Week 1 against the Chiefs, the first half was fairly close, but the game quickly got out of hand after halftime. Going into the final quarter, it was 24-10. Again, Denver could not run the ball whatsoever, and at the final gun, they had 61 rushing yards. Use the offense’s playmakers early and often The Broncos have a good defense. It was their catalyst from last season, and it has carried over into this year’s roster. Make no mistake, this is a very good team. They just defeated the Seattle Seahawks, who many believe is the best team in the NFC. Cardinals TE Trey McBride leads the league in receptions with 49. He has a knack for getting open, and so far, no linebacker has been able to cover him. Not sure if switching to a safety would help matters, but in a six-game sample, opposing defenses haven’t had an answer for him. The Broncos are ranked #5 in passing defense this year, so this is a tough situation for Arizona’s passing game. WR Michael Wilson is ranked #11 in the league in receiving. That means that the Cardinals have two top talents that should be thrown to repeatedly. Use this talent as much as possible. But the Cardinals have two aces in the hole: WRs Kendrick Bourne and Jalen Brooks. Bourne is the guy who can take the short-to-intermediate throws and advance a drive. Brooks can become a game-decider. In the Rams contest, he only had two catches, and the last one decided the outcome of the game. Use your weapons. Make QB Bo Nix very uncomfortable The Broncos signalcaller, Bo Nix, does really well when he has time to survey the field. He is a gifted quarterback who has a great arm and is very accurate. However, that is within the confines of a clean pocket. When Nix is forced to scramble or run, his ability to hurt a defense is greatly diminished. When he is flushed and expected to look downfield, he has lost a lot of his ability to move the sticks. But this article discusses how Nix has regressed this year. The key to disrupting Denver’s offense is to collapse the pocket and be on Nix’s tail every time he drops back to pass. Now, having said that, maybe Arizona’s defense can’t come through. Perhaps this shouldn’t even be listed as a method to defeat the Broncos. But it is a fact. But Denver’s passing attack is currently ranked #31 in the league. Their inability to pass the ball is their Achilles heel. The Cardinals’ pass defense is ranked #22, which is in the bottom third. Nix is ranked #21 in total passing yards (1,049), but is #73 in average yards per completion (5.6). He has thrown only six touchdowns all year, with three interceptions. Their offensive line is very good at run blocking, but has allowed the fourth-most sacks. That is a huge stat to know going into this weekend. Last week, the Seahawks contained Nix, and he had only 107 passing yards. Denver’s passing game is almost devoid of any explosiveness, as Nix relies on short completions as well as dink-and-dunk gains. Provide plenty of pressure on Nix. Now, can DT Walter Nolen step up? What about DE Josh Sweat? Can DE Darius Robinson show up two games in a row?

title: NFL predictions: Can Falcons take advantage of 49ers injuries?
summary: The Atlanta Falcons are sitting at 2-4 after a disappointing two-week stretch. Atlanta desperately needed to find a win over the past few weeks, instead dropping a game to the Tyler Huntley-led Ravens and (understandably) to the finally healthy Bears. The Falcons didn’t play terribly in either game, but in both, it was too little […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Mac Jones #10 of the San Francisco 49ers is rushed by Zach Harrison #96 of the Atlanta Falcons during the third quarter in the game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons are sitting at 2-4 after a disappointing two-week stretch. Atlanta desperately needed to find a win over the past few weeks, instead dropping a game to the Tyler Huntley-led Ravens and (understandably) to the finally healthy Bears. The Falcons didn’t play terribly in either game, but in both, it was too little too late from Atlanta’s offense. TNow the team enters the unenviable situation of needing a win against an undefeated 49ers team that has pretty consistently looked like one of the NFL’s best units despite a growing injury list. That lengthy injury list, along with some rest and off-field advantages, could help the Falcons pull off the unlikely upset in Week 7. The bettors seem to think so as well, as Atlanta is just a 2.5-point home underdog according to FanDuel. Falcons vs 49ers predictions On paper, the 49ers are clearly the superior team. San Francisco is one of only a handful of teams who are top-10 in both offense and defense, and one of only two who are top-5 in both categories. To put it simply, there aren’t any obvious glaring weaknesses on this team—except their long injury list, which is only growing heading into Week 7. That’s something the Falcons will have to take advantage of to come away with an improbable victory. The 49ers offense struggled mightily once Mike Evans, who Falcons fans know quite well, left the game against the Commanders in Week 6. Washington was close to mounting a comeback, but was ultimately unsuccessful due to their own issues. Evans, along with Deebo Samuel, have both been declared out for Week 7. Those are major losses, and when combined with San Francisco’s other injuries at the position, could be too much for the passing game to overcome. Atlanta is dealing with their own injury problems, particularly on defense. Starting slot corner Billy Bowman and linebacker Divine Deablo are both out, and three other cornerbacks are questionable. It does sound like A.J. Terrell and C.J. Henderson are likely to play on Sunday, but a new injury (and questionable designation) for rookie Avieon Terrell throw a wrench into things. Veteran Mike Hughes, who has struggled mightily this season, will be on track to start again unless those players are cleared. Already down Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr., Atlanta is looking at questionable designations for Za’Darius Smith and Samson Ebukam on the edge. Standout interior pass rusher Gervon Dexter Sr. also picked up a questionable tag heading into the weekend. Atlanta is perilously thin on the edge and can’t afford any more losses here. If Atlanta can get most of these players in the game on Sunday, they may have a significant health advantage over San Francisco. History is also unkind to West Coast teams traveling to play in the 1pm timeslot on the East Coast, and the 49ers are working off a rest disadvantage after just playing on Monday Night Football. Health and extra rest could be critical to the Falcons pulling off the upset. That’ll, plus Atlanta figuring out how to deal with blitz pressure and opposing defenses crowding the line of scrimmage. Michael Penix Jr. has been outstanding when kept clean this season, but he’s absolutely cratered when faced with pressure. Part of the issue is that Atlanta has been allowing the fastest time to pressure in the NFL by quite a wide margin, giving Penix little time to react. Hopefully that’s been a major point of emphasis in practice this week. I’m not confident in Atlanta’s ability to take down a superior opponent, especially coming off the past two weeks. So I’m going to say that the 49ers should win this game. However, Atlanta’s potential health advantage along with the extra rest and the West Coast-East Coast factors could combine to give the Falcons a real shot in this one. Plus, Evan would be remiss if I didn’t mention the RED HELMET ENERGY. It’s uncanny, but the Falcons typically play great in this uniform. Will they pull it off? That’s the question I don’t feel confident answering.

full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons passes the ball against Jordan Elliott #92 of the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter in the game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images At 2-4, your chances of pulling out of a tailspin and returning to relevance are not great. If you’re in the NFC South, your odds are more reasonable, but not if you’re all the way down at 2-5 and the Carolina Panthers are at 4-2, which is something that could happen this weekend. The Falcons need to get their first home win of the season against arguably the most daunting opponent they’ve faced thus far. It will not be an easy task. San Francisco has survived injuries that would have relegated a lesser franchise to a chain of losses and have still somehow managed to go 6-0. The sheer weight of those injuries is definitely impacting this team—the loss of Mike Evans caused their offense to crater in the second half against the Washington Commanders last week—but Brock Purdy is playing out of his mind and this is a very well-coached bunch, with Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris working some magic. How can the Falcons win? Let’s talk about what you need to know for Week 7. Team rankings Team Record Points Scored Yardage Passing Yards Rushing Yards Points Against Yardage Against Passing Yards Against Rushing Yardage Against Turnovers Created Turnovers Surrendered Falcons 2-4 16 12 24 4 23 18 28 4 27 28 49ers 6-0 3 9 12 6 4 5 11 8 19 11 Yeah, the 49ers are a lot better than the Falcons. Sometimes these rankings can be a little deceptive, but How the 49ers have changed in 2026 Maybe the biggest change was ending a carousel at defensive coordinator (I imagine, given the results) by hiring Raheem Morris. After spending two years as Atlanta’s head coach, Morris reunited with Shanahan and went back to being a defensive coordinator, something he’s done at a high level throughout his career. Thus far, Morris has this defense looking terrific, which is no great surprise. The team also went out and signed longtime Buccaneer Mike Evans, which was good tidings for Falcons fans sick of seeing him twice a year. While Evans is perptually dinged up at this stage of his career, he’s also been outstanding when he is on the field. They also traded for Osa Odighizuwa from Dallas, adding another formidable presence up front, and otherwise primarily focused on re-signings and depth needs to shore up a roster that seems to be among the league’s most injured every single year. The draft was pretty nails for San Francisco, as well, with receiver De’Zhaun Stribling looking excellent (until he got hurt), pass rusher Romello Height coming into his own (despite injuries), running back Kaelon Black looking like a solid complement to Christian McCaffrey, and defenders Gracen Halton and Jaden Dugger carving out major roles early (again, partially owing to injury). The early returns are incredibly promising. Otherwise, you have the strong core and coaching staff that has made this team an annual contender despite an unbelievable laundry list of injuries. I had my doubts about them coming into this year, but they’ve effectively erased those doubts. What to know about Week 7 Brock Purdy is the key. The Falcons utterly failed to slow Caleb Williams during the first half of Week 6 in particular, and he powered the Bears to a decisive victory. Late in Week 5, the Falcons couldn’t get pressure on Tyler Huntley before he got the ball out, and he willed the Ravens to a win. The problem with Purdy is that he’s generally excellent working against pressure, at least compared to his peers. His 54.3% completion percentage against pressure is the second-best mark in the NFL among starters, and he’s just one of four (out of 25 qualifiers who have played at least 50% of their team’s offensive snaps) quarterbacks who hasn’t thrown an interception under pressure. He doesn’t get the ball out quickly, but that’s both a function of better-than-expected line play and his feel for pressure, which allows him to evade and keep plays alive. He will hold on to the ball long enough to walk himself into sacks, which is Atlanta’s best bet. He’s still a lesser quarterback when pressured and sacks still matter; it’s just that the splits are much less sharp than they are for most passers. That’s especially true because the 49ers are working with a seriously depleted receiving corps. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel may well miss this game, leaving a diminished Christian Kirk, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing as their top three receivers. Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle take significant pressure off this corps and raise the urgency for the Falcons to be very sharp in coverage, naturally, but that’s not a great group for Purdy to work with. The hope is that Atlanta’s pass rush can get home often enough—and those receivers flub it up often enough—that San Francisco’s passing game goes from elite to good but not fatal. Of course, that’s assuming you can stop the run. Atlanta sold out to do so against the Bears and managed to wrestle Roschon Johnson, D’Andre Swift, and company to under 100 yards, but they paid for it through the air. They’ll have to decide whether it’s worth doing that with Christian McCaffrey and Kaleon Black, who have been an excellent tandem once again in 2026, when the passing attack is such an obvious threat. McCaffrey has historically been difficult for the Falcons to stop, while Black is a patient, physical runner who does a nice job of taking what his blockers give him; the 49ers will be intent on achieving balance and it’s up to the Falcons to make them one-dimensional in the hopes they can tee off on Purdy. There just aren’t any easy wins with this offense, unfortunately. Defensively, the 49ers are cooking under Raheem Morris, who will likely relish this chance to humble the team that fired him in the offseason. While the 49ers aren’t grabbing a ton of interceptions—Renardo Green is the only player on the team with any, and he has three—they’re getting pressure, piling up sacks, defending the run well, and forcing fumbles at an alarming rate. They aren’t doing anything poorly right now, even if injuries are making a slight dent in their overall talent level, and that makes this game a real challenge. I said the Falcons had to shut down the run against Baltimore (nope!) and Caleb Williams against Chicago (also nope!) to stand a chance the past two weeks, but this week there isn’t any one item to check off the list. It’s going to require Atlanta’s best full team effort, complete with minimal mistakes, penalties, and turnovers, to realistically stand a chance of knocking off one of the three or four most impressive teams in football. Anything short of that is going to make for a rough Sunday.
author: Dave Choate

title: Why the Falcons need to prioritize Kyle Pitts to solve passing game woes
summary: With less than 11 minutes left in the fourth quarter, Kyle Pitts caught his second pass on a quick out as the Falcons trailed 31-7. It’s normally a standard route and play for a tight end to make in a lopsided matchup. It became the spark the Falcons needed for an unexpected comeback attempt. It […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 11: Atlanta tight end Kyle Pitts (8) reacts after catching a touchdown pass during the NFL game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Atlanta Falcons on October 11th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With less than 11 minutes left in the fourth quarter, Kyle Pitts caught his second pass on a quick out as the Falcons trailed 31-7. It’s normally a standard route and play for a tight end to make in a lopsided matchup. It became the spark the Falcons needed for an unexpected comeback attempt. It also could prove to be the platform to help combat one of the most pressing issues surrounding the Falcons. The Bears soundly outplayed them in every phase of the game, making it an uncompetitive matchup at one point in the second half. The defensive front got bulldozed out of gaps and struggled to maintain its rush integrity against Caleb Williams. The special teams were an absolute disaster, headlined by Zachariah Branch’s nightmare performance that every rookie dreads. Despite those glaring shortcomings and breakdowns, the most damaging aspect of the loss was how overwhelmed the offense looked against Chicago’s pressure looks. For the second consecutive game, Michael Penix Jr. looked incapable of making the right reads and throwing accurately under pressure for long stretches. The coaching staff’s game plan to combat Dennis Allen’s constant schemed-up pressures should raise plenty of questions. Penix Jr. still could have operated better with quicker processing and better feel for blindside pressure. It took until the fourth quarter for him to find some rhythm against Chicago’s defense when they rushed five or six. That’s when Penix Jr. connected with Jahan Dotson for 32 yards on a stop route, where Dotson made a nice hesitation move that turned a solid completion into an explosive gain. It was a sharp play beating Chicago’s five-man pressure. Dotson’s career inconsistency and overall limitations make you cautious about his ability to create separation on the outside often enough to give Penix Jr. high-percentage looks against blitzes. What Pitts did on the next play can be replicated, albeit hopefully not as dramatically for the sake of the Falcons. Dangerous in the slot Per Pro Football Focus, Pitts ran 17 routes from the slot versus Chicago. That was a season high, easily surpassing the seven he ran against Carolina. Some of the high usage from the slot can be attributed to the game script. It was the first game this season where the Falcons were behind all game long with Penix Jr. under center. That proved to be a recipe for success after three quarters of a mostly inept dropback passing game. Chicago brought six with former Falcon Clark Phillips rushing in unblocked. Penix Jr. had to get the ball out quickly again to Pitts outside the numbers. The throw was inside of Pitts, allowing Elijah Hicks to close in for a potential interception. Somehow, the 2025 second-team All-Pro tight end ripped the ball away and juked past Nick McCloud to produce a remarkable 29-yard gain. In the process, he prevented a certain turnover with his improved contested-catch ability. Those types of completions could be an instant solution to the Falcons’ problems against crowded fronts and blitzes. Whether defenses only rush four or bring the entire house with seven or somewhere in between, Baltimore and Chicago have provided a blueprint to rattle Penix Jr. by crowding the line of scrimmage with bodies. Combine that with Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees falling short of answers schematically, and you get a dropback passing game that severely limits the offense. That can’t happen against top-tier teams like the Ravens and Bears. Three plays after the highlight-reel reception, Pitts was in the slot again on third down. Chicago rushed six, with Allen being relentless in trying to force Penix Jr. into another off-target throw or sack. Instead, the young quarterback found Pitts uncovered, as Hicks couldn’t make up the ground to stop him. It was a routine touchdown, but it showed how Pitts can be a dependable solution to a glaring problem. Despite being such a unique talent as a deep threat, Pitts can be maximized in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. He proved last year that he can consistently make defenders miss and run through contact after the catch. His blocking has improved enough that he can play more in-line and create more mismatches with his explosiveness off the line of scrimmage. While he should be used more in the slot following Olamide Zaccheaus’ poor play and Branch’s disastrous game, Pitts can also line up more traditionally as a tight end to bolster the Falcons’ aerial attack. Being quick and decisive After Jessie Bates connected on his signature peanut punch to force a fumble, as he does multiple times a year, it didn’t take long for Penix Jr. to go back to Pitts. Operating in no-huddle, they slowed Chicago’s pressure plan and capitalized on Pitts being isolated inside with an undersized defensive back. Targeting that mismatch helped Penix Jr. find Pitts to convert on third and nine. They connected again on the next play to get in the end zone, putting the Falcons within striking distance of an outrageous comeback. A slight rub by Zaccheaus on the slant-flat concept gave Pitts the space necessary to score his second touchdown of the game. As much as fans want to see Pitts be utilized like the unicorn he was projected to be, the coaching staff needs him more than ever as a possession pass-catcher in these situations to give Penix Jr. an immediate option under pressure. There will be instances where he can thrive in the slot, like against Chicago. He could also line up as an in-line tight end, chipping an edge rusher and serving as a reliable outlet underneath. Whatever the play design, Pitts needs to be a bigger focal point to make the passing game more efficient. According to TruMedia, the Bears blitzed Penix Jr. on an alarming 48.7 percent of his dropbacks. That could increase in upcoming matchups against Todd Bowles, Steve Spagnuolo, and Brian Flores. Those coaches won’t hesitate to ramp up the pressure on any quarterback, let alone a young passer who isn’t reacting well when seven defenders are lined up across the line of scrimmage. The coaching staff will have to do its share schematically to solidify their protection plan. Making Pitts a bigger focal point in the passing game is the other vital step to punish defenses for constantly blitzing. Signs are emerging in recent weeks, as Pitts’ target share has increased over the last three games. That said, those targets have to come earlier in games. Pitts catching only his second pass late in what was arguably the Falcons’ most disappointing performance of the season (with a starting-caliber quarterback under center) indicates he needs to be prioritized far more early and often.
author: Allen Strk

title: Ravens list QB Lamar Jackson as questionable for Sunday vs. Bengals
summary: The Baltimore Ravens listed quarterback Lamar Jackson as questionable for their Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after a full week of limited participation in practice, leaving his status for Sunday’s game up in the air. Jackson, 29, said that he was “heading in the right direction” to return from his two-game absence. The […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts after the Ravens score in overtime against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens listed quarterback Lamar Jackson as questionable for their Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after a full week of limited participation in practice, leaving his status for Sunday’s game up in the air. Jackson, 29, said that he was “heading in the right direction” to return from his two-game absence. The ninth-year quarterback went down in Week 5 against the Titans with an ankle injury that has been the subject of rampant speculation over the last two weeks. He revealed on Friday that he was dealing with a high ankle sprain, contradicting a report from NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. “He part of the training staff?” Jackson joked. The two-time MVP insisted that his condition was improving, but he is still struggling to put pressure on his left leg while running. He said he does not have to be at 100% to play, but characterized playing through injuries last year as “dumb, a little bit.” Remaining limited in Friday’s practice suggests that Jackson is not fully ready to play, but he twice noted having a “grace period” before making a final decision. The Ravens will have to be careful with how they handle Jackson’s status for Sunday. Last year, he was initially listed as questionable in Week 8 after a limited-limited-full practice week, his first since injuring his hamstring three weeks prior. He was ruled out on Saturday, prompting an investigation from the NFL and a $100,000 fine. The Ravens also listed defensive tackle Broderick Washington (ankle) as questionable on their final Week 7 injury report. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) and outside linebacker Tavius Robinson (pectoral) were ruled out; the latter will not play against this season and will likely be placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) is doubtful and will likely need at least one more week of practice before being activated from IR. By comparison, the Bengals are coming into Sunday’s matchup significantly healthier. They did not list a single player with an official injury designation for their trip to Baltimore.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens OLB Tavius Robinson out for season with pectoral injury
summary: Baltimore Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson will miss the rest of the 2026 season with a pectoral injury, head coach Jesse Minter announced on Friday. It is unclear exactly when Robinson suffered the injury. The 27-year-old was on the field throughout last week’s game in Cleveland, including the final play. He played fewer snaps than […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Tavius Robinson #95 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he takes the field against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson will miss the rest of the 2026 season with a pectoral injury, head coach Jesse Minter announced on Friday. It is unclear exactly when Robinson suffered the injury. The 27-year-old was on the field throughout last week’s game in Cleveland, including the final play. He played fewer snaps than usual, though that can also be explained by Trey Hendrickson’s return from a two-game absence and Mike Green’s increased snaps on the left side of the defense, where Robinson usually lines up. This is the second straight season in which Robinson will miss significant time. He spent two months on injured reserve last year after breaking his foot in Week 6. He returned with 2.5 sacks in his final four games and was expected to take another step forward in a contract year under a new defensive staff. Robinson got off to an excellent start this season with one sack and one tackle for loss in each of his first two games. Through six weeks, the 2023 fourth-round pick leads the defense with 3.5 sacks to go along with 18 tackles (three for loss), two passes defended, and a forced fumble that sent the Ravens’ eventual Week 5 win in Atlanta into overtime. The hit also knocked out Falcons quarterback Michael Penix, bringing Tua Tagovailoa onto the field to set up Kyle Hamilton’s game-sealing interception. Robinson’s underlying pass rush metrics indicate a lower direct impact, but his power, length, and motor have helped him set a hard edge and clean up plays in the backfield. The 6-foot-6 Canadian was in line for a major payday next offseason; the extent of his pectoral injury will determine his recovery time and adjust his market value accordingly. The Ravens will rely on their young outside linebacker depth to weather Robinson’s absence. Green will spend even more time on the left side, where he has been less effective as a pass rusher. He has improved as a run defender, which will be crucial with Robinson sidelined. Baltimore also has a pair of rookies who offer size and physicality that can fill Robinson’s role more directly. 6-foot-5 second-round pick Zion Young has excelled in run defense thus far but has struggled to win as a pass rusher. 6-foot-6 UDFA Ethan Burke played well enough during Hendrickson’s two-game absence to remain in the game day picture after his return. Both will be in line for significant increases in playing time. The Ravens also have Adisa Isaac and Kaimon Rucker on the practice squad. One will likely be elevated for Sunday’s game as injury insurance and special teams depth.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: AFC North Preview, Week 7: Bengals and Ravens face off in high-stakes matchup
summary: Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: @ New Orleans Saints (London), 9:30am EST The Steelers are traveling to London this week as the “road” team in a matchup with the New Orleans Saints — making them the second AFC North squad to play internationally this season. Last week, Pittsburgh escaped Tampa Bay with an overtime victory, […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - DECEMBER 14: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) sits on the field after being sacked during the game against the Baltimore Ravens and the Cincinnati Bengals on December 14, 2025, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Updated Standings : Cleveland Browns 4-2 Pittsburgh Steelers 4-2 Baltimore Ravens 4-2 Cincinnati Bengals 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: @ New Orleans Saints (London), 9:30am EST The Steelers are traveling to London this week as the “road” team in a matchup with the New Orleans Saints — making them the second AFC North squad to play internationally this season. Last week, Pittsburgh escaped Tampa Bay with an overtime victory, their first consecutive win of the year, and improved to 4-2. The Steelers have scored 24+ points in four straight games after a slow offensive start in the first two weeks. Against the Saints, the Steelers have a good chance to continue their scoring momentum. New Orleans is giving up 377.7 yards per game, fourth most in the NFL, and their allowing 29.7 points per game — tied for the worst mark. The Saints have been particularly vulnerable defending the run. Jaylen Warren’s production came back to earth in Week 5, but Rico Dowdle returned and was efficient with 40 yards on seven carries. The Steelers ran the ball only 22 times compared to 49 passes, so expect them to strike more balance in this game. Defensively, the Steelers will need to key in on slowing down star wide receiver Chris Olave — who ranks second in the NFL in receiving yards (580) and fourth in receptions (43). The Saints’ passing attack was prolific through Weeks 1-4 but has taken a step back over the last two games. The Steelers should be able to hold the Saints in check on the ground, though, so prevent quarterback Tyler Shough from making big plays remains the priority. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: vs. Cincinnati Bengals, 1:00pm EST Coming off a loss to the Browns, the Ravens are now trying to avoid a damaging 0-2 divisional record when they host the Bengals this Sunday. Baltimore’s Lamar Jackson-less offense regressed significantly last week. The Ravens scored 10 points within the first few minutes of the game and were shut out from there. Whether or not Jackson returns to action this week remains the biggest storyline and determining factor for the Ravens’ chances of winning. Regardless of whether he’s back or Tyler Huntley is starting again, the Ravens’ offensive line will need to have their best game of the season. The Bengals’ defensive front poses challenges, particularly on the interior with star defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence. Cam Jurgens, whom the Ravens recently acquired via trade, is set to make his first start with the team at center and will be immediately tested. Lawrence is capable of wrecking any game plan the Ravens have if they can’t block him. The offensive tackles will also need to be up to the task against Boye Mafe, Myles Murphy and Cedric Johnson on the edge. The Ravens will be similarly tested on defense in the secondary, where they’re tasked with slowing down Cincinnati’s high-powered passing attack. Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have given the Ravens issues over the years, and they will need a strong performance from Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey on the outside to limit explosive passing plays. Getting consistent quarterback pressure, like the Ravens did last week in Cleveland, will be important to make Joe Burrow uncomfortable. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: @ Baltimore Ravens, 1:00pm EST On the other side of this week’s AFC North showdown, the Bengals are fresh off a bye week and heading into Baltimore with extra rest and preparation time. Before their break, they snapped a two-game losing streak with a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins to get back over .500 by one game. Both Chase and Higgins were playing off of injuries in that game, so the bye week came at a good time for the Bengals to get extra healthy. If Jackson is not playing, the defensive task becomes much easier for the Bengals. Like the Browns did last week, the Bengals will likely crowd the box at the line of scrimmage and play tight man coverage — forcing Huntley to beat them downfield. The Ravens have not been as efficient running the ball this season and have struggled in short-yardage conversion attempts with Derrick Henry. If the Bengals can control the line of scrimmage with their defensive front, they should be able to find some defensive success regardless of the quarterback. The Ravens’ defense has played a lot of two-high safety looks and dared offenses to beat them in the middle of the field. The Bengals will likely try to establish the run in a difficult road environment, but that’s been an area of weakness for them this year. Their 82.8 rushing yards per game ranks fifth-worst in the NFL, while they’re in the Top 10 in passing yards. In 10 career games against the Ravens, Chase has totaled 75 receptions and 1,204 receiving yards with eight touchdowns. Cleveland Browns Matchup: @ Tennessee Titans, 1:00pm EST The Browns continue to defy expectations and improved to 4-2 with a win over the Ravens last week, reclaiming first-place position in the division. Like their previous three victories before, the Browns won by four points or less and their win came via a late fourth quarter scoring drive to take the lead. Whether or not this is sustainable remains to be seen, but they’ve put themselves in good position thus far regardless. A more favorable contest is on the docket this week against a one-win Titans team, who the Browns are narrow favorites to beat on the road. It’s projected to be another low-scoring affair. The Browns’ defense should be able to handle Tennessee’s offense with relative ease. The Titans are averaging just 14.0 points per game, tied for the worst mark in the league, and have the least productive passing attack of any team. They are coming off a season-best showing, however, having scored 26 points in their first win of the season last week. The Titans’ defense has been much more formidable, led by star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons up front, who is a game-wrecking talent. The Browns have continued to struggle running the ball, but Tennessee is vulnerable against the run, allowing over 122 rushing yards per game. Getting Quinshon Judkins back from injury would be a nice boost for this game. He’s on track to play after returning to practice this week in limited fashion.

Baltimore Ravens (4-2, loss to CLE, 0-1 AFCN) 8. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) 9. New England Patriots (4-3) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) 11. New York Jets (2-4, 2-1 AFC) 12. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) The 4-2 AFC tiebreakers explained In the 4-2 cluster, the AFC North is ordered first. The Browns are 2-0 against the Steelers and Ravens, so they are in first place. The 4-2 at the top of the conference is only between the division-leading Jaguars and Browns, and Jacksonville has a win over Cleveland. The Jags are third and the Browns are fourth. The 4-2 Wild Card teams are the Broncos alongside the Steelers thanks to Pittsburgh’s tiebreaker over Baltimore. AFC record is the first tiebreaker since they haven’t played each other, so the 2-1 Broncos followed by the 2-2 Steelers then the Ravens after that. AFC North standings right now 1. Cleveland Browns (4-2, wins over PIT & BAL) 2. Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2, 1-1 AFCN) 3. Baltimore Ravens (4-2, 0-1 AFCN) 4. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) Obviously with the Ravens facing the Bengals this week, it is an important matchup in the division. The Browns play the Titans while the Steelers are in the early Sunday morning game against the New Orleans Saints.

title: Introducing DIP: A new NFL defensive metric that accounts for quarterback competition
summary: What if we had a new way to determine defensive quality in the NFL that would adjust for opposing quarterback quality? It could provide a new answer on just how porous the Buffalo Bills defense really been through six games this season. Introducing: Defensive Impact on Passing (DIP) This new metric measures how every NFL […]
full_text: What if we had a new way to determine defensive quality in the NFL that would adjust for opposing quarterback quality? It could provide a new answer on just how porous the Buffalo Bills defense really been through six games this season. Introducing: Defensive Impact on Passing (DIP) This new metric measures how every NFL defense impacts quarterback performance relative to how those quarterbacks perform against the rest of their opponents. The idea with DIP is to provide a cleaner, more fair snapshot of each defense’s effectiveness by accounting for the quality of the collection of quarterbacks it has faced throughout the season. DIP adds vital context to EPA per dropback by calculating the difference in each quarterback’s performance against a specific defense compared to his baseline against other defenses. For example, if a defense plays an elite-level quarterback averaging +0.348 EPA per dropback and allows an EPA per dropback of +0.212, it would actually be viewed as a “successful” outing for that defense because it surrendered a lower EPA per dropback than what was expected from that quarterback entering the game. On the surface, allowing +0.212 EPA per dropback would be universally viewed as a bad outing for a defensive unit. But not with DIP. The opposite would be true if a defense allowed a “low” EPA per dropback of +0.08 against a quarterback who otherwise managed an EPA per dropback well into the negatives. And now that we’re six full weeks into the NFL season, somewhat of a baseline for each quarterback has been established, so we can measure how defenses are performing relative to expectation Because DIP is measuring EPA per dropback and not EPA per individual quarterback matchup when looking at defenses collective DIP throughout a season, the formula here is pretty simple: DIP = Total Actual EPA – Total Expected EPA / Total Qualifying DropBacks Like all defensive EPA-based statistics, a lower (negative) number is better, and I’ve adjusted for garbage time, so the “qualifying” stipulation in the denominator equates to those dropbacks when the the win probability is between 10% and 90%. Although I decided on the name DIP, the calculation is per dropback, so scrambles and sacks are counted as well. When determining the quarterback EPA per dropback baseline for a defense, his performance against that specific defense was excluded. Also, for a quarterback’s baseline to be counted, he needed to have at least 30 total dropbacks against other defenses to date this season. Yes, a lot of explainers, I know. Kind of necessary for the introductory article. Oh, and lastly, before I show you chart through Week 6, like all defensive EPA statistics, a negative number is better: Some quick takeaways: Unsurprisingly, the Seahawks defense is still incredibly stingy. The Patriots defense has been sneaky good. Before their Week 7 game against the Bears, they were 14th in EPA per dropback allowed in non-garbage time but were in the No. 3 spot in DIP through Week 6. Strong showing for the Jaguars in DIP too, as they went from No. 17 in EPA per dropback rankings yet are seventh in this metric. Coordinator Anthony Campanille has done a fine job, and he has the horses, particularly in his front seven. The Panthers defense only has 64.2% of their defensive dropbacks faced actually counted in DIP because they faced Cooper Rush in Week 2, Shedeur Sanders for part of Week 3, and Tanner McKee in Week 6, and none of those quarterbacks have at least 30 dropbacks against other defenses to compare to. Philadelphia’s defense has been better than probably given credit for despite facing a relatively strong set of quarterbacks in its first six weeks of the season, including Jayden Daniels, Matthew Stafford, Trevor Lawrence, and Bryce Young. The Texans defense is still not to its 2025 level, but it’s playing better than the raw figures would suggest. Houston is 21st in DIP (as opposed to 26th in regular EPA per dropback). The most sizable discrepancy between regular EPA per dropback allowed and DIP belongs to the Saints. They’re 22nd in regular EPA per dropback and 9th in this new metric. Teams with a lower DIP than their actual EPA per dropback allowed through Week 6 include the 49ers (7th to 16th), Browns (5th to 15th), Ravens (11th to 19th), and Giants (12th to 17th). The Bills get a bump from 25th in EPA per dropback to 23rd in DIP. They have seen a rather daunting run of quarterbacks to begin the year including C.J. Stroud, Goff, Maye, Stafford and Kirk. And it’s not as if things are getting easier when Buffalo returns from its bye in Week 8 to welcome the Ravens to Orchard Park. While the end of November does feature a clash with Patrick Mahomes, they do have games against Malik Willis and Geno Smith sandwiched between those battles with former MVP quarterbacks.

title: Dion Dawkins’ dramatic offseason weight loss ‘a gift and a curse’
summary: Many fans of the Buffalo Bills have noticed a slimmed down version of Dion Dawkins this season. The Shnowman, as he likes to be called, dropped forty pounds this offseason and had to relearn how to play left tackle a little because of it, but he’s happy with the results. “With losing 42 pounds as […]
full_text: ﻿Dion Dawkins poses in front of a Polaris off-road vehicle | Polaris press release Many fans of the Buffalo Bills have noticed a slimmed down version of Dion Dawkins this season. The Shnowman, as he likes to be called, dropped forty pounds this offseason and had to relearn how to play left tackle a little because of it, but he’s happy with the results. “With losing 42 pounds as a lineman, I’m telling you, it’s kind of a gift and a curse. I’m almost like a tank. When you’re a tank and you’re used to running through buildings and walls and going over things and ‘I did that easy’ and now you’re forty pounds less and you’re like ‘Oh, it took an extra gear to get through it all.” It feels great. “I feel like I look better. I feel better. I am able to move around quicker. In the profession of perfecting your body, I decided to drastically change my body so now I’m trying to re-perfect this new body that I have.” The Bills didn’t tell Dawkins to get lighter in the offseason. Already an NFL Top 100 player and a multi-time Pro Bowler, the veteran says they left it up to him what shape he would come into camp with and how to reshape his body in the offseason. In addition to boxing and walking five miles a day in a sauna suit bag, he would drink more than two gallons of lemon water and cut his food intake to one meal a day. “I talked to the strength staff [of the Bills]. It was just more so like ‘What should I be eating so I’m not hurting myself’ because I was losing so much weight. They kind of got me to the right protein amount and what I should not be eating.“ The protein was lean — either one piece of chicken of two pieces of salmon — and he threw in a handful of broccoli, too. “And I’m telling you, in the beginning it was hard, but once you get through the first week it’s just ‘I don’t wanna eat and do anything else but drink two gallons of lemon water and eat a piece of grilled chicken and I don’t even care about anything else.‘“ Dawkins says that while it’s fluctuated a little but, he’s been able to consistently idle in the 330 to 340-pound range. He thinks that is going to help elongate his career after turning 32 in April. “The overall goal was I want to play for as long as I can and to take a little bit off your body, it might help you. So I was just trying to figure out what really helped and what didn’t. With locking into training and understanding that you’re in the course of the gauntlet of training, just diving in, and when I dove all in for that month and a half to two months, it was just like I was training for a UFC fight. It felt like I was just cutting weight every day.” You can watch the full interview with Dawkins here, including some conversation about Polaris and Call of Duty that was really fun: Dawkins was made available to Buffalo Rumblings through his partnership with Polaris, Call of Duty’s official off-road vehicle partner. The addition of the Polaris DAGOR to Call of Duty highlights a different side of Polaris innovation, showcasing the company’s military and government capabilities alongside its recreational powersports portfolio. The DAGOR marks the latest milestone in Polaris’ ongoing collaboration with Call of Duty, following the introduction of RZR Pro R in 2024 and Sportsman XP 1000 in 2025. What began with vehicle integrations has grown into a broader collaboration spanning gaming, consumer engagement and real-world activations. DAGOR is a natural fit for Modern Warfare 4. Designed for rapid deployment, maneuverability, modularity and durability in demanding environments, it brings authentic tactical capability to the game while introducing players to a vehicle built for mission-focused mobility. The partnership helps tell a broader Polaris story. Polaris is not only a leader in recreational powersports, but also develops military and commercial off-road vehicles designed for mission-focused mobility and real-world applications. There is a strong element of pride in what DAGOR represents for Polaris – a company founded in 1954 and headquartered in Minnesota, with deep American roots and a history of engineering vehicles built to perform in challenging environments.

title: NFL trade deadline: Buffalo Bills trade candidate – Tariq Woolen
summary: How about cornerback for the Buffalo Bills at the trade deadline? If so, would Tariq Woolen move the needle? He’s the league’s largest outside cornerback at just over 6’4” and 208 pounds who signed a one-year deal in March with the now 2-4 Eagles. He’s most known for his six-interception rookie campaign, and he’s snagged […]
full_text: How about cornerback for the Buffalo Bills at the trade deadline? If so, would Tariq Woolen move the needle? He’s the league’s largest outside cornerback at just over 6’4” and 208 pounds who signed a one-year deal in March with the now 2-4 Eagles. He’s most known for his six-interception rookie campaign, and he’s snagged six since then in the regular season. This article is the third in the trade-candidate series I plan to sprinkle onto the site until the actual trade deadline until November 10, which is 18 days from now, and lands after Week 9. Past installments in this series: Derwin James , Brian Thomas Jr. Jessie Bates Age: 27 Woolen entered the NFL out of the University of Texas San Antonio in 2022 after one of the craziest combines we’d ever seen at the cornerback position. At his gargantuan size, Woolen ran 4.26 with a 42-inch vertical. The Seahawks drafted him in the fifth round that year. After the spectacular rookie campaign, Woolen’s ball production cooled, yet he’s established himself as one of the better young physical (and speedy) outside cornerbacks in the NFL. He was integral on Seattle’s Super Bowl winning defense in 2025, playing 72.8% of the snaps and logging 41 tackles, 12 pass breakups, and a pick during the regular season. In the playoffs, Woolen registered four more pass breakups with eight total tackles. 2026 snap splits Wide corner: 85.6% Box: 12.4% On the snap-split front, Woolen has a grand total of seven total snaps in the box, on the defensive line, and at free safety. For all intents and purposes, he’s about as full-time of an outside corner as it gets in today’s NFL. How he’d fit with Bills Given his size, explosiveness, experience, and pass-breakup radius (arm length in the 97th percentile), Woolen is a fun fit on just about every team. The Seahawks had the NFL’s fifth-highest zone coverage rate in 2025 and had a Top 10 zone-coverage percentage in three of Woolen’s four seasons with the club. The Eagles are almost right smack dab in the middle of zone-coverage rate (15th) in these first six games. Essentially, Woolen is best in an off-man, zone-coverage style defense, and while Jim Leonhard was known for a man-coverage philosophy, the Bills have the ninth-lowest man-coverage rate entering their bye week. Woolen has had double-digit pass breakups in each of his first four seasons in the NFL, and that six-pick rookie year of 2022 This year in Philadelphia, he’s played in all six games and has defended four passes to go along with 24 tackles. On 30 targets in his coverage area, Woolen has allowed 16 catches for 206 yards with three touchdowns. He’s surrendered a completion rate over 59% on targets in his coverage area in just one season to date in the NFL. In short, Woolen would fit schematically — if the Bills continue their zone-heavy ways — I just don’t know if there’s room for him to come in and start at outside corner. Financial obligation for Bills to trade for him 2026 salary: $1.26M If the Bills trade for Woolen after Week 9, they’d be on the hook for $630k in prorated 2026 base salary. He’s an impending free agent after this season, which simultaneously creates plenty of flexibility for the Bills if he were to be in their future plans and lowers his asking price. Projected cost to acquire Using Syndicate32.com’s trade machine , the projected cost to trade for Woolen is an early Round 4 pick in 2027. That feels just right for a player of Woolen’s caliber, at his age, and with his contract situation. He’s demonstrated big-play ability in his past but hasn’t been able to recreate the magic from his rookie season in 2022. Should the Bills trade for Tariq Woolen? If the Bills feel they desperately need to add an outside cornerback to the defense, Woolen should be at or near the top of their trade-candidate list at that position. With Christian Benford, Davison Igbinosun, and, yes, even Max Hairston (I’d be silly to quit on him at this juncture), I don’t necessarily see how swinging a deal for a starting-caliber outside cornerback would be something the Bills brass would believe is a necessity right now. Yet, given his expiring contract, the fact he should be in the prime of his NFL career, and what should be a relatively low acquisition cost, I could be talked into Woolen as a trade-deadline target simply because it’d give the Bills more talent in the secondary. His 70-plus games of NFL experience is very enticing too, especially relative to the youth in Buffalo’s cornerback room right now. If the Bills can pry Woolen away from Howie Roseman and the Eagles for a fourth or fifth-round pick, I’d view the towering, incredibly fast and lengthy cornerback as a fine addition to Buffalo. If he’s brought in, the Bills would have plus depth in their outside cornerback room.

title: Buffalo Bills Week 7 rooting interests: Who to root for during the bye
summary: After six weeks of the 2026 NFL season, the Buffalo Bills are sitting at 5-1 and holding down the AFC’s No. 2 seed. Not bad for a team some people were predicting would start the season 0-5.  Now comes the bye week. Personally, I’m not a fan of having it this early, especially with the […]
full_text: After six weeks of the 2026 NFL season, the Buffalo Bills are sitting at 5-1 and holding down the AFC’s No. 2 seed. Not bad for a team some people were predicting would start the season 0-5. Now comes the bye week. Personally, I’m not a fan of having it this early, especially with the Bills riding the momentum of a two-win West Coast trip. But there is some good news. No matter what happens around the league this weekend, Buffalo can’t lose its spot as the AFC’s second seed. Of course, the bad news is that the Bills can’t move up to No. 1, either. The worst-case scenario? New England wins and picks up a half-game on Buffalo in the AFC East. But with two losses already on their record, the Patriots would still be looking up at the Bills in both the division and conference standings. The best-case scenario? Kansas City loses, dropping the Chiefs to 5-1 and putting them in a tie with Buffalo. But , because the Chiefs would still hold the conference-record tiebreaker, Kansas City would hang on to the AFC’s No. 1 seed… for now. With all that out of the way, Let’s see who we want winning — and, more importantly, losing — this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ AFC Standings entering Week 7 1. Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) 2. Buffalo Bills (5-1) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) 4. Cleveland Browns (4-2) 5. New England Patriots (4-2) 6. Denver Broncos (4-2) 7. Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) 8. Baltimore Ravens (4-2) 9. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) 11. New York Jets (2-4) 12. Indianapolis Colts (2-4) 13. Houston Texans (2-4) 14. Tennessee Titans (1-5) 15. Miami Dolphins (0-5) 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) _____________________________________________________________________________ AFC East New England Patriots at Chicago Bears Root For: Chicago Bears The Patriots are the only team in the AFC East with a realistic shot at catching Buffalo right now, and they’re already just a game behind in the win column. A loss to Chicago would drop New England to 4-3 and give the Bills a little more breathing room in the division without even taking the field. Miami Dolphins at New York Jets Root For: Miami Dolphins Neither team is much of a threat to Buffalo at this point, but somebody has to win this one. The Jets already have two wins, while Miami’s still looking for its first. A Dolphins win would keep the Jets from getting any ideas about making a run at a playoff spot while also nudging Miami away from prime draft position. _____________________________________________________________________________ The rest of the AFC Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints Root For: New Orleans Saints Pittsburgh is one of several AFC teams sitting at 4-2, just a game behind Buffalo in the loss column. The Steelers are also in the middle of a crowded AFC North race. A loss to New Orleans would knock them back a step in both the division and wild-card standings. Plus, it’s an NFC team against an AFC contender. This one is pretty straightforward. Indianapolis Colts at Minnesota Vikings Root For: Minnesota Vikings The Colts are sitting at 2-4 and aren’t exactly breathing down Buffalo’s neck. But there’s no reason to help another AFC team get back into the playoff conversation. A Minnesota win keeps Indianapolis from gaining any ground. Additionally, the Bills play the Vikings in a couple of weeks, so a Minnesota win can help their Strength of Schedule score. Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens Root For: Cincinnati Bengals Both teams are chasing playoff spots, but Baltimore is the bigger concern right now. The Ravens are 4-2, while Cincinnati is 3-2. A Bengals win would pull Baltimore back into the pack and keep another four-win AFC team from gaining ground on Buffalo. Cincinnati would improve its position, but that’s a trade worth making. Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans Root For: Tennessee Titans Cleveland currently holds the AFC’s four seed, making this one an easy choice. A loss to Tennessee would drop the Browns to 4-3 and give Buffalo a little more separation from another division leader. The Titans, meanwhile, are sitting at the bottom of the AFC South. Letting them pick up a second win isn’t going to cause much trouble for the Bills. New York Giants at Houston Texans Root For: New York Giants There’s a small gamble in rooting against Houston. The Bills already beat the Texans this season, so another Houston win would improve Buffalo’s strength of victory. But it would also give the Texans a little life in the AFC playoff race, and there’s no reason to help another team get back into contention. Buffalo controls its own destiny right now, and as long as the Bills keep taking care of business, they won’t need that tiebreaker anyway. We’ll take the Giants and keep Houston down. Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals Root For: Arizona Cardinals Denver is 4-2 and currently holds one of the AFC’s wild-card spots. With the Bills sitting comfortably in second place, there’s no reason to let another potential playoff contender gain ground. A loss to Arizona would put another game between Buffalo and Denver, and that’s reason enough to pull for the Cardinals. Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders Root For: Los Angeles Rams These are the two teams the Bills just beat on their West Coast trip, so either outcome will help Buffalo’s strength of victory. But the Raiders are still hanging around the AFC wild-card race, while the Rams are safely over in the NFC. A Los Angeles win gives the Bills the tiebreaker boost without helping another AFC team get closer to the playoffs. Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks Root For: Seattle Seahawks This is the big one. Kansas City is the only team ahead of Buffalo in the AFC standings, and a Seahawks win would hand the Chiefs their first loss of the season. Both the Bills and KC would then be 5-1, although Kansas City would retain the No. 1 seed on the conference-record tiebreaker, but the Bills can take care of that themselves on Thanksgiving. Buffalo can’t take over the top spot this week, but having the Chiefs lose their cushion would be a pretty good way to spend the bye. _____________________________________________________________________________ NFC vs NFC games Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions Root For: Detroit Lions The Bills already have a win over Detroit this season, so every Lions win helps Buffalo’s strength of victory. And while Buffalo will travel to Green Bay later this season, the strength-of-victory boost from a Detroit win takes priority over the strength-of-schedule benefit of a Packers win. Games That Don’t Matter (to the Bills, Anyway) Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Carolina Panthers San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons _____________________________________________________________________________ Teams on Bye Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders _____________________________________________________________________________ There won’t be any Bills football this weekend, but there are still plenty of reasons to keep an eye on the scoreboard. If a few of these games go Buffalo’s way, the bye week might turn out to be pretty productive after all. Go Bills!

title: Panthers Injury Report & Transactions – Week 7
summary: The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries The Panthers overall team health continues to improve on the whole this week with only a couple of noteworthy injuries to monitor as Carolina faces the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jaelan Phillips #5 of the Carolina Panthers reacts during the second quarter against the Chicago Bears of the game at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries The Panthers overall team health continues to improve on the whole this week with only a couple of noteworthy injuries to monitor as Carolina faces the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The biggest loss this week is outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips who has been ruled out due to a hamstring issue. In five games this season the sixth-year veteran has 10 tackles, 2.5 sacks, and six quarterback hits. Veteran right tackle Taylor Moton made his 2026 debut last week and looks ready to roll in Week 7. Moton’s backup, first round rookie Monroe Freeling, is questionable for Sunday after missing the Panthers previous game with a knee issue. Running back AJ Dillon missed last week’s game with an ankle injury, but he has been a full participant in this practice leading up to Sunday’s kickoff. Transactions Designated LB Bam Martin-Scott to return to practice Martin-Scott suffered a hamstring injury before the season began and is still on the injured reserve. By now being designated to return to practice, the 21-day window is now open and he’s on the path to returning to action. The former South Carolina Gamecock joined the Panthers last year as an undrafted free agent and had a strong rookie campaign. He appeared in all 17 of Carolina’s games in 2025 as a special teams mainstay, registering 21 tackles and one forced fumble. Signed RB Tre Tyus to the active roster from the practice squad If you want to see how unstable life is for young undrafted players, just look at Tre Tyus’s transaction page . Tyus went undrafted last year, signed with the Detroit Lions, and was subsequently waived during final roster cuts. In October of last year he signed with the Panthers practice squad but didn’t see the field. Carolina signed him to a futures contract for 2026 and this year they have either waived him from the practice squad, re-signed him to the practice squad, or elevated him to the active man roster in 11 separate transactions since late August. He’s on the upswing this week after another elevation to the active roster. He has appeared in three games for the Panthers this year with five kick returns with an average of 25.4 yards per return. Waived OT Albert Reese With the return of Taylor Moton adding to the number of Carolina’s linemen on the active roster, the Panthers released offensive tackle Albert Reese. The 6-foot-7, 330-pound undrafted rookie from Mississippi State made the initial 53-man roster, but he never saw the field for the Panthers.

title: NFL predictions: The Bucs really shouldn’t be a problem for the Panthers
summary: We’re now at the point of the season where we traditionally would start phasing in heavier coverage of the 2027 NFL Draft and salary cap to provide an optimistic angle towards next season. Unfortunately for our traditions, the Carolina Panthers are actually playing well this year. They are entering the middle of the season as […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) holds his right hand as he walks off the field during the regular season game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on September 27, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.(Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We’re now at the point of the season where we traditionally would start phasing in heavier coverage of the 2027 NFL Draft and salary cap to provide an optimistic angle towards next season. Unfortunately for our traditions, the Carolina Panthers are actually playing well this year. They are entering the middle of the season as the number three seed in the NFC playoff picture and are forcing their fans to confront the fact that some games should be expected as wins. I’m not saying that it will be easy. I’m not saying that an off day by Bryce Young or Will Lee III couldn’t derail their entire season’s momentum. But the most-of-Baker Mayfield they’ll be playing against on Sunday, led by the owner of the hottest seat in the NFC South in Todd Bowles, aren’t the kind of team that should be expected to be beat a good team right now. The Carolina Panthers are trying to convince us all that they are a good team. The next step in their argument will always be simple: play the next game on their schedule and play it well. I think maybe they can do just that. So, too, do the folks over at FanDuel . They’re holding the Panthers as -2.5 point favorites after opening with them as -3 point favorites. Staff predictions for Week 7 Walker Clement Panthers 31, Buccaneers 7 -Bryce Young keeps the offense on track, but the wheels start to come off for both Mayfield and Bowles. The reaper may well strike again. Jonathan DeLong Panthers 27, Buccaneers 14 – The defense capitalizes on whatever the Bucs have going on at quarterback while the offense keeps rolling. Brian Beversluis Panthers 21, Buccaneers 24 – Baker Mayfield has a classic angry game, Panthers lose.* *Editor’s note: Brian hasn’t predicted a win for the Panthers since Week 3 against the Cleveland Browns. Daniel Belton Panthers 30, Buccaneers 17 – The Panthers didn’t Panther last week against a depleted and inferior team, and hopefully that’s a sign of things to come this week against another depleted team. Eric Buchanan Panthers 27, Buccaneers 17 -I’m buying the good vibes in the building right now. The Bucs continue to underperform and half their roster has an illness. A trip to Bank of America won’t be the cure. Andrew Sweat Panthers 27, Buccaneers 17 – The Bucs have failed to score 20 points in four of their last five games, and the Panthers offense is rolling.

title: Brian Answers: Injury woes, scoring points, safety room, and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! I’m here to answer all your questions from earlier in the week, whether they be Panthers related, football related, or even completely off topic! Let’s dive right in to all your questions! kevinjalltheway: The Eagles still had a very […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Zakee Wheatley #20 of the Carolina Panthers defends against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! I’m here to answer all your questions from earlier in the week, whether they be Panthers related, football related, or even completely off topic! Let’s dive right in to all your questions! kevinjalltheway: The Eagles still had a very good defense. If we had wanted to, we could have made it a 2 touchdown win at least with a field goal, let alone powered it in for another touchdown and a 18 point margin of victory. Points scored do matter in playoff scenarios right? I believe I remember years ago when we were competing with the Packers for a playoff spot and we were piling up points on the Buc’s (?) as Green Bay was piling up points against whoever they were playing and we were scoreboard watching. Its very rare that points scored factors into anything, usually the head to head matchups end up being the tie breakers for playoff scenarios in the wild card. I also think with how beaten up this offensive line has been, just getting out of there with the win made a lot of sense. I’m not concerned at all with the decision, and we don’t have to deal with the same hate as fans we had for Sean Payton for running up the score. @WTMealey: BY5K? He’s certainly on pace for it. The Panthers still have a long schedule ahead of them and an injury or two to the receiving options makes that harder. So my official answer is, improbable, but not impossible. schrodingersblackcat: You’re suddenly and inexplicably teleported to the opposing team’s pass rush. Would you rather try to get past Tremble or Hubbard? Chuba Hubbard is a great pass blocker for a running back, but I’m definitely not trying to square up with Tommy Tremble in this scenario. Dude already entered the league as a great blocker and his receiving skills have developed over time. brake23: The safety room has become very interesting. Zakee Wheatley is beginning to emerge as a clear starter moving forward and played 81% of the snaps on Sunday. However, I noticed Ransom to be missing. I thought that he and Chau Smith-Wade’s snaps would have went up with Jaycee and MJ out. Smith-Wade had 2 snaps on defense and Ransom only had 1!!! Is this a result of bad play from either one of them or is Evero just obsessed with sticking with Nick Scott and now Akayleb Evans? I guess this speaks volumes on how he feels about Wheatley being in most of the game as a rookie and essentially benching Ransom. Lathan Ransom’s skillset mirrors that of Tre’Von Moehrig, so I think its more about fielding a diversified skillset rather than having preferences or one guy playing worse than another. Nick Scott is still their deep middle safety, but I think Zakee Wheatley will eventually take that role from him now that we’re seeing consistency. Ejiro Evero has very specific roles in his defenses and he’s fitting the pieces in. Akayleb Evans having a large amount of snaps is puzzling, but I am willing to let Evero cook after a fantastic showing against the Eagles by the entire secondary. sgtx: Hey Brian, The Panthers are riding high and I don’t know how to feel? Help me out. I feel things. I am not sure what they are. But feeling things is better than feeling nothing, which was the norm since the end of the 2010s. DeacCat: Do we need to be concerned that Jaeden Phillips has (I think) only seven tackles in the last four games? Oysters: Raw, Roasted, Steamed, Other? Jaelan Phillips has shown more of an impact simply being on the field than he has as a pass rusher from a statistical standpoint. He collapses the pocket, sets the edge, and pursues in both the rushing and passing game extremely well. His presence opens up the rest of the defense for better matchups and paths in their gaps and pass rushing lanes. Certainly concerning he has been injured, but when he’s in the game, he’s been worth every penny. I am definitely a raw oysters guy. There’s just nothing like it, and a versatile dish. That said, I’m pretty much okay with any style of oyster. Sound off on your favorites in the comments! hollywud: Since someone brought up our safeties, How would you view Tre’von Moehrig’s play this year overall? He doesn’t get mentioned much but seems to be Evero’s chess piece in the defensive scheme. Once Evero started using him as more of a pseudo-linebacker last year, he’s been excellent. His strengths have always been as a blitzer and in run support, and the way Evero deploys him allows them to use guys like Zakee Wheatley, Lathan Ransom, and Nick Scott in more complimentary roles. I think Zakee Wheatley is the big benefactor of having someone like Tre on the field, because he does a lot of things that Wheatley doesn’t excel at. They are building a nice little stable of safeties. Coach_K: Trade deadline not til Nov 10th, but stories/speculation is increasing this week as more players are being waived. Cornerback will be spotlighted no doubt. But how about the running back position? Heard Jonathan Brooks is getting close to coming back, at least jogging. Do you think we’ll bolster that RB position regardless? For instance, saw Najee Harris was let go the other day. It seems like it’s always been for us to have two running backs to share the ball The Panthers seem content shuffling their group of running backs as the rest of the guys behind Chuba Hubbard get healthy. They brought back Trevor Etienne and he had a role this week. I don’t expect them to make any major moves on RB unless Chuba becomes unavailable for an extended period. Probably looking at more of a waiver wire or free agency transaction than a trade. SnarkyComet: Which injured player do you think we’re missing the most right now? Not necessarily our best player who’s out, but if you had a magic wand and could heal any player and insert them directly into the roster, whose return would make the biggest difference given where the team stands today? Probably Jaycee Horn by a country mile, and that’s no slight on anyone else who is injured. There was a clear plan for Horn to man the middle as their nickel corner while still playing outside, he was another chess piece Evero intended to move around as needed. Horn can do it all, he can even blitz extremely well when called upon. I think this defense would be in much better shape if Will Lee was only filling in for Mike Jackson rather than being the number one corner by default. But EDGE Nic Scourton is a very close second, I think this pass rush would be much better rushing four guys if Scourton was fully healthy. SnarkyComet: Looking at the Bucs’ record and the fact that we’re road favorites again this week, it’s easy to feel pretty good about this matchup. But it’s also a divisional rivalry, and we all know how quickly those games can defy expectations. So, what does a Panthers loss look like on Sunday? What are the biggest things Carolina needs to avoid to make sure we come away with a win? The Bucs defense, especially against the run, is underrated. If the Panthers are forced to be one dimensional on offense or simply can’t keep on schedule, that creates a recipe for a very close game that’s won by only one or two big key plays. And the Panthers just can’t stop getting flagged for penalties. They need to come out swinging fast to win this one, in my opinion. That’s all for this week Panthers fans! Enjoy Game Day, and KEEP POUNDING!!
