title: Chicago Bears Week 7 Flashbacks: A GW Drive, NFL History, and More!
summary: Even though the Bears beat the Patriots on Thursday night, this time machine has no brakes! We’re back with three more games from Week 7 from Chicago Bears history. Hop aboard and enjoy this trip on the Gridiron Time Machine! 1. 2007, Bears @ Eagles: Griese engineers a 97-yard miracle October 21, 2007 | Bears […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - OCTOBER 22: Eddie Jackson #39 of the Chicago Bears reacts after the Bears intercepted the football in the fourth quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Soldier Field on October 22, 2017 in Chicago, Illinois. The Chicago Bears defeated the Carolina Panthers 17-3. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Even though the Bears beat the Patriots on Thursday night, this time machine has no brakes! We’re back with three more games from Week 7 from Chicago Bears history. Hop aboard and enjoy this trip on the Gridiron Time Machine! 1. 2007, Bears @ Eagles: Griese engineers a 97-yard miracle October 21, 2007 | Bears win 19-16 The defending NFC champions had stumbled to a 2-4 start in 2007, and things weren’t looking particularly promising in Philadelphia. Chicago’s offense struggled to find the end zone for most of the afternoon, relying on four Robbie Gould field goals to keep pace with the Eagles. When Donovan McNabb connected with Matt Schobel for a touchdown late in the fourth quarter, Philadelphia took a 16-12 lead. The Bears eventually got the football back at their own three-yard line with 1:57 remaining, no timeouts, and needing a touchdown. Enter Brian Griese. With communication problems affecting his helmet headset, Griese called his own plays and marched Chicago 97 yards down the field. He connected with Bernard Berrian and Devin Hester on crucial completions before finding Muhsin Muhammad for a 15-yard touchdown with nine seconds remaining. Griese finished with 322 passing yards and a touchdown, while Muhammad caught five passes for 79 yards. Chicago escaped with a 19-16 victory, improving to 3-4 and keeping its postseason hopes alive. 2. 2017, Bears vs. Panthers: Eddie Jackson makes NFL history October 22, 2017 | Bears win 17-3 Sometimes the defense doesn’t just help win a football game. Sometimes it scores every touchdown. That was the case when Carolina visited Soldier Field in Week 7 of the 2017 season. Rookie safety Eddie Jackson wasted little time announcing himself. On this day in 2017, Eddie Jackson made history with a 75-yard fumble return TD and 76-yard pick six against the Panthers pic.twitter.com/ygZZgVv838 — Depressed Bears Fan (@ImBearsFan) October 22, 2025 On Carolina’s opening possession, Jackson scooped up a loose football and raced 75 yards for a touchdown. Early in the second quarter, he intercepted a deflected Cam Newton pass and returned it 76 yards for another score. Just like that, Jackson had scored 14 points by himself. He became the first player in NFL history to record two defensive touchdowns of at least 75 yards in the same game. The Bears defense finished with three takeaways and five sacks, holding Carolina to just three points despite being outgained 293-153. Perhaps the most ridiculous statistic from the afternoon belonged to Chicago’s offense. Mitchell Trubisky completed just four passes for 107 yards, while the Bears managed only five first downs. None of it mattered. Chicago walked away with a 17-3 victory, improving to 3-4 and recording consecutive wins for the first time since 2015. 3. 2022, Bears @ Patriots: Chicago spoils Belichick’s historic opportunity October 24, 2022 | Bears win 33-14 This one seems particularly appropriate with New England visiting Soldier Field Thursday night. The Bears entered their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup in 2022 riding a three-game losing streak. Meanwhile, Patriots coach Bill Belichick was sitting on 324 career victories, including the postseason, tied with Bears legend George Halas for second-most in NFL history. A victory against Chicago would move Belichick past Papa Bear himself, but the Bears had other ideas. Justin Fields had a solid game, completing 13-of-21 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown while rushing for another 82 yards and a score. Throwback to the last time the Bears beat the Patriots, which coincidentally happened in Week 7. pic.twitter.com/bOclQcaeKV — 𝕲𝖗𝖎𝖒 𝕮𝖚𝖙𝖙𝖞 (モナンがい 𝕾𝖟𝖓) (@iamcogs) October 22, 2026 Chicago jumped out to a 10-0 lead before New England turned to backup quarterback Bailey Zappe, who briefly sparked the Patriots offense and gave them a 14-10 advantage. That was the last time New England would score. The Bears rattled off 23 unanswered points, rushing for 243 yards while forcing four turnovers, one of which forced by Spider-Man himself, rookie Kyler Gordon. Fields led the way on the ground, while David Montgomery and Khalil Herbert each contributed 62 rushing yards. Cairo Santos added four field goals as Chicago cruised to a 33-14 victory. The win was Chicago’s first in Foxborough and prevented Belichick from passing Halas in front of the franchise he helped build. Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

title: Bears vs. Patriots Game Balls: A Signature Victory
summary: This week’s Thursday Night Football victory for the Chicago Bears over the New England Patriots will go down as one of the team’s signature victories of 2026. The reigning AFC champions came into Soldier Field on a short week and with a long list of injuries. The Bears, though, were also no strangers to the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week’s Thursday Night Football victory for the Chicago Bears over the New England Patriots will go down as one of the team’s signature victories of 2026. The reigning AFC champions came into Soldier Field on a short week and with a long list of injuries. The Bears, though, were also no strangers to the injury report, missing key contributors such as RB Kyle Monangai, DE Dayo Odeyingbo, as well as LB Jack Sanborn and original starting LT Braxton Jones, among others (S Coby Bryant has yet to play this season). Plus, DE Montez Sweat was out for the final game of his two-game suspension. And then there’s QB Caleb Williams, who returned on Sunday from a hamstring injury that he can still be seen favoring at times if you look close enough. But that didn’t stop the team from winning the game from bell to bell, and although things tightened up at the end, the Bears showed once again that they know how to play with a lead. That’s a diversion from last year, when the team’s calling card was coming from behind to win games. Let’s get to this week’s game balls. Offense Game Ball: WR Luther Burden III This award could go to Caleb Williams pretty much every week, and this week was no exception. Williams was terrific once again, but we’re going to look to WR Luther Burden III who had his best game of the young season. Burden was the team’s key target in the first half, and he scored the Bears’ second touchdown of the game when he received a short pass from Williams that he broke into a 24 yard touchdown reception. That touchdown made the score 20-7 with 14 seconds left in the first half. Burden III's speed, the elite blocking 🤌 BEARS SCORE AGAIN. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ozZU6idmRd — NFL (@NFL) October 23, 2026 In addition to his touchdown in the second quarter, Burden also had a 58 yard reception late in the first quarter that was nearly a touchdown. "WIIIIIDE OPEN" Luther Burden III was 11.3 yards away from the nearest defender when this pass arrived for a 58-yard gain, per @NextGenStats 😱 NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7hU4Tg7ptF — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) October 23, 2026 Burden ended the night with four catches for 130 yards, one touchdown, and one run for seven yards. Defense Game Ball: LB D’Marco Jackson Jackson continues to be a heck of a find for the Bears, who claimed the former New Orleans Saint last year off of waivers and saw him work his way up the depth chart due to injuries, elevating his game in the process. He’s become one of the team’s most dependable players on defense. Jackson picked off QB Drake Maye in the end zone, stopping a potential Patriots scoring drive that could have ended up swinging the game. With a touchdown and successful extra point on that drive, the Patriots would have gone up 14-13. It was Maye’s first interception in three weeks. D'Marco Jackson PICKS OFF Maye in the end zone. BEARS BALL. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wq8LKTC3lX — NFL (@NFL) October 23, 2026 Jackson is signed with the Bears through the 2027 season, having signed a two year extension back in March, but the team might want to start thinking about keeping him around even longer. Special Teams Game Ball: K Cairo Santos I went back and forth on this one a little bit. Santos made a clutch 58 yard field goal (his career long) to ice the game toward the end of the fourth quarter, but the reason the team badly needed those points was because Santos had missed a 53 yarder just a few minutes earlier in the fourth quarter. To go up two possessions… DOINK 😭 NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Q3Dxx5y7Io — NFL (@NFL) October 23, 2026 In the end, I felt Santos was deserving due to the fact that his prior miss would have caused a lesser player to shrink under the pressure. But Santos wanted the pressure. In fact, he seemed to relish it. Santos told Bears special teams coach Richard Hightower he was ready to kick the field goal, and head coach Ben Johnson trusted his guy. Right down the middle. Never a doubt. A career-long 58-yard FG from Bears kicker Cairo Santos — and a gutsy decision from HC Ben Johnson. pic.twitter.com/wDNqEVwzxV — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 23, 2026 Who would have received your game balls? Let us know in the comments section below.

title: 5 trade targets for Bears to pursue by the 2026 trade deadline
summary: After their Thursday night win over the Patriots, the Bears now sit with a 5-2 record coming out of Week 7. It’s been a great start for them, having overcome the loss of Caleb Williams for a few weeks to remain firmly in the playoff picture in a loaded NFC. Especially after defeating the reigning […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 20: DeForest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts runs onto the field before an NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs on Sep 20, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After their Thursday night win over the Patriots, the Bears now sit with a 5-2 record coming out of Week 7. It’s been a great start for them, having overcome the loss of Caleb Williams for a few weeks to remain firmly in the playoff picture in a loaded NFC. Especially after defeating the reigning AFC champions, the Bears feel like a team with aspirations for a deep playoff run this season. If they truly want to do so, it could make sense for them to pursue a splash move at the trade deadline, which would likely come on the defensive side of the ball. Which players could make the most sense for the Bears to acquire, though? Who are some notable players at positions of need who could be dealt before the Nov. 10 trade deadline? Here are five defenders that could make sense for Chicago to pursue in the coming weeks. DeForest Buckner, DT, Indianapolis Colts Stylistically, DeForest Buckner doesn’t fit the physical mold that Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen prefers at defensive tackle. Buckner is 6’7”, while none of Chicago’s current defensive tackles are taller than 6’4”. But when you have the chance to acquire one of the best defensive tackles in the NFL from a selling team, you can stand to be more flexible on those measurements. Going into Week 7, Buckner ranks third in the entire NFL with a 93.3 PFN DT Impact grade. He has 4.0 sacks in six games and ranks second among interior defenders with 14.2 disruption EPA. He’s graded as a top-ten player at his position in six of the last seven seasons, and his elite pass-rushing arsenal and quickness off the snap makes him a three-down threat up the middle. It goes without saying that he’d be a massive upgrade for the Bears’ defensive line. Estimated trade value : 2027 second-round pick and 2028 third-round pick Khalil Mack, EDGE, Los Angeles Chargers What a return it would be for the Bears to trade for Khalil Mack eight years after making him one of their biggest blockbuster acquisitions in franchise history. Obviously, Mack wouldn’t cost nearly as much at 35 years old as he did when Chicago got him from the Raiders at 27. That said, he’s still playing at a high level, ranking No. 18 in the league with an 81.1 PFN EDGE Impact grade. Through six games this year, Mack has 3.0 sacks and 19 tackles this season. His 13.1 disruption EPA ranks No. 12 among 122 qualified edge rushers, but it’s going largely unnoticed for an 0-6 Chargers team. Given how far behind Los Angeles is this year, the team could look to sell off some assets to embrace the tank and acquire some future draft capital. Given Mack’s age and production, he clearly doesn’t fit the Chargers’ current state, but he’d be a great fit in the Bears’ defensive line rotation. Estimated trade value: 2027 fifth-round pick Moro Ojomo, DT, Philadelphia Eagles His production has dipped since his stellar 2025 season, but Moro Ojomo still projects as one of the top defenders with an expiring contract at the end of this season. He had 6.0 sacks last year for the Eagles, and though he hasn’t tallied one yet in 2026, he carries an elite athletic profile and is just 25 years old. If the Eagles choose to trade Ojomo, they’d likely look to acquire a late third-round pick in the mix, as that’s roughly the compensatory pick they would receive for letting him walk in free agency. By trading him now, they could receive that third-round pick a year early, further accelerating their rebuild. The Bears could use this opportunity to get an immediate upgrade along the defensive line and get ahead of a potential contract extension for one of the top projected free agents in the 2027 offseason. Estimated trade value: 2027 third-round pick Riq Woolen, CB, Philadelphia Eagles Devan Kaney, the newest Bears reporter for FOX Chicago, recently noted three current Eagles players she thought could be good fits for Chicago in a potential trade . This is particularly notable because Kaney previously served as a sideline reporter for the Eagles. In addition to the aforementioned Ojomo, one player who caught my eye was cornerback Riq Woolen, who signed a one-year, $15 million deal with Philadelphia this offseason. Given the fact that Woolen is only a one-year rental, it would be surprising to see him cost more than a Day 3 draft pick. With a 73.5 PFN CB Impact grade that ranks No. 62 among 102 qualified cornerbacks, he certainly hasn’t been a standout starter this year, but he’s certainly been better than Tyrique Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson, who rank No. 95 and No. 102 in the metric, respectively. It could be worth giving up a Day 3 selection for an upgrade at cornerback for the second half of the season. Estimated trade value: 2027 fifth-round pick or 2028 fourth-round pick Jeffery Simmons, DT, Tennessee Titans Jeffery Simmons is probably the best player on this list, and he also might be the toughest to convince his team to part with. He’s been with the Titans his entire career, and he just signed a three-year extension with them in the 2026 offseason. Tennessee would only free up just over $10 million in 2027 cap space by trading him before the deadline, with the bulk of that financial freedom not coming until 2028 and 2029. But there’s no denying that Simmons, one of the best defensive tackles in the NFL, doesn’t fit the Titans’ current rebuilding status. They have a 1-5 record to start the season, and they finished with 3-14 records in both 2024 and 2025. It doesn’t seem likely they’ll do much better than that in 2026. Simmons is definitely their best player, as he leads the NFL with a 99.8 PFN DT Impact grade, his 16.4 disruption EPA, and tying for first place among defensive tackles with 4.0 sacks. The Bears would have to give up a lot to acquire Simmons, who’s an elite defender in his physical prime. But it could be worth it to have a true superstar up front, and the Titans certainly need more draft capital to build an actual contender for once. Estimated trade value: 2027 first-round pick and 2028 first-round pick

title: 10 Bears Takes: 2 Wins in 5 Days, A QB Battle for the Books, and a 5-2 Start
summary: With quarterback Caleb Williams back in the swing of things, the Chicago Bears turned around on four days’ rest to host Drake Maye and the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football. The defense grabbed the early headlines, but in the end, the offense got the team to the finish line as they take a […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after scoring a 24 yard touchdown against the New England Patriots during the second quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images With quarterback Caleb Williams back in the swing of things, the Chicago Bears turned around on four days’ rest to host Drake Maye and the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football. The defense grabbed the early headlines, but in the end, the offense got the team to the finish line as they take a 5-2 start into a mini-bye week before heading to Seattle to face the Seahawks in Week 8 on Monday Night Football. It’s been a season of ups and downs, but there’s little debate as to how good this team can be with their starting quarterback under center, no matter the opponent. Before we turn the page on another thrilling and high-scoring victory, let’s dive into our 10 Bears Takes for Week 7 following a 30-24 win at Soldier Field. 1. Thursday night featured two of the league’s best young quarterbacks. One team had to lose, but both impressed for the majority of the night under different circumstances. Last year was a breakout for both Williams and Maye, but when all was said and done, only one of them finished neck-and-neck in the MVP race and took their team to the Super Bowl. Even so, you’d be hard-pressed to find many Bears fans who would look back at Williams’ 2025 and have much bad to say about it. Sure, there was the completion percentage talk, but that was a moot point when he was leading comebacks like no other quarterback in the league. 2026 got off to a much different start for both quarterbacks. Maye struggled with turnovers and overall poor play over the first three weeks of the season, while Williams was lost for three games at the end of their Week 2 loss to the Vikings at Soldier Field. Since Maye’s early struggles, he has been a completely different quarterback, and despite an early interception on Thursday night, his gifts were on full display. Williams has hit the ground running since returning from his hamstring strain, and has now turned in back-to-back 300-yard performances. Offense started slow for both teams, but Williams struck first blood with a handful of good drives that led to 10 points. Maye, on the other hand, was struggling to get into a rhythm… Until he wasn’t. Both quarterbacks finished with completion rates over 65%, and both quarterbacks eclipsed the 300-yard mark. Maye’s second-quarter interception was the only turnover from either quarterback, but both 2024 draft classmates were responsible for some big plays down the field. Despite their differences, they also shared plenty of similarities. Pre-game, it was clear both had developed a strong respect for one another, and some of that was because they came up at the same age, etc. Maye is a great athlete in his own right, and even if he doesn’t share the same slipperiness in the pocket as Williams, his ability to evade the pass rush and make plays downfield was on full display on Thursday night. In addition to another good game in the books for Maye, he was down two starting guards and didn’t let that affect him nearly as much as it would for many other quarterbacks. Naturally, these two, along with Jayden Daniels and the rest of the six quarterbacks taken over the first 12 picks of the 2024 first round, will be tirelessly compared. That said, it’s hard to imagine either team came away from that game feeling bad about their situations. Both Maye and Williams have established themselves as plus-starters in the league, and both can elevate themselves into the elite category. Thursday night was just another prime example of how comparing two different quarterbacks isn’t always going to be an apples-for-apples situation. 2. Speaking of quarterback play, the start of Williams’ season could not have gone much better through four games. Despite Williams’ heroics at the end of games and the highlight-reel plays he made last season, the narrative heading into 2026 revolved around his ability to be more accurate and play more in structure. Week 1 was quite the performance, and even if the following week was nothing to write home about before his injury, he still had his team in position to take the lead late in the fourth quarter. Since returning from his Grade 2 hamstring injury, Williams has stacked back-to-back 300-yard performances, totaling three passing touchdowns, and most importantly, no interceptions. In addition to those numbers, he has completed 52-of-69 passes, which has been good for a 75.3% completion rate. It’s clear he’s seeing the field well, and although his sack numbers have elevated from a year ago, he’s still evading pressure at a much higher rate than he’s taking bad sacks. While some– mostly fans from other division rivals– will point out his air yards in Week 6, he’s still making plenty of accurate throws down the field when they are there. On Thursday night, he came up big with multiple throws down the field, but none bigger than his third-down conversion to Rome Odunze backed up at the goal line. Ultimately, it sparked a drive that gave them back a two-score lead in the final two minutes of the game. As Williams gets healthier, his willingness to take off will return, but even with a more conservative approach, he’ll still escape the pocket and make plays with his legs when needed. All around, he’s playing a much calmer, more in-command brand of football than we saw for most of last season. The growth under head coach Ben Johnson has been remarkable, and it’s not a stretch to say that he’s far from a finished product. Although the team went 2-1 in his absence, it’s also clear that for this offense (and team) to reach its ceiling, he must be on the field and playing at a high level. Through four starts, it’s easy to say that he’s done that for the majority of the time, even with a monsoon game in Week 2 that dragged down the offensive numbers as a whole. Williams’ ability to extend plays and throw darts down the field is one thing, but progressively taking more of what the defense gives him on a down-to-down basis and his growing control at the line of scrimmage is where we’ve seen him make the biggest strides so far in 2026. Ultimately, the three games he’s missed will probably be enough to keep him out of serious MVP considerations, but make no mistake about it- Caleb Williams is playing at that high of a level through his first four starts of the season. Even if the defense continues to play the way they have, his ability at quarterback will give them a chance to win, and win big every weekend. 3. The 10-day mini-bye week will be welcome for the Bears, but they must now sift through a few new injuries while potentially getting a few key players back heading into Seattle. It’s hard not to feel emotional after what looked like a serious knee injury suffered by tight end Cole Kmet. Not only is Kmet one of the team’s longest-tenured players, but he’s also been through the (mainly) lows to enjoy the highs this group has experienced over the last two seasons. Beyond being a great ambassador for the team, he’s a much bigger part of the offense than his numbers might suggest. Although the official prognosis has yet to be announced, there’s an ominous feeling around what appeared to be a season-ending knee injury for the seventh-year tight end. In addition to Kmet, fourth-round rookie Malik Muhammad suffered a toe injury, and although the severity of that injury is still unknown, it’s worth noting that he did not return after leaving the game. Like most rookies, it’s been an up-and-down seven-game campaign for Muhammad, but there’s been a lot more good than bad so far in the early going, especially when considering how much has been asked of him as a rookie. It was also reported that linebacker Demarco Jackson was seen in a walking boot postgame. Still, a…

title: Updated: Bears tight end Cole Kmet is out for the season
summary: UPDATED: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed that Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season and will be placed on injured reserve. “I’ve got so much respect for the player that he is, but also the person, the leader,” Johnson said about Kmet via the Score’s Chris Emma. “He’s everything we want […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Cole Kmet #85 of the Chicago Bears is carted off the field after being injured in a play against the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images UPDATED: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed that Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season and will be placed on injured reserve. “I’ve got so much respect for the player that he is, but also the person, the leader,” Johnson said about Kmet via the Score’s Chris Emma. “He’s everything we want to be about here. He’s one of the glue guys. He’s one of the guys that I can count on, whether it’s a messaging standpoint or getting the pulse of the team. He’s going to be sorely missed. Really, he’s Chicago. He’s been here his whole life, and he’s a big part of our heartbeat. So, it stinks, it does, I hate it for him, I hate it for his teammates as well.” When Cole Kmet immediately grabbed his knee after being tackled in last night’s game, I hoped he’d just taken an awkward hit and would walk it off, just as we’ve seen so often during his seven-year Chicago Bears career. Then the cart came out for him, and I hoped it would just be precautionary. But then head coach Ben Johnson met the media after the game and didn’t seem optimistic, saying it didn’t look very good. The Bears have yet to make an official statement, but according to Ian Rapoport , the NFL Insider for ESPN and NFL Network, Kmet is “believed to have suffered a serious, likely season-ending knee injury.” He added that Kmet will undergo more tests this morning and “until those results come back, there is no finality.” I reached out to a source to corroborate Rapoport’s report and was told it’s believed to be a torn ACL. “I don’t have the words to describe what Cole is to me, what Cole is to this team, to this organization,” Caleb Williams said about Kmet in his postgame press conference. “He’s the longest-tenured Bear, I believe. He’s been through it. So, it’s challenging; it’s tough. I’ll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. Cole has been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, the second year, and now through this year. So, I can only do the same for him.” Kmet, drafted with the 43rd overall pick in the 2020 draft, is the longest-tenured Bear, and having grown up in suburban Lake Barrington, Illinois, as a Bears fan, he’s had Navy and Orange in his blood his whole life. Last month, Kmet wrote an article for The Player’s Tribune about his lifelong love of the Bears. I just want to win games and represent for this city, and for this team that I’ve loved since way back when I got that badass Urlacher jersey for Christmas. I want to do all I can to help bring another Lombardi Trophy home to Chicago. And hopefully we can all join together to make that happen this season, because I’d love to see all of you on Michigan Avenue for a big parade this winter if everything goes our way. Kmet did a lot of the little things on the football field to help the Bears win games, so his contributions will definitely be missed, but what he brings to the locker room as a team leader will be missed as well.

title: Bears vs. Patriots: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and 300 passing yards
summary: The scoreboard says it was a six-point game, and there were several moments when it felt like the New England Patriots were about to come back, but the Chicago Bears led this one wire to wire. It wasn’t a clean game by Chicago, but they made big plays when they needed them and won 30 […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after defeating the New England Patriots in the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The scoreboard says it was a six-point game, and there were several moments when it felt like the New England Patriots were about to come back, but the Chicago Bears led this one wire to wire. It wasn’t a clean game by Chicago, but they made big plays when they needed them and won 30 to 24 against a very good Patriots squad. The overall numbers were relatively close, but the Bears had the edge in a few critical categories. Chicago had the game’s only turnover, picking off New England’s Drake Maye in the end zone. The Bears converted both of their 4th-down attempts, while the Pats were stopped on their only try. The Bears did have more yards (405 to 380), more first downs (21 to 20), ran more plays (66 to 50), and had a better third-down conversion rate (33.3% to 28.6%). Both teams were hit with their fair share of penalties, with the Patriots flagged 10 times for 71 yards and the Bears hit with 9 for 69. The time of possession for the game wasn’t as lopsided as the Bears are used to (32:24 to 27:36), but in the fourth quarter Chicago held the ball for 12 minutes and 21 seconds. It was just two long drives with methodical precision, aided by a couple of huge third-down conversions from Caleb Williams to Rome Odunze, and a fourth-down conversion on a pass to Colston Loveland. Their first fourth-quarter drive ended when Cairo Santos’ 53-yard field goal doinked, but Santos redeemed himself with a career-long 58-yarder on the final drive. More on that further down the page. Let’s look at the Bears’ playing-time breakdown and a few individual stats from the game. OFFENSE Caleb Williams has thrown for 300+ yards in two straight games, something he’s done for the first time in his career. He’s the first Bear to have two in a row since Mitch Trubisky had three straight in 2018, and he’s the first quarterback this season with consecutive 300-yard passing games with no interceptions. He’s now up to seven 300-yard games in his career, tying him for third most in Bears history. Here’s the full list with games played in parentheses. Jay Cutler – 16 (102) Billy Wade – 9 (59) Caleb Williams – 7 (38) Mitch Trubisky – 7 (51) Erik Kramer – 7 (49) Speaking of Billy Wade, Caleb’s back-to-back 300+ yard games in wins mark only the third time this has happened in franchise history, joining Wade in 1962 and Sid Luckman in 1947. I’ve got one more 300-yard nugget for you: he also extended his own team record for most 300-yard passing games with no interceptions to 6. His only 300-yard day with an interception came in the third game of his career (9/22/24), when he threw for 363 yards, 2 TDs, and 2 INTs. DEFENSE Drake Maye has been on a heater the last three games, but the Bears rattled him a bit early. He settled in and finished with 321 passing yards and 2 touchdowns, plus 26 rushing yards and a TD. The Bears held the Patriots’ running backs to 44 yards on 13 carries. Kyler Gordon’s ramp-up is going well so far; he played 26 total snaps in Atlanta and 35 last night. He’s now at 4 sacks, tying him for the team lead. In case you were wondering, Chicago’s record for sacks by a defensive back is 7, set by Dave Duerson in 1986. Gordon is up to 5 tackles for loss this season, which is also tied for the team lead. Jamree Kromah made his career debut a week ago but was held without a stat, so it’s good to see him scratch the stat sheet this week. Daniel Hardy picked up his first career sack last week, then added a half sack against the Patriots. But more importantly, his Jeff Hardy sack celly is a thing. SPECIAL TEAMS* *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos wanted to redeem himself after that doink, and when he heard Ben Johnson on the headset ask special teams coordinator Richard Hightower if Cairo wanted to try the 58-yarder, he said yes. Check out this quick clip of Santos describing the moment. Cairo Santos said Ben Johnson initially called for a punt but an injury timeout gave them more time to talk it over. Santos was confident he could make a 58-yarder to essentially seal the win, and he told his coach that. pic.twitter.com/ipywfFqqTm — Sean Hammond (@sean_hammond) October 23, 2026 Santos was 3-for-4 on field goals and hit all 3 extra points. Tory Taylor punted twice, averaging 53.5 (44.0 net). Rome Odunze recovered the onside kick. Zavion Thomas returned 3 kicks for 92 yards. Kalif Raymond had 1 punt return for 7 yards. Dillon Thieneman and Daniel Hardy had 2 tackles each on special teams. Practice squad call-up Buddy Johnson had 3 tackles. To check out the complete Bears vs. Patriots box score, I find ESPN’s site is easy to navigate. All statistics and snap counts, as well as the accompanying pictures, are taken directly from the NFL’s Game Statistic and Information System.

title: Bears send a message to the NFL with the win over Patriots
summary: The Chicago Bears got the job done on Thursday night, defeating the New England Patriots 30-24 to improve their record to 5-2 for the season. It was a particularly strong performance from their offense, as Caleb Williams threw for 308 yards and two passing touchdowns in the victory. In the four games that Williams has […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a touchdown against the New England Patriots during the third quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears got the job done on Thursday night, defeating the New England Patriots 30-24 to improve their record to 5-2 for the season. It was a particularly strong performance from their offense, as Caleb Williams threw for 308 yards and two passing touchdowns in the victory. In the four games that Williams has played, the Bears are 3-1. In the three of those games that weren’t played in the pouring rain, the Bears are 3-0. We haven’t seen much of this team at full strength, but when they have been there, the results have been extremely promising. Even with a short week against a tough opponent, the Bears were able to pick up the win, and they now have a few extra days of rest leading into their Week 8 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks. For this week, though, these are some of my takeaways from the game. Another high-powered offensive performance Going back to the “when Caleb Williams is healthy” bit, the Bears are now averaging 40.0 points per game in the three healthy, non-monsoon games that he has played in 2026. Granted, that’s partially swayed by the Panthers game in which the offense put up 59 points, but Chicago is still coming off of consecutive games in which its offense scored 30 or more points, as well as consecutive games in which Williams threw for over 300 yards with multiple touchdowns and no interceptions. It feels weird to say, but it feels like the Bears genuinely have an elite quarterback. After Thursday night, Williams ranks No. 4 in the entire NFL with an 84.2 PFN QB Impact grade. He’s surrounded by one of the brightest offensive minds in football, and he has plenty of talent on the offensive line and in the skill positions surrounding him. Against a solid defense in the Patriots, the Bears were incredibly effective. Thursday was just another instance of this team showing why it has one of the best offenses in the game. The Jaylon Johnson conversation Involving personal bias, it hurts to talk about Jaylon Johnson in a negative light. He was a rare bright spot on so many bad Bears teams, and he’s finally getting the chance to experience team success with the organization that drafted him back in 2020. By all accounts, he seems like a great guy. That said, his performance so far in 2026 is unacceptable for the massive salary he’s currently making. So far this year, Johnson is allowing a targeted completion percentage of 71.4% and a targeted passer rating of 113.1 for the Bears. He looks a step slower coming out of his breaks than what we saw from him in his All-Pro campaign in 2023, as well as his Pro Bowl season in 2024. Additionally, he had two major whiffs as a tackler against the Patriots, including the last-second receiving touchdown by Rhamondre Stevenson, which saw him waltz into the end zone thanks to passive coverage by Chicago’s secondary and bad tackling by multiple players, including Johnson. Unless he can bounce back to his prior form, it’s starting to feel like the beginning of the end of his time with the team. The ceiling of this Bears team Negativity around that one subject aside, this was a massive win for the Bears. The Patriots were a red-hot team who had won three games in a row going into Week 7, and Chicago managed to shut them down and pick up the win. Now sitting at 5-2, this group is well-positioned for a playoff push and contention for first place in the NFC North, even with how talented the division is currently. The Bears’ offense is operating at an incredibly high level. Their defense is manufacturing pressure up front with creative blitz looks and is still generating turnovers. I think it would really benefit the team to pursue a trade for a top defender before the 2026 trade deadline, as weaknesses at defensive tackle and cornerback still stand out. Even so, this Bears team is one that has proven it can take on top competition and be victorious. They could be a dark horse to make a deep playoff push when it’s all said and done.

title: 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Ravens
summary: The 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Baltimore to face the 4-2 Ravens. This is a rare 1:00 p.m. ET game when facing Baltimore on the road. Can the Bengals pull out a crucial divisional victory, or will they drop to 0-2 in AFC North games to start the season? Let’s take a look at […]
full_text: The 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Baltimore to face the 4-2 Ravens . This is a rare 1:00 p.m. ET game when facing Baltimore on the road. Can the Bengals pull out a crucial divisional victory, or will they drop to 0-2 in AFC North games to start the season? Let’s take a look at some of the key matchups for the game this upcoming Sunday, which includes a matchup that we saw at Bengals training camp previously throughout the years. Trey Hendrickson vs. Orlando Brown Jr. We all remember the Trey Hendrickson vs. Orlando Brown Jr. scuffle from training camp back in 2023. Hendrickson had claw marks on his neck after the two got into it. They will get to carry that over to a real game this week. Hendrickson is coming off of a game with six pressures and a sack against Cleveland. He has been dealing with a hand injury for most of the season, but is likely fired up to face his former team this week. Meanwhile, Brown Jr. had arguably his best game of the season against Miami a couple of weeks ago. He allowed just one pressure and 0 sacks. I imagine the Bengals will also look to give Brown some additional help with chips from tight ends and running back throughout this one. Vega Ioane vs. Dexter Lawrence Cam Jurgens could be making his debut at center for the Ravens this week, after dealing with a concussion. If he does, he will also get a heavy dose of Dexter Lawrence to deal with. If there is a healthy Jurgens, we will see talented rookie Ioane facing Lawrence from his guard position. Either way, we’ll see Ioane take on powerhouse Dexter Lawrence on the interior this week. The 6’4”, 328-pound rookie from Penn State has been one of the better linemen for the Ravens this year. He has shown his versatility by logging 3 starts each at right guard and center for Baltimore. Lawrence has been a havoc creator all season long for Cincinnati. He has 19 pressures, 3 sacks, and has just been a dominating presence on the interior of the defensive line. Dexter Lawrence vs. Miami Lawrence was fantastic again on Sunday, recording 4 pressures and 4 run stops during the game. He has 3 or more pressures in all 5 games this season for the Bengals pic.twitter.com/l53QcsObYs — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 Zay Flowers vs. Dax Hill Flowers has been the go-to guy for both Lamar Jackson and Snoop Huntley so far this season for the Ravens. In 5 games played, Flowers has 471 receiving yards. He also has an additional 3 carries for 34 yards this year. The Bengals will have to watch out for him not just as a receiver, but on jet screens. Flowers is a big play waiting to happen, and the Bengals will have to keep him in check if they want to win this game. The main player who will be tasked with doing so is Dax Hill. Hill has played his best two games of the season since moving back inside to the slot after Jalen Davis went to IR. Hill has allowed just 28 total yards in those two games combined. If he can put together another performance like that against Flowers, there will be a lot more buzz about how good he is playing in the slot. Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins vs. Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase The Ravens secondary has been a weakness in years past. This year they are closer to the middle of the pack in this area. Through 6 games, the Ravens as a team are 13th in passing yards allowed. The two guys on the outside are a reason for a lot of that improvement. The veteran Humphrey has a 74.4 coverage grade this season. Last year that number was a career-worst 43.8. In his 10th season in the league, Humphrey appears to be playing at a very high level. Meanwhile, third-year corner Nate Wiggins is playing solid football of his own. He has a 68.8 coverage grade this year. Both guys will have their toughest test of the season going against Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Chase has 27 receptions, 289 yards, and 4 touchdowns through his first 5 games of the season. Those numbers would be even higher if he wasn’t knocked out of the game with a concussion before halftime of the Jaguars game. Tee Higgins also has 27 receptions this year. He has just 1 receiving touchdown, but he does have a team-leading 423 yards through 5 games played. While the Ravens cornerback duo is playing at a high level, I still give a sound advantage to Chase and Higgins. These should be entertaining matchups all day long on Sunday. Tee Higgins is the Bengals leading receiver in yardage with 154 through two games. He is averaging 19.3 yards per catch, but it really hasn’t been on the normal contested catch jump balls we know he can win yet. Higgins could be in line for a monster game versus the Steelers this… pic.twitter.com/cujEC8c4Ki — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 25, 2026

full_text: Cincinnati Bengals star receiver Ja’Marr Chase has had his fair share of success against the Baltimore Ravens. Heading into Sunday’s matchup, Chase has played the Ravens 10 total times in his career. In those games, he has racked up 75 receptions, 1,204 yards, and eight touchdowns. That’s a decent season’s worth of work for some receivers, and Chase has done it in just 10 games. Baltimore’s secondary is certainly aware of Chase’s success against them, and when speaking to the media Thursday, Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey had an… interesting take on lining up across from “Uno.” Marlon Humphrey on Ja’Marr Chase: “It would be cool if I didn’t match up with him so much.” — Jeff Zrebiec (@jeffzrebiec) October 22, 2026 I mean, at least he was honest? Typically, you see cornerbacks and receivers talking trash about getting the better of one another, but Humphrey seems to hope Chase is someone else’s problem. If the Bengals are going to get their first AFC North win of the season, Chase having one of his classic breakout performances against Baltimore would go a long way. Chase is off to the slowest start in terms of receiving yards of his career and is yet to hit 100 yards receiving in a game this season. Humphrey doesn’t seem too interested in trying to stop that from happening. Each player listed has put together successful young careers for the Bengals, but Turner has been a level higher so far in Cincinnati. title: Trey Hendrickson trying to downplay his first game vs. the Bengals

While he’s trying to downplay the matchup against the Bengals, the reality is he can’t. “We’re a team. This isn’t an individual […]
full_text: It’s becoming more than an undercard in Sunday’s AFC North showdown. Trey Hendrickson will be facing his former team for the first time when the Bengals play in Baltimore against the Ravens Sunday afternoon. While he’s trying to downplay the matchup against the Bengals, the reality is he can’t. “We’re a team. This isn’t an individual sport,” Hendrickson said this week. “It’s about the team and what I can bring and what they can bring, and what we can collectively do as a unit. I think that’s what makes football special, and I’m looking forward to it Sunday.” You can hear it in the tone of the Bengals’ players and head coach Zac Taylor when they’ve been asked about Trey Hendrickson. They’re ready to move on and focus on who’s on the field for them. While Hendrickson has 83 sacks in his career, now in his 10th season, he hasn’t sacked Joe Burrow. Hopefully, that doesn’t happen on Sunday. But this is a major storyline going into Sunday’s game, with Hendrickson facing the Bengals for the first time since walking in free agency in March. After all the drama between the All-Pro edge rusher and the Bengals, the Bengals want to show they were correct to move on and commit that money to different players like Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence, and Jonathan Allen. summary: As the Cleveland Browns get ready to travel to Nashville to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season, the top of the AFC North continues to belong to the orange and brown. Injuries, including DT Mike Hall Jr. being out this week, continue to be a big variable for the […]
full_text: As the Cleveland Browns get ready to travel to Nashville to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season, the top of the AFC North continues to belong to the orange and brown . Injuries, including DT Mike Hall Jr. being out this week , continue to be a big variable for the Browns and their opponents . All the positivity heading into Week 7 wasn’t as strong if we look back to when Hall, along with DT Mason Graham , were injured in Week 4 versus the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football. Graham is expected to return in Week 7 after getting injured early in Week 4 and being ruled out after halftime. Just before the intermission, Hall injured his ankle, was helped off the field, and then carted into the locker room. Cleveland (and Pittsburgh) fans know what happened next for the former Ohio State defensive lineman: The Browns defense pick up their 4th sack of the night! @PITvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/IGODY4j1OS — NFL (@NFL) October 2, 2026 Hall later said he knew his teammates needed him with Graham out for the game. From being carted off the field to exploding for a huge third-down sack that pushed the Steelers out of field goal range, Hall’s impact was appreciated after a game where the score (27-24) might have been decided, partially, by his return and big sack. Since that game, Hall is set to miss his third straight contest. While that may be frustrating to some Browns fans, it also puts his Week 4 return into context. Running off of adrenaline and knowing what his teammates needed, Hall not only returned to the field but made a huge impact, while dealing with an ankle injury that will have needed a month off, at least, between games played. Three weeks later, it is clear that Hall’s ankle injury was and is significant. That adds even more respect to his Week 4 return and play. Join the conversation! title: NFL Week 7: 3 other games for Browns fans to keep an eye on
summary: The Cleveland Browns face off against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 of the NFL season, with a win moving the visitors to 5-2 and a loss calling their early-season success into question. Injuries mean that any Saturday news from the Browns will be analyzed and scrutinized, including whether RB Dylan Sampson is activated from […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns face off against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 of the NFL season, with a win moving the visitors to 5-2 and a loss calling their early-season success into question . Injuries mean that any Saturday news from the Browns will be analyzed and scrutinized, including whether RB Dylan Sampson is activated from injured reserve. The bigger questions will be about practice squad elevations on defense, with CB Denzel Ward and LB Quincy Williams questionable for the game . With Cleveland sitting at the top of the AFC North and fourth in the AFC playoff picture , there are a couple of games of importance going on around the league that they’ll want to watch. Two of the teams ahead of them in the playoff seeding, the Buffalo Bills (2nd seed) and Jacksonville Jaguars (3rd seed), have their byes this week, which limits the games of interest. With the Los Angeles Rams owing the Browns their first-round pick in the 2027 NFL draft, “Rams Watch” is on every week, especially with injuries piling up and WR Puka Nacua questionable for Week 7 . With two AFC North teams facing off this week, that leaves just three vital games for Cleveland fans, besides their own, to watch in Week 7: Steelers vs. Saints in Paris, early Sunday kickoff The first game on Sunday, kicking off at 9:30 AM on NFL Network, is important for Browns fans for two reasons. First and obvious, the Pittsburgh Steelers are part of the AFC North and are tied for the best record in the division. Second, the Steelers and New Orleans Saints are Cleveland’s next two opponents . The result of the game will be important, but watching to see how Pittsburgh’s energy is and any injuries coming during an international game could be a big deal for Week 8’s AFC North matchup. Last year, the Browns traveled to London the week before having to face the Steelers and looked lethargic after the long travel. The only difference this year is that Paris is a little further away than London, and Pittsburgh gets to play at home the next week, whereas Cleveland had to go on the road. Bengals vs. Ravens at 1 PM At the same time the Browns are playing, a pretty big matchup between the Cincinnati Bengals and Baltimore Ravens will be going on. The Bengals are in last place in the AFC North, at 3-2, and go on the road to face the Ravens, who should be getting QB Lamar Jackson back . Too early in the season for tiebreaker conversations; instead, fans will be rooting for a very physical game on the field. Ramvs vs. Raiders at 4:25 PM Los Angeles could have Nacua playing this week, but his injury flaring up during practice calls that into question, along with the team having to go on the road. DE Myles Garrett could start practicing soon, but will have at least a week or two before he’s likely to play once he begins that process. A loss in Week 7 would drop the Rams to 2-5 and potentially lead to Los Angeles selling heading into the NFL trade deadline. Given some of the matchups this week, the Rams could be slotted to send the Browns a Top 8 pick by the time this week’s slate of games is over. Given that the Jaguars and Bills are on byes this week, a Cleveland win would slide them up to the third seed for now (5-2 gets the nod over JAX at 4-2). Checking in on the Steelers and Saints while getting your breakfast and game-day spread will have you more prepared for the Browns Week 8 and 9 matchups, while “OctoBox” users on YouTube will probably want to have Bengals vs. Ravens available at 1 PM as well. The chance for Los Angeles to lose again and have their season continue to head in a negative direction would just be icing on the cake for Cleveland fans in Week 7. title: NFL predictions: With the defense cooking, will the Browns-Titans matchup be put to bed early?
summary: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (4-2) take on the Tennessee Titans (1-5). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. Browns’ Defense is Cooking… …except for the start of football games. In four of their six games, including their last three […]
full_text: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (4-2) take on the Tennessee Titans (1-5). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. Browns’ Defense is Cooking… …except for the start of football games. In four of their six games, including their last three games, this has been the result of the opposing team’s opening drive: Week 1, Jaguars: 8 plays, 59 yards (Touchdown) Week 4, Steelers: 17 plays, 73 yards (Touchdown) Week 5, Jets: 8 plays, 90 yards (Touchdown) Week 6, Ravens: 11 plays, 66 yards (Touchdown) In that first game, the defense was just bad the whole first half. In the other three games, they did a pretty solid-to-dominant job the rest of the way. I’ve harped a bunch of times this season on how much I value the adjustments that Mike Rutenburg has this defense making in-game, which is something I thought I never saw from Jim Schwartz . We’re also seeing where a defensive front is not reliant on one guy ( Myles Garrett ) to save the day. Players are collectively stepping up and rallying together, and you’re also seeing great individual efforts out of the likes of Denzel Ward , Carson Schewesinger , and Maliek Collins . This week, the Browns get Mason Graham back, who looked like a beast to begin his second year before hurting his knee. With the defense playing so well, it’s also encouraging this week that they are facing the 32nd-ranked offense in the NFL. Cam Ward hasn’t been able to muster much in the passing game. Also last year, RB Tony Pollard had his best game of the season against Cleveland, going off for 161 yards on 25 carries with 2 touchdowns. Hopefully, that element can be contained, especially with help returning at defensive tackle. But the Offense Needs to do More The fourth quarter, game-winning drives have happened four times this season, which is great on one hand. It almost happened a fifth time (the loss to the Jets). On the other hand, we’re starting to reach a bit of a tipping point on needing to see more productivity and points on the board in the rest of the game. Over those first few games of the season, the feeling was, ‘Alright, we’re seeing some encouraging things, maybe as the offense continues to build a rhythm, we’ll see better results.’ Instead, things have gotten pretty stagnant from an overall game perspective. Cleveland has scored 12 and 13 points in their last two games, fortunate to have gone 1-1 during that stretch. Over the last three weeks, Cleveland is the only team to have a victory on the board after scoring that few of points. The last team that won with that low of a point total was the Giants back in Week 3, when they won 12-7 over…the Titans. In other words, Cleveland was lucky to scoot by with a victory in that sense last week, and if their offense is not better, even against the Titans, you’re going to have teams beating you. What can get better? Last week, one of the adjustments seems to have been getting Jerry Jeudy more involved in the game again. The running game also showed some progress, but ironically enough, many fans feel that was because Quinshon Judkins was out, and Jaleel McLaughlin was back. I’m not trying to be a Judkins hater by any means — like I’ve said multiple times, I thought he looked very sharp last year, and this year, I think he looks as pedestrian as you can get. Dylan Sampson might also return this week. Something is off that KC Concepcion is six games in, and has 186 yards receiving (average of 31 yards receiving per game). I go back to what I saw from him in training camp, and I know that was just training camp, but my takeaway multiple times was, ‘ This guy is something special.’ And it’s also not like I say that about every receiver that comes through the team because I’m a homer. I don’t think I’ve ever felt that about a receiver in camp. And during the regular season, I think he’s looked the part still — it’s just, tying in with the rest of the offense, the production isn’t there yet. Harold Fannin , also, has 2 catches for 13 yards in the last two games. The Titans have defended tight ends fairly well this year, so I don’t know if there’s a breakout to be expected this week, but the young tight end needs to get involved more. Tennessee picked up their first win of the season last week, but their offense didn’t find themselves. They were shut out 13-0 at the half, then forced a fumble, got an interception (which both led to field goals), and then blocked a punt for a touchdown, to generate points. That should be a talking point for the Browns this week, but if they protect the ball and are diligent about special teams assignments like they’ve been, Tennessee’s offense shouldn’t beat them. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 1.5 point favorites against the Titans. The over/under is 37.5. Quick Hitters Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer was asked about getting his top two running backs returning this week: Yeah, it’s huge. I mean, it’s obviously our top two backs. So, yeah, those two are a big part of what we do on offense, run and pass. And they’re also, we talked about this last week too, a little bit of a one-two punch, if you will, whatever you want to call it. They have different skill sets that we can utilize for both of them. So, yeah, having those guys back is going to be huge. Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg talked about Emmanuel McNeil-Warren getting a lot of action last week after Grant Delpit exited early: I mean, he did a great job in the game. Was excellent with his communication, was excellent with his assignments, and then you saw his playmaking ability come to life. But that goes back to him continuing to build his confidence. You saw it earlier in the year on special teams, playing really, really well on special teams, getting more opportunities on defense, playing really well in practice, and him transferring that to the game. And he’s going to continue going this way because of, number one, just who he is. He wants to be coached, he wants the information, he wants to be challenged, he wants to be told when it’s good, when it’s bad. And then you can see his play continuing to rise because of who he is. Special teams coordinator Bryon Storer was asked about Corey Bojorquez not having his best game last week: “Yeah, I mean, we didn’t think it was, he could have…He had more opportunities that he could have taken advantage of. It’s the minus, the two minus-45 kicks, where you’re like, we’ve got to have those balls inside the 20-yard line. And that’s what I told him after the game, looking at it, it’s like, ‘we’ve got to get the ball inside the 20 on those’, because if you get the ball inside the 20 on those, you’ve got four inside the 20 for the game. And you only gave up, I think it was like 7.5 yards per return, and so if you handled those punts better, you’re looking at the game completely differently. But we talked about it, and really just trying to keep the ball from going out of bounds so early, because you leave it up to the official to mark wherever he thinks it goes out. Now, I think there is some technology to it now that we learned, but he’s got to do a better job of keeping it in play. And we’ve proven now with Malachi (Corley) that we can down the punt inside the 10-yard line. So, I think we learned from that and we’ll see improvement from us.” Here are predictions from multiple staff members at DBN: Predictions Chris Pokorny: “Many are predicting this to be a close game, with Cleveland squeaking out a win. I can’t blame them, considering the Browns’ four victories have been by a combined 13 points. But with the momentum the Browns continue to build, I feel like their defense is rocking with confidence this week, and the offense finds a slight groove to make this a double digit win.” Browns 27, Titans 10 Jared Mueller : “A road game with a bit of weird attached to it with the Jordan Elliott release from the Titans and his history with the…

title: Should the Browns trade Jerry Jeudy? Our panel weighs in and is not unanimous
summary: The Cleveland Browns find themselves in unknown territory at the top of the AFC North Division. The view is quite good. From one spot, you can actually see four states. And what are all these white, fluffy things that keep floating by? Someone mentioned, maybe clouds? RELATED: JEUDY “FITS THE BILL” AS A TRADE TARGET  […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns find themselves in unknown territory at the top of the AFC North Division. The view is quite good. From one spot, you can actually see four states. And what are all these white, fluffy things that keep floating by? Someone mentioned, maybe clouds? RELATED: JEUDY “FITS THE BILL” AS A TRADE TARGET The Browns are having a great season and are winning games in the last portion of the fourth quarter. Kardiac Kids 2.0? We prefer a different moniker for a completely different team and era. Myocardial Vascular Adolescents. And as games fall off the calendar, various media outlets, Facebook fan pages, and some in the Cleveland fanbase have made a bold suggestion: The Browns should trade WR Jerry Jeudy. Jeudy is a roller coaster. He will disappear in games, and then catch two balls in clutch situations. We have all seen this. Would Cleveland have beaten the Baltimore Ravens last weekend if Jeudy didn’t snare that 33-yard pass from QB Deshaun Watson on a third-and-five that ended up on Baltimore’s 29-yard line with 42 seconds remaining? What about the 17-yard and 10-yard passes he caught on Cleveland’s final drive that ended with a 56-yard Andre Szmyt field goal to defeat the Pittsburgh Steelers? The NFL trade deadline is still weeks away on November 10, 4:00 (Eastern). But already, WR Marv Harrison, QB J.J. McCarthy, C Cam Jurgens, and CB Joey Porter, Jr. have been shipped off to new homes. Is Jeudy next? Jeudy has one more year on the three-year, $58 million contract extension ($41 million guaranteed) he signed after being traded to the Browns from the Denver Broncos in 2024. He balled out in his first season with Cleveland, gaining 1,229 yards and making the Pro Bowl. He tanked his second year, with his production cut in half. And now? He has played in all six games with three starts, has 19 targets, 12 receptions for 150 yards, zero TDs, nine first-down conversions, a 12.5 average per reception, 39 YAC, and zero drops. Here at DBN , we have assembled some folks who are in the business of covering and discussing the Browns. Trade Jeudy, or keep him? Here’s their take. Kenny “Mac” MacDonald President: Ottawa (Canada) Browns Backers Co-host: The Dawgs Podcast LINK: OTTAWA BROWNS BACKERS LINK: THE DAWGS PODCAST KEEP JEUDY Should the Browns trade Jerry Jeudy? No—keep him and build on what’s working. Jerry Jeudy needs to remain a Cleveland Brown. Going back to training camp, there were already Browns fans and pundits looking at Jeudy as a veteran the team should trade. I understood the conversation, especially with younger receivers coming in. But having promising young players does not automatically make an experienced receiver expendable. As Browns fans, years of rebuilding have conditioned us to look ahead to the next draft pick. Eventually, we need to put that same emphasis on consistently winning football games. We cannot keep moving experienced players and assuming the next group will immediately replace everything they bring. Anyone who plays fantasy football knows how quickly injuries can wreck a roster. Depth looks expendable right up until you need it. Why give that away when the return might not adequately replace its value? I’m not going to lie: Jeudy’s performance against Baltimore strengthened my opinion. He caught four passes for 69 yards, including the 33-yard reception that helped set up the winning field goal. That is a contribution to winning right now. The younger receivers may eventually take over, but there is value in having someone alongside them who has been there and done it. Their development and Jeudy’s contribution can happen at the same time. We do not have to choose between helping the young guys grow and keeping an experienced weapon. I know plenty has been said about his demeanor, and I don’t always like his body language either. But frustration does not automatically mean a player has checked out. Before judging him, we should also consider his opportunities and how the offense is using him. Getting more out of the passing game is a shared responsibility. His reaction to receiving the game ball mattered to me, too. I saw a player excited to contribute and celebrate with his teammates. To me, that looked like someone who is bought in. That belongs in the conversation alongside his statistics and contract. I would consider a trade if Cleveland had a clear surplus of dependable receivers or if Jeudy personally requested a move. Right now, I don’t see enough reason to give up that experience and depth for the sake of adding another draft pick. Keep him. Keep building his role. We have spent enough time talking about future assets. I want to see the Browns turn the talent they already have into consistent wins, and Jerry Jeudy can help them do that. EZ Weav DBN Staff KEEP JEUDY In 2025, Jerry Jeudy had the chance to showcase himself as a primary target in our offense. Of course, the performance of the quarterback position all throughout 2025 was…challenging. No doubt that colors how one should judge his statistical accomplishments in terms of considering trading for him. However, as Browns fans are well aware, it was more than just a lack of production – he had a big problem hauling in passes and was pretty well plagued with drops, which would be the exact opposite of the thing you’d want to trade for. Now certainly he’s not without talent; he’s a crisp route runner and often can get plenty of separation. But with the aforementioned, you’re not likely to garner much for him considering his contract ($17.5m/year). The Panthers moved up from the sixth round to the fifth round for WR Dionte Johnson in 2025, and the Jaguars gave up a seventh-rounder to get WR Christian Kirk. These are receivers who are roughly comparable to Jeudy in terms of contract/production, so we probably can’t exactly expect a major haul, unless we find a partner that wildly deviates from this precedent. Moreover, with the additions of receivers Denzel Boston and K.C. Concepcion in 2026, Jeudy now doesn’t have to assume the role of primary target-bearer. And in the limited opportunities he’s been called upon this year, he’s been fairly reliable. Would that some of those targets last week had gone to him instead of Isaiah Bond, but I digress. At that point, the only real impetus to move him would be either because we need to immediately clear cap space (which we don’t) or in order to clear room for some promising WR prospect we’ve got on the roster (which we also don’t). Why bother moving a guy that’s currently serving a complementary role when the compensation is nil and the replacement options bleak? That said, if it’s something like what the Steelers got for Johnson earlier in 2025 (CB Donte Jackson and a 6-7 pick swap were on the table) – and not necessarily at CB but just a competent, veteran player that can fill a role, then I might be down. Don’t expect that to be the case, though, so I say keep him and have him help take some of the attention off our stud rookies, as we try to win some games out here. Glenn Bam Caudill DBN Regular KEEP JEUDY Keep Jerry Jeudy (JJ). Before examining every factor involved, I have been saying trade JJ. Since Kevin Concepcion Jr and Denzel Boston have taken the starting jobs, reducing the amount of time JJ is on the field, one has to ask what a trade would look like. Factors such as value, depth, cost, and the locker room come into play. He is said to be a good blocking receiver, and we have never heard of any drama he caused. The Browns often have depth issues on the team, but they also have receivers Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley. It’s tough to know if this team can make the playoffs this year with a weaker schedule that they have. If you were confident of a playoff berth and a deep run into the playoffs, JJ would be a perfect depth piece. I felt like he had a high drop rate as a Brown. This is where you are not counting how many drops he has had, but how often he has dropped one. Jerry Jeudy (JJ) had…

summary: The Cleveland Browns will look to pick up their second road win of the season on Sunday when they head to Music City to take on the Tennessee Titans. full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns will look to pick up their second road win of the season on Sunday when they head to Music City to take on the Tennessee Titans. Cleveland is coming off its latest fourth-quarter comeback, their fourth of the season, as they beat the Baltimore Ravens and move into first place in the AFC North Division. Meanwhile, the Titans finally opened their account last week, picking up their first win of the 2026 season in a victory over their divisional rival, the Indianapolis Colts. The Browns continue to find ways to win in the fourth quarter while waiting for the offense to play a complete game. Getting things in gear this week, with a visit to Pittsburgh coming up next week, would seem like a good idea. It’s the Browns vs. the Titans in a contest that harkens back to the days of the AFC Central Division, and here is everything to know about the game. Game Info Records: Cleveland is 4-2. Tennessee is 1-5. Kickoff: 1 p.m. Stadium: Nissan Stadium, Nashville, Tenn. TV: CBS Announcers: Andrew Catalon, Logan Ryan and AJ Ross (sideline reporter) Radio: 850 ESPN Cleveland, 92.3 The Fan WKRK, 98.5 WNCX, 1300 AM La Mega (Español) Announcers: Andrew Siciliano, Nathan Zegura, and Je’Rod Cherry (sidelines) Last meeting: The Titans won the last meeting, 31-29, in Week 14 of the 2025 season. First meeting: The Browns won the first meeting, 28-14, on November 22, 1970. All-time series: Cleveland leads the all-time series, 37-33. The Browns have split the past four road games against the Titans. Weather: 75 degrees and sunny, with no chance of rain. Wind from the north/northeast at 2 mph. ( weather.com ) new road combo 🛣️ @RiddellSports | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/jSUHyDbAwh — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 22, 2026 Uniform: Tennessee changed its uniform this season to a shade of blue that links the franchise to its days as the Houston Oilers. That sets up what could be a nice, old-school uniform matchup. So, naturally, the Browns decide to mess it up by wearing their awful brown pants with their clean white jersey. Injury report: Browns – Out: Defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), right guard Teven Jenkins (knee), quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back), and defensive tackle Kalia Davis (quad). Questionable: Cornerback Denzel Ward (hand), linebacker Quincy Williams (neck), safety Grant Delpit (concussion), and running back Dylan Sampson (knee). Titans – Questionable: Safety Tony Adams (ankle), linebacker Dorian Mausi (foot), wide receiver Calvin Ridley (hip), running back Tyjae Spears (knee), and safety Kevin Winston Jr. (quad). The line: Browns -1.5 points, with an over/under of 37.5 points, per FanDuel . Carson's a dawg day in and day out pic.twitter.com/QCXpail7l4 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 22, 2026 News & Notes The Titans are No. 32 in passing yards at 153.5 yards per game. Tennessee defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons has four sacks and six tackles for loss on the season. He is joined by defensive ends John Franklin-Myers (1.5 sacks, 3.5 tackles for loss), and Jermaine Johnson II (three sacks, four tackles for loss). Simmons (46.5 career sacks) needs two more sacks to move past Robert Brazile for ninth-place on the franchise’s all-time list. The Browns rank No. 24 in rushing offense at 94 yards per game. Cleveland is averaging 17.7 points per game, which currently ranks No. 28 in the league. In 2025, the Browns averaged 16.4 points per game. The Browns have scored just 43 points in the first halves of games this season. Tennessee wide receiver Carnell Tate’s 344 receiving yards are the most by a Titans wide receiver since the team relocated in 1997. Cleveland wide receiver Denzel Boston is first among all rookie wide receivers in receiving yards (345) and receiving touchdowns (three). He is also tied for first among all players with three receptions of 40-plus yards. Titans quarterback Cam Ward has a total QBR of 19.7 against zone defenses in 2026. That ranks No. 32 out of 33 qualified quarterbacks, according to ESPN Research. Tennessee is ranked No. 31 in passing plays of 20 yards or more with 10. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson’s total dropback EPA in the first three quarters is minus-23.35, which ranks at No. 37 among quarterbacks. Watson’s total dropback EPA in the fourth quarter is 21.13, which ranks at No. 6, according to The Athletic. Cleveland’s defense has allowed just one rushing touchdown this season. Cleveland has gone 51 consecutive games without allowing a 300-yard passer, the longest current streak in the league. Tennessee quarterback Cam Ward has yet to throw for 300 yards in his 23 career NFL games. OC Travis Switzer on Austin Barber pic.twitter.com/Rpl3LLJoCc — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 22, 2026 In Case You Missed It Respect is coming slowly, if at all, for the Browns so far in 2026: Big betting line change Should the Browns work out a trade for RB Jonathan Taylor? Let’s explore 3 keys to Week 7 for the Browns to beat the Titans NFL trade deadline: Browns connected to a whole lot of edge defenders as targets Browns TE not sweating the small things at the moment Cleveland Browns vs. Tennessee Titans Week 7 TV Map Will the Browns dominate the Titans, or just barely win? Reacts Survey Browns: Quarterback D-Day is looming on the horizon NFL predictions: Get ready for a rock fight in Titans-Browns matchup (Music City Miracles) 5 Titans players need to show up vs. Browns in Week 7 (Music City Miracles) A Final Quote Cleveland offensive tackle Tytus Howard on Tennessee defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who he faced nine times while with Houston: “He has no weaknesses in his game. He’s quick, he’s got power and plays the run. My biggest thing I tell the guys is don’t get back and let him attack you. You have to bring it to him and don’t back down because he’s looking for guys to back down. How he plays, you just have to stand ten toes (down).” What are you looking for from the Browns in the game against the Titans? Let everyone know in the comments!

title: Respect is coming slowly, if at all, for the Browns so far in 2026: Big betting line change
summary: The 2026 NFL season has a long way to go before completion. The results in Week 7 will not define the season, per se, but could go a long way for many teams, including the Cleveland Browns. A win versus the Tennessee Titans would run HC Todd Monken’s squad’s record to 5-2 with a high […]
full_text: The 2026 NFL season has a long way to go before completion. The results in Week 7 will not define the season, per se, but could go a long way for many teams, including the Cleveland Browns. A win versus the Tennessee Titans would run HC Todd Monken’s squad’s record to 5-2 with a high probability of being in the playoff conversation all year. Despite the quality record and wins versus four teams expected to compete for the NFL playoffs prior to the season, the Browns continue to linger low in power rankings and see very minimal betting line respect week in and week out . While the week-to-week respect still seems to be lacking, the betting line respect for the season is growing, appropriately. Prior to the season, the over/under line for Cleveland was between 5.5 and 6.5 games at most markets. Higher expectations than the win totals the two previous seasons, but low compared to the rest of the NFL. At this point, there are negative odds (bettors have to bet more than $100 to win $100) up to 8.5 wins (-150). The first positive odds (bettors win more than $100 when they bet $100) come at 9.5 wins (+260). FanDuel now believes that the Browns will at least win eight games this year, with a Week 7 win likely bumping that number up to a winning record of at least nine victories. Despite that, Cleveland is still just a 1.5-point favorite on the road in Tennessee this week against a one-win Titans team whose win total expectation is hovering around five this season. Week to week, the Browns continue to not be shown a lot of respect. Last week, I was the lone SB Nation expert to pick them to beat the Baltimore Ravens. This week, the tide is changing, with just two staff members picking against the Browns. Nationally, we are still seeing doubt about Cleveland’s chances in Week 7 . Despite that lack of week-to-week acknowledgement, expectations for the season have now risen quite significantly, and would rise again if the Browns can be successful on the road this week. What do you think of the current 8.5 win over/under line? What do you think it will take before the Browns earn national respect? Would it come if they win in Week 7? Join the conversation!
