title: Should the Browns work out a trade for RB Jonathan Taylor? Let’s explore
summary: When Todd Monken was hired as the new head coach of the Cleveland Browns, he let it known that his new offense would feature quite a bit of 12 and 13 personnel, be involved in the short passing game, and run the ball. Well, the first two have been featured, but running the ball hasn’t […]
full_text: When Todd Monken was hired as the new head coach of the Cleveland Browns, he let it known that his new offense would feature quite a bit of 12 and 13 personnel, be involved in the short passing game, and run the ball. Well, the first two have been featured, but running the ball hasn’t exactly gone as planned. RELATED: NFL TRADE DEADLINE – BROWNS CONNECTED TO EDGE RUSHERS In fact, Cleveland’s run game has failed. It is not good. Anytime a new system is put into place, obviously things don’t change overnight. This will take time, and we get it. However, the Browns have a decent team this year. They currently have a good record and are tied for first place in the division. Maybe waiting for next year has nobody interested. Overall, according to ESPN, the Browns are ranked #29 in total offense. The offense is ranked #23 in total yards (564), #17 in rushing attempts (155), #27 in average yards per carry (3.6), #26 in rushing touchdowns (3), #26 in first-down conversions via the run (29), and #10 in rushing plays for 20+ yards (4). Look at the team’s total rushing yards by game so far in 2026: @ Jacksonville: 87 @ Tampa Bay: 44 Carolina: 132 Pittsburgh: 112 @ NY Jets: 96 Baltimore: 93 The NFL trade deadline is still weeks away on November 10, 4:00 (Eastern). But already, WR Marvin Harrison jr., QB J.J. McCarthy, C Cam Jurgens, and CB Joey Porter Jr. have been shipped off to new homes. …Jonathan Taylor? https://t.co/P2NyBW4wyw pic.twitter.com/tKKHTK2HSe — SleeperBrowns (@SleeperBrowns) October 21, 2026 Should the Browns consider making a trade for one of the league’s best running backs? Namely, Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts. So, what’s the issue? Well, right out of the gate, Cleveland hasn’t had healthy running backs. In the last game against the Baltimore Ravens, neither of their two starting running backs was even on the roster to begin the season. Jaleel McLaughlin was in Denver Broncos training camp and was a last-day cut. Two days later, he signed to the Browns practice squad. Audric Estime was on the practice squad of the Minnesota Vikings . This meant that, except for FB Michael Burton, the entire running back room against Baltimore was practice squad athletes. Cleveland’s starting RB, Quinshon Judkins, has been out since he injured his ankle in the Week 5 loss to the New York Jets. His projected backup, Dylan Sampson, sustained a knee injury in the opening game versus the Jacksonville Jaguars. Both have a projection of returning to the field against the Tennessee Titans. Raheim Sanders has nine carries for 43 yards and a single TD. In five games this year, Judkins has 73 rushes for 221 yards, a single TD, and has averaged just 3.0 yards per carry. He also has 18 receptions for 102 yards. Is that good? Does this need improvement? Cleveland sits at 4-2-0. And that is in spite of a stellar rushing attack. What would this offense be if this offense had a stud running back? #Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, asked if he’s thought about his future and the trade deadline: “I haven’t given it any thought. … I think it would be a discredit and a disservice to my teammates and this whole organization to think about what could, what should, what may be.” pic.twitter.com/kL5koFkpqu — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) October 22, 2026 The Colts are in a tailspin this season. They have already fired their GM. They may start selling off their key pieces, including Taylor. Think about what this offense would look like if Taylor were to be starting behind QB Deshaun Watson on game days. Taylor has played in one more game than Judkins and already has 492 yards and seven rushing touchdowns. Seven! He is also active in the short passing game with 15 receptions for 163 yards. Another issue is that Cleveland’s offensive line features two rookies. Pro Football Focus (PFF) currently ranks the Browns offensive line group at #22. That is a huge detriment in trying to run the ball. PFF run blocking grades: LT Spencer Fano: 57.7 LG Zion Johnson: 67.3 C Elgton Jenkins: 56.1 RG Austin Barber: 73.0 RT Tytus Howard: 58.6 But as fans and the media, there seems to be a constant dialogue to badmouth the offensive line. It’s a steady out when things just don’t go right, and the quarterback is getting sacked eight times in a game. But consider this: The Browns replaced all five guys along the offensive line from last year. All of them. An offensive line isn’t five individual players, but one cohesive group. And that group needs time to gel. The season is entering the seventh week, but Cleveland’s O-Line hasn’t had six weeks together. OT Dawand Jones has subbed in for RT Howard. C Luke Wypler had to take over for Jenkins in a game. And how many weeks has RG Tevin Jenkins missed due to a back injury? Maybe this offensive line is great. Maybe it can become one of the best groups in the league, but it must be able to play together for a while. Taylor, age 27, is listed as the #6 running back in the league. He would be a major upgrade to the running back room and would vault this offense from not being able to run to taking over games. As Cleveland keeps winning with an eye towards the postseason, it would seem that a deal to bring in Taylor would become an ideal situation without really thinking about it too much. Why Cleveland may not make the Taylor trade The beauty with sticking with Judkins is the fact that he remains on his rookie deal that is paying him $1.4 million with a cap hit of just $2.6 million with two more years remaining. In contrast, Taylor is making $6.9 million with a cap hit of $16.2 million that ends this year. Which means any trade for Taylor will come with a huge extension. A trade for Taylor could be expensive. Right now, Cleveland has two first-round draft picks, a second and a third, and three fourth-round selections. What would it take to acquire Taylor? According to Jacob Richard of the Cleveland Browns on SI , it won’t be cheap: “The Colts will be asking for a first-or second-round pick plus a late pick swap for Taylor. Quinshon Judkins showed promise in his rookie season, is adjusting to rushing from the shotgun position, and with experience, he will get better.” One reason for Taylor’s ascent this year is the Colts offensive line, which PFF ranks #3 and is coming off a 1,585-yard season, and remains one of the best running backs in the NFL. Having the meat upfront to move huge bodies out of the way is certainly an advantage. Taylor would not be getting that sort of run blocking if he came to the Browns. In 2024, the San Francisco 49ers acquired RB Christian McCaffrey for a 2023 second-round pick, a third-round pick, a fourth-round pick, plus a fifth-round pick in 2024. It is doubtful that the Colts would get as much for Taylor, but this seems to be the parameter at the moment. Once Cleveland’s coaches get their running backs back healthy and in-house, Monken can evaluate what he has and if he needs to have GM Andrew Berry reach out for one of the league’s stud running backs. He just may decide that what he has will work out. “The potential for Cleveland’s running backs has not been touched, and the offense will benefit when the group is full and healthy. If the Browns wish to add to the room, then they have other options. The rushing attack is not a finished product, and there is still plenty of time for improvement without having to drain the resources by trading for Taylor.” Without looking forward to solving this in next year’s NFL Draft, perhaps when Judkins and Sampson are completely healthy and are getting snaps in live action, the run game will improve. Then again, maybe not. The clock is ticking on the trade deadline. And you can be certain that there are other teams that have this same idea for Taylor. If the Browns are indeed buyers and see Taylor as the bell cow looking forward to a playoff run, they will need to strike quickly. What do you think, should the Browns trade for Taylor, given the estimated cost, or keep riding with what they have?…

title: Breaking down the numbers: Cowboys at Eagles preview
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the Cowboys travel to Lincoln Financial on Monday Night Football to take on the Philadelphia Eagles. Cowboys […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the Cowboys travel to Lincoln Financial on Monday Night Football to take on the Philadelphia Eagles. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 258 yards on an astonishing 54 attempts. He’d finish the game with a 65.2 passer rating. Javonte Williams rushed the ball just 11 times against Green Bay for 41 yards. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens combined for 15 receptions on 29 targets, racking up 143 receiving yards Brevyn Spann-Ford split time with Jake Ferguson at a near 50/50 rate. The second-year tight end continues to improve his stock this season. The defense didn’t force a third-down stop until the near the six-minute mark in the second quarter. They tightened up in the second half, allowing just two third-down conversions and a total of 83 yards. Eagles key stats from last week The Eagles offense gained a total of 222 yards last week in their loss against the Panthers. Just 35 of those yards came on the ground from the beat up Philadelphia rushing attack. Tanner McKee threw the ball 45 times, finishing with a 77.5 passer rating. The leading receivers for the Eagles were DeVonta Smith ( seven receptions, 75 yards) and Dallas Goedert ( six receptions, 61 yards). Stay grounded This game could come down to which team’s rushing attack is the most successful. Last week, Javonte Williams and the run game had a few moments, but Dallas got away from it far too early. Coach Brian Schottenheimer has been under scrutiny this week for completely abandoning the run game, a tendency we’ve seen often throughout his career in Dallas. This week, it’ll be imperative to run a balanced offense against an Eagles defense that has struggled, but isn’t void of talent. On the Eagles side, it looks like Saquon Barkley has a good shot at returning to the lineup this week. This offense will not want Tanner McKee to throw the ball over 40 times again if it can be avoided. The Eagles offensive line has struggled to get much going for any of their running backs this season. But Dallas has also had their share of problems in limiting opponent’s rushing attacks. The formula is clear for Philadelphia, but can they execute? What do the numbers mean? This week, we’ve got two underperforming NFC East teams in a primetime Monday night matchup. The Eagles offense has struggled this season, even before the unfortunate Jalen Hurts health situation. The Cowboys have been mostly healthy on offense, but have lacked the killer instinct situationally while also no-showing the last two weeks. So which team has a better shot at putting up points and securing the win? As bad as Dallas has been the last two weeks, this offense still features two of the league’s scariest targets on the outside. They still have a top 10 quarterback who, at times, elevates himself into top five territory. The offensive line still features several All-Pro and Pro Bowl players. Make no mistake, they are dangerous and can go off any given week. This week, if coach Schottenheimer can return to a balanced offensive attack, the Cowboys will take home the win. The Eagles simply do not have the firepower to keep up, even against a struggling Dallas defense. And if Prescott and the offense can jump out to an early lead, this could get ugly for Philadelphia. The Cowboys have not put a holistically decent product on the field, especially the last two weeks. They have certainly been bad. But the Eagles have been just as bad, if not worse, and are now without their franchise quarterback. Tanner McKee is a stationary target without a good offensive line. They lack adequate talent at wide receiver, outside of DeVonta Smith. If the Cowboys defense ever had a moment to show up and get right, this would be a great time. If the Cowboys can stifle the biggest threat on the field in Barkely, this should be a long day for the Eagles backup quarterback. Everything points to Dallas winning, which of course should scare the pants off Cowboys fans. We saw a similar situation against a backup quarterback in Tampa Bay in week five. But records aside, that Buccaneers team is better than Philadelphia. They possess more offensive weapons, they have a mobile quarterback, and Todd Bowles put together a defensive gameplan that exposed a fatal weakness. The Eagles defensive scheme is vastly different and won’t crowd the line of scrimmage throughout the game. This plays to the Cowboys favor. Dallas has done very little to earn or trust this season. But if they can head up to Lincoln Financial and simply do their jobs against a beat up and beaten down Eagles team, this game should finish with a convincing Cowboys win.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys news: Dak Prescott explains why establishing the run is so important
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are averaging less than 80 yards a game running the football, and they need to get it going somehow against a tough Philadelphia Eagles defense. Mike Pettine provides a ton of experience to the Cowboys, and they hope it spreads throughout the entire coaching staff. It’s been struggle for the Cowboys’ offense […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are averaging less than 80 yards a game running the football, and they need to get it going somehow against a tough Philadelphia Eagles defense. Mike Pettine provides a ton of experience to the Cowboys, and they hope it spreads throughout the entire coaching staff. It’s been struggle for the Cowboys’ offense handling pressure over the last two games, but correcting won’t be difficult according to Dak Prescott. Also, Dallas continues to get good news when it comes to injuries. Dak Prescott details how finding rhythm in run game can help spark Cowboys offense – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys running game has taken a step back from last season. Dak Prescott dives into the importance of finding it again going forward. If Dallas can get the run game going, then it sets up an area Prescott is confident in and one he’s been at the best at over the course of his career: Play action, which can also get the Cowboys’ offense back to hitting more explosive plays. “From there, you get your play action, your passes,” Prescott said. “If you look at those numbers, I can guarantee you more than half of those were run action type plays and explosives. From there, a lot of things can open up.” Cowboys leaning on Mike Pettine as sounding board for Christian Parker, coaching staff – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Mike Pettine will spend most of his time watching film on the Cowboys and their opponents. The goal is to help Christian Parker and the other coaches as well. Pettine started working Wednesday of last week. He said his first few days were like drinking water from a fire hose. By Sunday, he was in the coaches’ box in Green Bay helping Parker and the Cowboys defense. Parker reflected on when the two coached together in Green Bay, starting in 2019. Parker was in the coaches’ box back then, operating as Pettine’s “eyes in the sky.” The roles were reversed Sunday. “He’s the same for me during the game,” Parker said. Will Cowboys Brian Schottenheimer give up play-calling? Here’s his answer – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Dallas has seen their offense hit a rough patch lately. Despite this, Brian Schottenheimer is certain he can get them back on track with him as the play caller. “No, absolutely not,” Schottenheimer said. “I have incredible confidence in our offense. We have not played well the last two weeks, we have addressed a lot of the reasons why. We haven’t changed who we are. We are still a good explosive offense with weapons. We can hurt you a lot of different ways. I certainly haven’t lost the ability to call plays. I’m an elite play-caller in this league, and it can change around quickly.” The Cowboys have played poorly vs. the blitz the past 2 weeks. What’s the problem? – Jon Machota, The Athletic Dak Prescott has been kown for being excellent against the blitz. With that not being the case lately, some serious questions need to be answered. “I just have to simplify the plan,” Prescott said after Sunday night’s 23-13 loss at Green Bay . “That starts with me and really it ends with me. You give yourself a few options on a blitz and you get in the game and you want to do this one, want to do that one, and I just have to be more simple and more direct in exactly what I want to do. I don’t want to get too into it and tell my answers, but it is definitely fixable.” Cowboys Injury Report: Dallas Getting Much-Needed Defensive Reinforcements – Randy Gurzi, SI.com Dallas hasn’t had the best luck on the injury front this season. Thankfully, their defense is set to get some key guys back on Monday night. Injuries have been a major concern for the Dallas Cowboys this season, especially on the defensive side of the ball. That’s been frustrating for a unit that was struggling to start the season, and things only got worse when their most talented players were put on the shelf. There has been some good news this week, however, with players such as linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and cornerback Cobie Durant trending toward a return when Dallas plays the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 7.

title: Cowboys at Eagles: 3 causes for concern in Philadelphia
summary: The Dallas Cowboys return to action Monday night for their third consecutive primetime matchup, taking on the Philadelphia Eagles. If the Cowboys want any shot at making the playoffs, they absolutely need to walk out of Philly with a win. Before the two teams square off, here are three causes for concern in the matchup. […]
full_text: (Photo by Tim Nwachukwu/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys return to action Monday night for their third consecutive primetime matchup, taking on the Philadelphia Eagles. If the Cowboys want any shot at making the playoffs, they absolutely need to walk out of Philly with a win. Before the two teams square off, here are three causes for concern in the matchup. 1) Cowboys’ Offensive Line Woes The last two weeks have been bad for Dallas’ offensive line. In their two matchups against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers, the Cowboys have allowed 30 total pressures, 25 QB hurries, and 5 QB hits. Dak Prescott’s mobility has kept them from allowing a single sack, but Dallas’ offensive line has been struggling as of late. This week, the Cowboys face another tough test against an Eagles’ defensive line that has a knack for creating some pressure. In their matchup last week against the Carolina Panthers, Philadelphia recorded 17 total pressures, 12 QB hurries, and 3 sacks. If Dallas’ offensive line comes in out of sync and struggles to pick up a blitz like they have the past two weeks, Philadelphia’s defensive line could dominate this matchup. Fixing their protection issues should be one of the Cowboys’ top priorities heading into this game. 2) Dallas’ Defens ive Struggles on Third Down If you looked at just first and second down, the Cowboys’ defense was outstanding last week. Unfortunately for Dallas, there’s more to playing complete defense than being good on the first two downs. In the first half, the Packers converted 9 of 10 third downs, leading them to take a commanding 17-0 lead at halftime. While Dallas played a lot better on third down in the second half, Green Bay finished 11-for-18, an outstanding 61.1% success rate on the most important down in football. Dallas’ third-down struggles on defense were not a one-game issue; they’ve been arguably their biggest problem all season long. This season, the Cowboys’ defense has allowed a league-worst 54.7% third-down conversion rate, a historically bad number. It doesn’t matter who is playing quarterback for the Eagles this week; if Dallas’ defense is as bad on third down as it was last week, it will struggle to leave Philly with a win. 3) Playoff Hopes Hang in the Balance If the Cowboys walk out of Philadelphia on Monday night without a win, you can put a nail in the coffin for their playoff hopes this season. Losing a third straight game, two of which they were favored in, bringing them to 2-5 and 1-2 in the division, would be a near-impossible deficit to recover from. On the flip side, if the Cowboys can find a way to defeat this beat-down Eagles team, their next five matchups feature some winnable games. Including this week, Dallas will likely be favored in four of their next six matchups, with four of those matchups coming at home. If the Cowboys play like they have the past two weeks, none of it will matter, but Monday night’s game has a chance to be a season-defining matchup for this 2026 Cowboys team.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: The Brian Schottenheimer Dallas Cowboys have been terrible in primetime
summary: Sometimes the lights are too bright. It is hard to not come to this conclusion these days, as silly as it is, given everything we have seen from the Brian Schottenheimer-led Dallas Cowboys. Over these last two losses the Cowboys have been handled rather easily and each time it occurred in primetime television slots. Maybe […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images | Getty Images Sometimes the lights are too bright. It is hard to not come to this conclusion these days, as silly as it is, given everything we have seen from the Brian Schottenheimer-led Dallas Cowboys. Over these last two losses the Cowboys have been handled rather easily and each time it occurred in primetime television slots. Maybe you don’t find it silly. Maybe you believe that playing in primetime adds to the pressure. There is certainly an argument to be made. Again, I feel like the Cowboys play in so many big games that this is sort of a moot point overall, but the data is pretty overwhelming. The Cowboys have been really bad in primetime This discussion carries merit because Monday’s Dallas Cowboys game is, like the last two, in primetime. America’s Team, baby. Monday will mark the fourth game this season that Dallas plays in primetime and the previous three, Week 1 against the New York Giants was the other, have all been losses. Here’s the thing, the Cowboys have been horrendous in primetime for a while now. Here is, shout out to Stathead , their primetime record under Brian Schottenheimer specifically. The Cowboys are 1-7-1 in primetime under Brian Schottenheimer. One. Seven. And one. So far Schotty has only overseen one successful primetime game and it was also a Monday night affair, last year’s win against the Las Vegas Raiders. Is this truly something that we can connect to time? Do we really believe the lights get too bright for this team? Or is it simply a matter of coincidence? As I’ve stated several times I find it hard to believe that the big stage of things bothers them. It wasn’t a primetime game by definition, but the team did beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving Day last year so we know they can rise to the occassion. Maybe I’m wrong, though. Perhaps you believe that the pressure rises for them in these instances. Let us know what you think in the comments down below.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: We ate the cheese again
summary: It has become an all too familiar pattern. The Dallas Cowboys come off a disappointing season. They draft and sometimes dip into the free agent and trade markets to improve the roster. Usually there is some kind of significant coaching change. We watch the offseason and training camp activities with decidedly rose colored glasses. Our […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images It has become an all too familiar pattern. The Dallas Cowboys come off a disappointing season. They draft and sometimes dip into the free agent and trade markets to improve the roster. Usually there is some kind of significant coaching change. We watch the offseason and training camp activities with decidedly rose colored glasses. Our hopes soar for it to finally be the year we see real playoff success. And things crash to the ground. Or more likely make a wet splatting sound. Why do we do this to ourselves? Tom Ryle and Sean Martin dig into things. (And share your pain.) Tom – There are so many parts of this. One thing is certain, this team has not had a clear-eyed view of itself for many, many years. So let’s start with one element that has been constant throughout the long drought for Dallas: Ownership. You’ll notice I don’t single out Jerry Jones, but use that term to include Stephen as well, and even encompass any inputs Charlotte and Jerry Jr. might make. Most of the, um, smoke getting slung our way does come from Jerry, but Stephen usually contributes to it. He’s just not as flamboyant and flat out loud as his father. Obviously there are myriad reasons to question Jerry Sr.’s acumen as a football executive, but one thing that is unquestioned is his talent at marketing. When the team had its great success in the early nineties, he not only returned them to their status as the glamor franchise of the NFL, he took them to new heights. Sadly, he fails to see that selling a brand is much more useful than overselling a team’s ability to actually win on the field. Unwittingly (perhaps) the media plays right along with that, reporting every convoluted statement and bizarre metaphor he issues. And we just kind of get sucked in. Now we have reached a point where it has spread to the players themselves. Yes, I’m going back to the ludicrous, in hindsight, ‘Greatest Offense There Is’ label that the players, apparently led by Dak Prescott, came up with. While some of us were a bit hesitant to buy all the way in, we still thought the offense was the real strength of the team. But lately, they have been floundering, while the defense looked a lot better against the Green Bay Packers. If they are to win Monday against the Philadelphia Eagles, who now have lost Jalen Hurts for the season, it may be on the defense to carry things. Who would have guessed that a couple of months ago? Sean – Being adverse to change at a wide enough or fast enough scale is a topic that’s been talked about for literal years on end when it comes to both the shortcomings of the Cowboys, and why we fall for it as fans. Exhaustion doesn’t even begin to describe how much I don’t want to have that same talk anymore, but let’s just frame this one way with the road game at Philadelphia looming. In year one of Brian Schottenheimer, and game number one, a close loss to these Eagles in primetime was seen as an actual good sign and the effort of the team was complimented in that process. 22 games later, the pitchforks are already out, and a close loss at the birds this time will get exactly zero brownie points from the fanbase. The team’s effort is no longer good enough. Hell, even a win might not make us feel great. That is an amazing amount of dropoff normally reserved for a team that lost its starting quarterback for significant time. Oh that’s right, it’s the Giants and Eagles with season ending quarterback injuries, and the Commanders having every reason to think they could have the Cowboys sitting at 1-5 if their QB didn’t come out of that week two game. Things are very not fun right now, Tom. Tom – No, they are not. But they could at least get interesting with a win at Philadelphia, because the rest of the division has so many struggles right now. String a few wins together and they could win the NFC East. Whether that would help in the long run is of course a big question. Staggering into the playoffs and going out in the first round would leave many questions, including whether they need to make a change at the top of the coaching staff. That does not seem terribly likely, given Jerry Jones’ tendency to stick with head coaches a season or two too long. And a win this week would turn down the heat on Schottenheimer’s seat a bit. Likewise, a close win would not bode well. This is a wounded Eagles team. If the Cowboys were just competent on both sides of the ball, they should be able to win by a decent margin. That would boost confidence in a locker room that has to be reeling a bit. A lot is riding on this one. Sean – I said I would continue to try to find any reason for some optimism until it’s flat out impossible, and you gave me something to work with here Tom, when it comes to this up-for-grabs NFC East. I actually think one of the things that could inspire a head coaching change or other change of real meaning would be making the playoffs but exiting in the Wild Card round again, which is the overwhelming expectation for whoever comes out of the division right now. Moving on from Schottenheimer before he reaches the playoffs at least once is likely a level of failure the ownership you talked about isn’t willing to admit. Finding out as soon as possible that Schotty is the latest coach whose ceiling is getting the team in the dance, but not going home with the prom queen could be the catalyst. It could also lead to a little less of a firestorm that we’ve seen in the recent offseasons, where the pressure is firmly on to get back in the playoffs. As far as your other point about winning in any type of convincing fashion at the Eagles, I have my serious doubts. There’s a running theme we’ve been touching on already about recent game box scores not even telling the full story. The Texans were penalized to death in a game the Cowboys still flirted with losing. The Bucs spoiled a home party with a UDFA QB, and also a slew of penalties. The Packers dropped multiple touchdowns, and you guessed it, committed a lot of penalties too, and beat these Cowboys by ten. This is just not a winning outfit right now, simply put. Tom – I can’t argue with your last point. As troubling as the bad performances on the field are, I am at least as worried about how there just doesn’t seem to be a winning culture in Dallas. Now, I realize that can be a bit of a circular argument, since winning itself seems to be the prime determinant of a winning culture. Still, this team is not responding well to adversity. They are dealing with injuries, but have you looked at the San Francisco 49ers? They are almost out of wide receivers, yet they still are undefeated after a bit of a narrow escape against the Washington Commanders. Clearly coaching is playing a part there, which just increases the questions about that of the Cowboys. It may only be week seven of the season, but the Philadelphia game looms as a crucial test for Dallas. A win gives them some hope of making something good out of the season. A loss will inevitably be seen as virtually ending their chances at the postseason this year. I wish I could say that I have optimism they are going to show us some real spine and get a clear victory. But that would be a lie worthy of a political ad. Sean – Glad we could air out some frustrations, Tom. It’s perfectly clear we aren’t the only fans with such feelings. Personally, I don’t think things will ever get bad enough for me not to enjoy a win against the Eagles at least a little bit, so let’s see what happens. Bobcats are back home here in Bozeman for the first time in several weeks on Saturday, followed by a Sunday where the Cowboys can’t hurt any of us. Cheers to the weekend.
author: Sean Martin

title: How the Cowboys offensive line matches up with the Eagles
summary: If the Dallas Cowboys want to win this week, they could use a boost from their offensive line. With Tyler Smith back and healthy, there is no excuse for this line to not start taking over games. Here is how they match up with the Eagles defensvie front. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive […]
full_text: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If the Dallas Cowboys want to win this week, they could use a boost from their offensive line. With Tyler Smith back and healthy, there is no excuse for this line to not start taking over games. Here is how they match up with the Eagles defensvie front. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 50% (17th) Run Block Win Rate – 69% (31st) Pressure rate allowed – 27% (10th) Sacks allowed – 6 (2nd) Last three week trend: Allowing too much pressure is pass pro, run game struggling The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Dallas cannot let Philadelphia’s interior take away the running game The Eagles’ biggest strength up front is not rushing the passer, it’s stopping the run. Philadelphia rank fifth in Run Stop Win Rate at 32%, and Jordan Davis has been one of the biggest reasons why. Davis owns a 83.2 run-defense grade on PFF, fifth among qualifying interior defensive linemen. He has also registered 14 defensive stops making him one of the most effective at his position. At 336 pounds, Davis is extremely difficult to move when Dallas wants to run directly between the tackles. That’s concerning because the Cowboys are already struggling badly there. Dallas rank 31st in Run Block Win Rate and then produced only 48 rushing yards against Green Bay. Javonte Williams only managed 41 yards on 11 carries and failed to reach the endzone. The return of Tyler Smith has not immediately fixed everything. Smith, Cooper Beebe and Tyler Booker give Dallas plenty of talent inside, but this is a week where communication and double teams have to be cleaner. If Davis is allowed to control the middle by himself, Philadelphia can keep its linebackers free to attack Williams. If Dallas needs two blockers just to stop Davis moving into the backfield, the Eagles are already gaining an advantage because another defender is now free to attack the runner. PRESSURE POINT: Jalen Carter is still the player who can wreck a passing play The season statistics have not been vintage Jalen Carter. He has produced 10 pressures and one sack, while his 60.0 pass-rush grade was well below the standard he established earlier in his career. Dallas should not mistake that for Carter suddenly becoming an easy matchup and interior pressure is especially dangerous for Prescott. An edge rusher normally forces a quarterback to step forward. A defensive tackle winning directly through the middle removes that escape route altogether. Dallas saw what pressure did to its offense against Green Bay. Prescott was hurried into uncomfortable throws, Dallas turned the football over twice through interceptions, and the offense spent too much of the night reacting to the defense rather than dictating the game. The Eagles only have eight sacks this season, but Dallas cannot allow Carter to become the player who suddenly wakes their pass rush up. Where To Attack Every defensive line has a weakness, here are the Packers soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Make Philadelphia’s edge defenders stop the run Do not repeatedly run directly at Jordan Davis, make the Eagles move sideways instead. Jalyx Hunt has a 53.0 PFF run-defense grade, 88th among qualifying edge defenders. Nolan Smith has been better against the run, but he is now in the concussion protocol after leaving Sunday’s loss to Carolina. Hunt is also dealing with ankle and knee issues. That makes the outside of Philadelphia’s defensive front much more interesting than the middle. Dallas can use outside-zone runs, counters and pulling guards to move the point of attack away from Davis, and this plays into Booker’s strengths. Instead of asking him to repeatedly move a 336-pound defensive tackle straight backwards, Dallas can pull Booker into space and let him attack a linebacker or edge defender. Carolina offered evidence that Philadelphia can be worn down this way. Chuba Hubbard carried 28 times for 120 yards and a touchdown in Sunday’s win at Lincoln Financial Field. Dallas needs that same patience. GREEN LIGHT: Trust the tackles against a struggling pass rush This is the matchup Dallas should be willing to test. Philadelphia is ranked only 25th in Pass Rush Win Rate at 44%, and generating pressure on only 37% of opposing dropbacks, with that falling to 29% when they don’t bother to blitz. And now Nolan Smith’s availability is uncertain. Smith recorded his third sack of the year before suffering a concussion against Carolina. Hunt is also carrying an injury. That should give Tyler Guyton and Terence Steele an opportunity to recover from Green Bay. Guyton had been one of Dallas’ best run blockers, carrying a 90.0 PFF run-blocking grade, fourth among qualifying tackles. He had also allowed 12 pressures but no sacks entering the game. Steele remains the shakier side. His 54.4 pass-blocking grade ranked 63rd among 72 qualifying tackles, although he has surrendered only one sack. Philadelphia should not force Dallas to constantly keep a tight end or running back in protection. If the Eagles rush four, Dallas needs to trust its five offensive linemen. That allows Jake Ferguson, Williams and the other eligible receivers to get into routes and gives Prescott more places to go with the football. The Chaos Report Here’s the Philadelphia Eagles defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 8 (31st) Pass Rush Win Rate – 44% (25th) Run Stop Win Rate – 32% (5th) QB Pressure Rate – 37% (5th) Last three week trend: Strong run defense, poor pass rush Matchup of the week Cooper Beebe vs. Jordan Davis This matchup gets directly to Dallas’ biggest offensive-line problem. Can the Cowboys finally run the football? Beebe gets one of the NFL’s better run-defending defensive tackles in Davis’ and his sheer size makes him extremely difficult for a center to handle alone. Beebe will get help from Smith and Booker on plenty of snaps, but Dallas cannot dedicate two blockers to Davis forever. If Beebe can hold his ground long enough for one of the guards to move onto the second level, Williams suddenly has space. If Davis pushes Beebe backwards, the play can be over before Williams even reaches the line of scrimmage. Best route to success: The Eagles are strong inside against the run but have struggled to create consistent pass pressure, Dallas needs to use that information. Force the edge defenders to tackle Williams, use screens and quick passes if Philadelphia becomes aggressive, and when the Eagles rush four, let the offensive line prove it can protect Prescott without extra help. Philadelphia’s front has talent, but the numbers show areas Dallas can attack. Injury Updates: Dallas currently has no new injury concerns among its five starting offensive linemen. The major Philadelphia injury to monitor is Nolan Smith, who suffered a concussion against Carolina and will have to clear the league’s concussion protocol before playing. Jordan Davis suffered an ankle injury on Sunday but practiced in full on Thursday, while Jalyx Hunt is also dealing with ankle issues.
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys at Eagles: 2 players Dallas should use more in Week 7
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are stuck in the mud. After two straight losses in which they didn’t come close to winning either game, Dallas sits with a 2-4 record, desperately needing a win in Week 7. If the Cowboys want to turn this around, they’ll need to mix some things up this week against the Eagles. […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are stuck in the mud. After two straight losses in which they didn’t come close to winning either game, Dallas sits with a 2-4 record, desperately needing a win in Week 7. If the Cowboys want to turn this around, they’ll need to mix some things up this week against the Eagles. With that thought in mind, here are two players the Cowboys should use more on Monday night in Philly. 1) WR George Pickens After a career year in 2025, expectations were sky-high for George Pickens entering his second season in Dallas. Many believed Pickens, the Cowboys’ best receiver last season, was ready to add consistency and take the next step to become one of the NFL’s elite receiving threats. Unfortunately for both Pickens and the Cowboys, that hasn’t happened yet. Six games into the 2026 season, the 25-year-old wideout is yet to have a true breakout game, and his numbers year over year are down in every statistical category. 2025 (6 games): 48 targets, 32 receptions, 66.7% catch rate, 525 receiving yards, 16.4 Y/R, 6 touchdowns 2026 (6 games): 52 targets, 33 receptions, 63.5% catch rate, 428 receiving yards, 13.0 Y/R, 1 touchdown The thing that made Pickens so dominant during his first season in Dallas was his ability to make big plays down the field. So far in 2026, the wideout has recorded just three receptions of 20+ yards. To Pickens’ credit, he has only been given seven such chances this year, a number that should be exponentially higher. This week, facing off against a talented Eagles’ defense, the Cowboys need to make it a focal point to get Pickens involved early and often. Dallas’ offense is struggling, and giving Pickens consistent chances to make game-changing catches (or drawing flags) down the field could be just what they need to get out of their offensive rut. 2) LB Shemar James One of the more impressive defenders for Dallas last week was linebacker Shermar James. After Dee Winters left the game early with an Achilles injury, James was thrust into a critical role in Dallas’ defense and performed well. The linebacker was tied for the team lead with three defensive stops, along with four tackles and an 80.0 tackling grade . While it appears the Cowboys will get DeMarvion Overshown back this week, they need to find a way to keep James consistently in the linebacker rotation. The former fifth-round pick has serious limitations in coverage, but his ability to be a sure tackler has been superior to rookie Jaishawn Barham, who has missed at least one tackle in every game this season. On run downs, the Cowboys should keep James on the field and see if he can turn his solid performance in Week 6 into a positive trend moving forward.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: The Cowboys offense hasn’t been this flat in a while
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have a lot of problems right now. Speaking in a macro sense, they exist on both sides of the ball. The defense has been moribund for a long time now so struggles there are hardly new. We unfortunately know to expect the team to have issues there. But entering this season it […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys have a lot of problems right now. Speaking in a macro sense, they exist on both sides of the ball. The defense has been moribund for a long time now so struggles there are hardly new. We unfortunately know to expect the team to have issues there. But entering this season it was a foregone conclusion, well beyond an assumption, that the offense would at least take care of business and therefore give the team a chance. They started off this season in a manner that wasn’t quite “GOTI” level, but they at least looked like a group that could somewhat live up to that idea. That has not been the case over the last two weeks. We haven’t seen the offense this low in a long time Combing through the insights from NFL Pro for this week’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles unveiled something that really surprised me, and it really captures how and why it feels like the offense is broken in a way that it hasn’t been in a long time. Consider that the Cowboys have only scored 29 points over their two-game losing streak. Before we go further, let’s stipulate that going off of ‘points scored’ is casting a very, very, very vague net over things, but this tidbit is still interesting. The 29 points that the Cowboys have scored in this two-game span are the fewest that they have scored in any two-game span where Dak Prescott started and finished both games in question since Weeks 12 and 13 of the 2019 season. Dallas barely squeaked out 24 points against the New England Patriots and Buffalo Bills (Thanksgiving) during that span, and a few weeks later Jason Garrett would not be asked to return as the team’s head coach. It is also worth adding context that this was the first year in which Kellen Moore was the team’s offensive coordinator. But holy cow. Obviously the qualifier of Dak starting and finishing both games in question moves the goalposts of spans a little bit, but that is necessary to fully evaluate what is happening here. Consider that the 2019 span also preceded CeeDee Lamb even being on the Cowboys roster. There is absolutely zero reason for why the offense should be pulling teeth to score right now with Prescott, Lamb, and everyone else healthy and available. If we are pointing a finger at any one “why” here, it seems that the current book on how to stop the Cowboys is to fluster Prescott specifically with pressure. For so long he was a quarterback who excelled against the blitz, and he has seemingly not been able to thrive at all against them in these last two games. NFL Pro also noted that Prescott has thrown over 60% of his passes short (so within 0-9 air yards) over the span in question. It was 61.9% against the Buccaneers and 63% against the Packers, if you are curious. Dak has had a short pass rate of at least 60% a total of five times throughout the Brian Schottenheimer era and all five of those have been losses. If you can get to him quickly and not allow him time to work downfield with Lamb or George Pickens, your odds are pretty good. Prescott, Lamb, Pickens, and Schottenheimer all have to find a way to counteract this phenomenon and they have to find a way to do that immediately. If they don’t, they are going to keep running into this challenge and so long as it is effective, why would anybody do anything different?
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys news: Brian Schottenheimer is feeling the pressure
summary: As Eagles fans love to say, it’s “Dallas week”. The Cowboys vs Eagles matchups are some of the more anticipated matchups on the schedule every season. We already know Jalen Hurts will not be playing, but Saquon Barkley is expected to make his return. The Cowboys will also be getting some reinforcements back with Cobie […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As Eagles fans love to say, it’s “Dallas week”. The Cowboys vs Eagles matchups are some of the more anticipated matchups on the schedule every season. We already know Jalen Hurts will not be playing, but Saquon Barkley is expected to make his return. The Cowboys will also be getting some reinforcements back with Cobie Durant and DeMarvion Overshown expected to return to the starting lineup and hopefully provide a nice boost the the struggling Cowboys defense. Schottenheimer stands firm amid Cowboys’ struggles: “I know what a great coach I am” – Briana Aldridge, CBS Sports Brian Schottenheimer has done a lot of talking this season, but we have yet to see much action. If the wins don’t start coming soon, the Cowboys second-year head coach could be in trouble. “We’ve got to play better; I’ve got to coach better,” said Schottenheimer. The words might mean more in Week 7 if they didn’t seem repetitive after back-to-back losses. The honeymoon phase seems over, and Cowboys Nation’s frustration isn’t going unnoticed. “No one likes it. I block out most of it; some of it gets to me, but at the same time, I’ve got strong shoulders,” Schottenheimer said. “I know what a great coach I am, and I know what this team is capable of. That’s what I focus on.” Dallas Cowboys Injury Report For Week 7 vs Eagles: George Pickens, 10 Others Listed – Josh Sanchez, SI.com Despite remaining very healthy on the offensive side of the ball, the Cowboys defense has been very banged up to start the season. Based on the first injury report for Week 7, the Cowboys may be getting healthy at the right (most desperate) time. With practice picking up, the team has dropped its initial injury report for the week , with 11 total players getting listed. Von Miller was given a veteran rest day, while All-Pro return specialist KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and starting linebacker Dee Winters (calf) were also among those who did not participate. Star wide receiver George Pickens also popped up on the injury report, officially listed as limited with a shoulder injury. With the Cowboys’ struggling offense trying to find its groove again , the last thing they can afford is for a player of Pickens’ caliber to be sidelined, so hopefully he will be back to full participation by the end of the week. Cobie Durant aiming to do his part for Cowboys secondary, help create turnovers – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Cobie Durant looks to make his return in week 7. His play in the secondary has been severely missed after missing the last four games due to a hamstring injury. “A blessing for sure,” Durant said. “Injuries happen, things happen man, but you’ve just got to stack those days that you’re missing and do your part. And then be ready when your name is called when you get back out there.” Durant was officially listed as limited on the practice report Thursday, and added that detail when talking to reporters in the locker room Thursday. He and the team are being cautious as hamstring injuries can sometimes be unpredictable. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Is blueprint out for stopping Cowboys’ offense? Teams are beating Dak Prescott in this key area – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News What is going on with the Cowboys inability to beat the blitz? After years of Dak Prescott dominating against the blitz, this year has been much different. Can the Cowboys adjust their protection rules and get back on track or is the blueprint out? The Cowboys ‘ offense has struggled the last two weeks, especially compared to how they performed last year with similar personnel. There’s a host of reasons: big plays have disappeared; deficits have been common; the running game has lowered both its productivity and its usage. Those factors might stem from one overall concern: Is a blueprint out there on how to quell the Cowboys and quarterback Dak Prescott ? The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Green Bay Packers, the last two teams the Cowboys have faced, sure looked like they followed one. Both teams blitzed Prescott 17 times, according to pro-football-reference.com. It was the two-highest blitz totals Prescott has seen this season. Cowboys can get the victory Monday night in Philadelphia – Mike Poland, Blogging the Boys The Cowboys have already lost a game against a young, inexperienced QB. On Monday they face another. The Cowboys are 2-4 after losing to Green Bay, but Monday night gives them the perfect opportunity to change the mood. Philadelphia is also 2-4, has lost four games in a row and will be without Jalen Hurts. Hurts will miss the remainder of the season after being diagnosed with blood clots and undergoing treatment. Philadelphia will instead start Tanner McKee.

title: Broncos vs. Cardinals: 3 Players to Watch in Week 7
summary: For their Week 7 matchup, the Denver Broncos trek south to take on the Arizona Cardinals. The Broncos have fared well thus far going 4-2 against a tough gauntlet of opponents. In order to achieve their fifth victory of the season, these three players need to show up and make an impact against the Cardinals. […]
full_text: Aug 21, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos defensive end Zach Allen (99) before the preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For their Week 7 matchup, the Denver Broncos trek south to take on the Arizona Cardinals. The Broncos have fared well thus far going 4-2 against a tough gauntlet of opponents. In order to achieve their fifth victory of the season, these three players need to show up and make an impact against the Cardinals. Zach Allen — Defensive Lineman Sunday’s matchup will be bittersweet for Zach Allen. It’s a return back to where he started his NFL career. He spent four seasons with the Cardinals having the privelege to learn under J.J. Watt and was coached up by Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph. Flash forward to the present day and Allen has cemented himself as one of the best interior defensive lineman in the National Football League. The eighth year pro is coming off back-to-back All-Pro seasons. Through six games, the former third-round pick out of Boston College is putting up another incredible season . He already has 4.5 sacks, 31 tackles, and 16 quarterback hits. Finding a way to pressure and rattle Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett will be a huge key to the game. I have a feeling Allen will be playing with a little bit more intensity and fire going up against the team that drafted him all those years ago. I have no doubt he is going to have an impact and help lead the Broncos to a big win. Jonathon Cooper — Edge Rusher After spending the first six games on the NFL Commissioner’s Exempt List, Jonathon Cooper is scheduled to make his 2026 regular season debut against the Cardinals. With Jonah Elliss sidelined with an injury suffered against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football , the Broncos will need the sixth-year edge rusher to hit the ground running and make an impact versus the Cardinals. The past three seasons, Cooper has been one of the most underrated edge rushers in the NFL. He posted at least eight sacks a season from 2023-2025, averaged over 15 quarterback hits a year, and has been a strong defender against the run. His presence in the starting lineup should help Denver’s defense be even more formidable. J.K. Dobbins — Running Back A lot of fans across Broncos Country were hoping for Denver to make a big splash this off-season to add more juice to their running back group. Instead, the Broncos brought back J.K. Dobbins on a two-year deal. He showed a lot of promise early on last season, but missed most of the second half of the season due to injury. In six games, Dobbins hasn’t made much of an impact for Denver. Quite honestly, he looks like he may have hit a cliff. He has just 270 yards on 81 carries with two touchdowns. Outside of a few runs of ten yards or more, he is really struggling to get quality yardage and sports a paltry 3.3 yard per carry average. The Cardinals have a bottom ten run defense in the NFL. They’ve allowed at least 140 yards or more in three contests. If there was any game for Dobbins and the Broncos’ rushing attack to finally make a mark, this one would be it. In the event that doesn’t happen, I’m not sure what Denver should do. More carries to RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman make sense, but perhaps General Manager George Paton might need to get on the phone and inquire about adding a back before the trade deadline. With Chris Ballard out in Indianapolis, perhaps Paton can ask about what it would take to get Jonathan Taylor? Probably too much, but a strong running game will be essential for Denver to be contenders this season.

title: The Broncos aren’t overlooking the Cardinals
summary: After their first six games of the 2026 season, the Denver Broncos find themselves in familiar territory. They sport a 4-2 record—just like last season. It wasn’t pretty then and hasn’t been thus far. Nevertheless, more wins than losses is always a good thing. Strong defensive performances and penchant for fourth quarter heroics have continued […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images After their first six games of the 2026 season, the Denver Broncos find themselves in familiar territory. They sport a 4-2 record—just like last season. It wasn’t pretty then and hasn’t been thus far. Nevertheless, more wins than losses is always a good thing. Strong defensive performances and penchant for fourth quarter heroics have continued for this year’s Broncos. This weekend, they face off against the Arizona Cardinals who are currently 2-4 and coming off an impressive victory the Los Angeles Rams. Even though the Cardinals have a losing record, the Broncos aren’t overlooking their Week 7 opponent. Each game provides an opportunity for every team in the National Football League. For the Broncos this Sunday, it’s a chance to get an important fifth win of the season. Moreover, it could become a streak starter. A gridiron battle—if won—that would give them confidence and momentum as the second half of the season approaches. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton touched based on a variety of topics. However, finding a way to improve and string together more victories to go on a run [like last year] was a point of emphasis. “That 4-2 mark a year ago, we’d come off of a real good defensive effort in London. It just can’t be a yo-yo. Any team that I can think of, there are runs. I think more importantly the last thing I just said to them was, ‘We have to be ascending, improving.’ I think they understand that,” stated Payton. The Broncos haven’t played a complete game thus far. Interestingly enough quite similar to 2025. The major exception being the matchup versus the Cincinnati Bengals who were without star quarterback Joe Burrow. There is no doubt Payton’s right. Denver needs to keep pushing forward and make the necessary adjustments to become a more complete team that’s built to compete for the long haul. A huge part of that is finding a viable recipe for success offensively. Broncos Country has grown accustomed to slowing starts on offense the past several years, only to find relief in the second half of the season when things finally started to click. Though with a little extra preparation for their Week 7 matchup, the team hopes that spark comes sooner than later. The Cardinals may not have a lot of star power on defense and rank in the bottom half of most metrics across the board. However, they put together a quality outing against the Los Angeles Rams last weekend. They give a lot of different looks and switch up a lot between Cover 3, Cover 4, and Cover 6 coverage looks—zone principles that Bo Nix and Denver’s offense are failing to find ways to beat. In order for the offense to do better, Payton acknowledged that it will be critical to be able to decipher and adequately react to their unique defensive packages. “Our defense, we see a base-look, kind of an Okie structure. There’ll be some similarities. Then they have a nickel package, a dime. Their penny—and we have a penny too—it can be a little blurry. One of the important notes this week was Communication ID,” mentioned Payton. “Usually there’s someone in the huddle that’s looking, and Bo is stepping into the huddle. They’re saying, ‘Nickel, nickel,’ or ‘Base, base.’ Then I’ll a lot of times say, ‘Hey Bo, this is base defense here.’ When we’re game planning, if you’re wanting to run a play against their base defense, there are certain things in order to know you’re getting base. There’s no 100 percent. That’s an important thing this week,” added Payton. How the Broncos choose to combat Arizona’s defense will be interesting to watch. Everyone is hoping to see Nix dial it up through the air, yet the biggest weakness the Cardinals have defensively is stopping the run. They’ve given up over 140 yards in three contests thus far. I think a big part of their game plan will be a healthy dose of J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey, and giving reps to Jonah Coleman who is expected to play on Sunday. If Denver can establish a formidable rushing attack, that would bode well for Nix and the offense, who have thrived off play-action principles and deep shots when the running game is clicking. Can Denver’s offense finally find a recipe for success on Sunday? You’ll just have to tune in and find out.

title: Do you think Bo Nix is ready to go on a run?
summary: There has been a lot of hand wringing over the Denver Broncos offense and Bo Nix in particular, but the coaching staff has no lost faith in him at all. Offensive coordinator Davis Webb came out and defending him hard this week and even said he feels like Nix is about to go on a […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos reacts on the field during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images There has been a lot of hand wringing over the Denver Broncos offense and Bo Nix in particular, but the coaching staff has no lost faith in him at all. Offensive coordinator Davis Webb came out and defending him hard this week and even said he feels like Nix is about to go on a bit of a run. DNVR Spots posted this clip of Webb’s comments: I’m kind of feeling it too. Nix has started slow in every season he’s been in the NFL and right about this time is when he gets a little hot for a stretch. It would be perfect timing if he did because they could seriously close the gap on the Kansas City Chiefs with wins this week and next week. Broncos daily recap Scouting the Enemy: Arizona Cardinals The Denver Broncos battle the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Here is a deeper look at their Week 7 opponent. The Broncos offense needs more from Bo Nix Denver’s found ways to win, but the offense needs more consistency and production from Nix to reach its potential. Potent quotables Sean Payton Opening statement “A little breezy today, but good Friday work. Any questions?” On how OLB Jonathon Cooper looked in practice this week “Good, good. The good news with the current protocol is they can stay in shape, and train, and all those things where eight or 10 years ago it was different. So that’s benefited him.” On if he would like to see QB Bo Nix run more “I think you have to be careful about that. There are certain on-the-move plays, but I think some of that can happen organically. A lot of that happens with back-to-the-quarterback defense. It’s a little bit different when eyes are to the quarterback. So when you get the man combinations or the match stuff… It’s not on my Top-10 list of things that we’re working on.” On why he keeps a fullback on the roster “I think this: it’s real simple. Those teams that don’t, they have an ‘F’ tight end that would do the same things, maybe a bigger stature, play special teams. So let’s just hypothetically say we didn’t have a fullback. [TE] Nate Adkins would fit in a lot of those ‘F’ roles. So when you see more tight ends, there’s one of them usually on each roster that’s doing fullback things. So a lot of it’s just roster building. I kind of prefer having that true ‘F’, but the right one, not at the expense of the better one.” On why FB Adam Prentice’s snap count has decreased from last season “I think it depends on what we’re trying to get each week. We talk about, are we wanting their base defense or are we wanting their sub defense? So that can impact his role in the gameplan, but that makes sense though.” On the Cardinals retiring Pro Football Hall of Fame WR Larry Fitzgerald Jr.’s number on Sunday “He was amazing. Fortunately I was able to spend some time with him at the [Pro Football] Hall of Fame. There are so many things that he represented that are right. So consistent, competitive. It was an amazing statistic, I never knew they kept track of it. He had more tackles—maybe that’s not a good stat—but he had more tackles than dropped passes. He was smart, tough, reliable. He knew then that he was going to be at this game and gave me a hard time about it. Tremendous player. Really, really good.” On if the extra rest has helped DL Zach Allen “It’s always that balance with those interior guys when you’re in a rotation. The game ends, and I always first thing on Monday, I’m always looking at the pitch count and then special teams. How many plays? Usually it’s the backup quarterback or the backup lineman that might have the… But how many plays? it’s purposeful with his energy and the way he plays, and so it helps to have depth.” On if the extra rest has helped DL Zach Allen take a leap as a run defender “His tape has been fantastic. He’s really, really athletic at the snap, and so I’m glad he’s ours.” On managing the return of a veteran who has missed several weeks compared with a rookie “I think the first thing would be injury, no injury, experience. I’m always mindful of anyone’s first game back if it’s been past a month, call it the pitch count. That would be the big difference. These players that are returning off of reserve/injured or just making sure that we’re keeping track of, ‘What’s the goal before we play? What do we see pitch-count wise?’ Then paying attention to it.” On if CB Pat Surtain II will play this week “We’ll see, we’ll see, we’ll see. We’re not announcing starting lineups now.” On the key to stringing wins together “I think there are some similarities and differences, but I think that 4-2 mark a year ago, we’d come off of a real good defensive effort in London. It just can’t be a yo-yo. Any team that I can think of, there are runs. I think more importantly, the last thing I just said to them was, ‘We have to be ascending, improving.’ I think they understand that.” On what has enabled the team to embrace a next-man-up mentality “Fair enough. I think depth at certain positions, like corner for instance. It’s one thing to say next man up, but having developed guys and having that depth in key areas. It is an attrition league. You hope that your offseason, how you’ve prepared, you’re reducing your injuries. Yet with the rosters the way they are, it’s very likely. So I’m pleased that we’ve got that depth.” On how he prepares backups to step in for injured players while keeping them healthy “When we have practice, you’ll see let’s say a team period. The front line [goes], but then very quickly in that team period, you’ll see other guys that might have to play that are getting reps. That would be part of the weekly process.” On if CB Ja’Quan McMillian went undrafted because teams didn’t view him as an outside corner “Yes, that’s a good question. It’s a great question. We can think of just a long line of players that have all these other things that are important to playing well. He’s playing at a real high level now. So his instincts, all those things that you’re looking for, especially within the framework of our defense. A lot of times you say, ‘Who’s the nickel? What type of structure do they run?’ You’ve seen some bigger Buffalo nickel teams of late, but each defense has a certain thing they’re looking for. The ball kind of finds him. That’s a good trait. He endears himself to his teammates too, so he’s a great get.” On what he’s seen from QB Bo Nix’s mindset this week “Just queue Monday’s presser, queue Wednesday’s presser and we’ll go to Friday. I think all of us feel like we have to be moving in that forward needle.” On if he saw what he wanted from RB Jonah Coleman this week “Oh yes.” On the skills third-down backs have to balance with catching the ball and pass protection “It’s a great question because you want to make sure it’s not one or the other. A lot of it depends on who they might be blocking. I remember the old 49ers teams, [ILB Patrick] Willis and [ILB Navarro] Bowman. [Former Saints RB] Sproles was our third-down, two-minute back. We never wanted that matchup. There was one two-minute play where he ended up on one of the two of them, and he was fantastic, but if I asked him to do that twice, it would’ve been hard. We consider all of that as to not only third down, but drop back. That’s a real big self-scout thing, if [RB] RJ [Harvey] is in, if [RB] J.K. [Dobbins] is in. Whoever the back is in, we have to pay attention there.” On how RB RJ Harvey has performed “He’s made some big plays for us, screens. [Offensive Coordinator] Davis [Webb] just pulled up last week… He’s instinctive. I like his progress for early part of Year 2.” On if the Cardinals present more defensive fronts “Our defense, we see a base-look, kind of an Okie structure. There’ll be some similarities. Then they have a nickel package, a dime. Their…

title: Scouting the Enemy: Arizona Cardinals
summary: The Denver Broncos will finish up their slate of NFC West games on Sunday when they head on the road to face the Arizona Cardinals. The Cardinals are 2-4 entering this matchup, but are coming off an impressive Week 6 win against the Los Angeles Rams. Here ia deeper look at Denver’s Week 7 opponent. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals warms up before a game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos will finish up their slate of NFC West games on Sunday when they head on the road to face the Arizona Cardinals. The Cardinals are 2-4 entering this matchup, but are coming off an impressive Week 6 win against the Los Angeles Rams. Here ia deeper look at Denver’s Week 7 opponent. 2025 Arizona Cardinals Regular Season Review The Cardinals finished their 2025 regular season with 3-14 record and were last place in the NFC West. That led to the firing of Head Coach Jonathan Gannon after three seasons with the team. He was replaced by Mike LaFleur. 2026 Arizona Cardinals Offseason Additions and Departures When coaching regimes change, rosters also change. The Cardinals made a lot of moves this past off-season and are clearly trying to establish a different culture and identity. On offense, there were two significant departures. They moved on from quarterback Kyler Murray and recently traded wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. On defense, they parted ways with defensive linemen Dalvin Tomlinson and Bilal Nichols and linebacker Akeem-Davis Gaither. In free agency, they signed Gardner Minshew to be Jacoby Brissett’s backup. They revamped their receiving corps adding Kendrick Bourne, Devin Duvernay, and Simi Fehoko. Tyler Allgeier was a big signing to bolster their ground game, and they added several starters to their offensive and defensive trenches. In the 2026 NFL Draft, the Cardinals took Notre Dame standout Jeremiyah Love to help be a foundational piece of their offense. In the second round, the drafted Texas A&M guard Chase Bisontis. Unfortunately, he tore his MCL in the preseason and is out for the year. Georgia quarterback Carson Beck was their third round selection. Overall, they haven’t had a big impact from their rookie class . Offensive X-Factor: Tight end Trey McBride The focal point of the Cardinals passing attack is fifth-year tight end Trey McBride . He is one of the NFL’s best tight ends. I feel he is easily the biggest X-Factor for Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and his players to try to combat on Sunday. McBride is coming off a remarkable 2025 season where he had 126 catches, 1,239 receiving yards, and 11 touchdowns. That incredible production earned him first-team All-Pro honors. This season, he leads the NFL with 49 catches in six games. However, his decline in yards per catch is drastic, with just 361 yards on those receptions with 3 touchdowns. For the most part, Denver’s defense has done quite well limiting the top receiving option for opposing teams through six games. In order to win on Sunday, they can’t let McBride have a big game. He will be targeted often and has a penchant for moving the chains on third down. Limit his impact and things should look good for the Broncos. Defensive X-Factor: Defensive back Budda Baker The Cardinals have struggled on defense this season. However, one player in particular stands out above the rest on their roster. That’s defensive back Budda Baker. Since being selected in the second-round of the 2017 NFL Draft, Baker has been a mainstay in the Cardinals’ defensive backfield. He is an eight-time Pro Bowler and a four-time All-Pro. Some of the best seasons of his career were when Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph was calling the shots for their defense. A decade later, Baker continues to be an impact player for their defense due to his versatility. In his tenth season , Baker already has 42 tackles, 4 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 5 quarterback hits, and 1 interception. He is a do-it-all player that can make a huge impact in Sunday’s matchup. The Cardinals run a lot of Cover 3 looks and he has a nose for the football. Despite his size, he is quite tenacious in run support and does well executing his run fits. In pass coverage, the veteran defensive back has taken a bit of a step back this year. While he has allowed just 13 of 25 targets in his direction to be completed (52-percent), those completions have gone for 197 yards three of those have been touchdowns. Even so, I still think he is the player Bo Nix and the offense needs to be the most cognizant about. He has had a remarkable career and has made a lot of big plays. Denver can’t let that happen on Sunday. How the Broncos can achieve a victory over the Cardinals Like most of Denver’s wins this season, they are going to need a great performance from their defense. The Broncos will need to dial up the heat and put pressure on Jacoby Brissett. I think Zach Allen is poised for a big game returning home to face the team who drafted him, and believe Jonathon Cooper can make a difference at edge rusher. On offense, Denver needs Bo Nix to finally play a good game. Let’s see the aerial attack finally take flight. But in my opinion, this is a prime opportunity for their rushing offense to get going. The Cardinals are one of the worst defending the run. It’s time for Denver to run the ball with authority. That would help their offense significantly. Hart’s Prediction: Broncos 27, Cardinals 16.
