full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - OCTOBER 04: Jacksonville Jaguars offensive tackle Anton Harrison (77) jogs off the field before the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Per a recent report from NFL insider Ian Rapoport, Jacksonville Jaguars starting left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season with a torn ACL. The torn ACL was reportedly revealed during his Thursday surgery. #Jaguars starting LT Anton Harrison was revealed to have suffered a torn ACL during his surgery yesterday, sources say. The hope was just an arthroscopic procedure, but instead there was more damage. Harrison, who is already on Injured Reserve, is now out for the season. pic.twitter.com/YFtVWYMOlq — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 23, 2026 Harrison was carted off the field at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in the third quarter of the improbable, 19-17 Week 5 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. He was subsequently placed on IR, with the hope of it just being a three to five week recovery. Contingency Plan In Motion While many in the Jacksonville fanbase have been quick to label reserve offensive lineman, Walker Little as an offseason (and in-season) trade piece, the reported news of Harrison’s loss shows exactly why Little has major value on this roster: as a stand-in at both tackle and guard spots. After stepping into the left tackle role for the final quarter against Philadelphia, giving up zero quarterback pressures, Little surrendered just two pressures in Week 6 to the Houston Texans dominant defensive front. The team will need that continued level of play as they continue their playoff push moving forward. Jaguars Schedule Through November: Week 8: Indianapolis Colts (at home) Week 9: Baltimore Ravens (road) Week 10: Tennessee Titans (road) Week 11: New York Giants (road) Week 12: Tennessee Titans (at home) With this upcoming slate after the bye week, Jacksonville may be able to weather the early storm, while allowing Walker Little additional time to acclimate next to Emmanuel Pregnon. Notably, the team has Wyatt Milum and Daniel Faalele as additional options to step in as the sixth offensive lineman or new swing guard and tackle. Impact on Scheme, Negotiations? Before this injury, Harrison had missed just three games in his first three NFL seasons since being drafted 27th overall out of Oklahoma in 2023. The Jaguars recently picked up his fifth-year option in April, with the accompanying flip from right tackle to left. In terms of his contract negotiations, this injury clearly puts Harrison in an interesting spot also, as he was just settling in on the left side, with a few up and down performances. While Jacksonville may be one of the better positioned teams to take on the loss of their left tackle, it clearly is a significant loss that will change how they run their offense. For instance, Harrison, in 2025 and 2026 has routinely been left on an island, which allows the Jaguars to play with more receiving options in the field on passing plays. With Walker little sliding in at left tackle, the Jaguars will, presumably, be more prone to providing chips and double teams to both Little and a rebounding Cole Van Lanen at right tackle. This could result in fans seeing more offensive sub-packages, with the team likely leaning into more two tight end sets, 13 personnel, and jumbo packages to slow down the rush. Only time will tell, however. Jags just had 412 yards of offense and scored 31 points in his first start btw lol https://t.co/PxtS5ex43Y — The Notorious D.R.E. (@DreDay911) October 23, 2026 With Anton Harrison out for the season, how are you feeling about the remaining schedule, Duval? Have the last two games improved your Walker Little reservations? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

title: Chiefs sign WR Andrew Armstrong to the 53-man roster; will elevate RB Jadyn Ott for Sunday
summary: In the midst of wide receiver injuries, the Kansas City Chiefs elevated Andrew Armstrong from the practice squad for Week 6’s contest against the Los Angeles Chargers. Armstrong, a 2025 Miami Dolphins undrafted signing out of Arkansas, caught one pass for 13 yards in his NFL debut. Armstrong finished the game with 42 offensive snaps […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Andrew Armstrong #85 of the Kansas City Chiefs makes a catch against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of a preseason game at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the midst of wide receiver injuries, the Kansas City Chiefs elevated Andrew Armstrong from the practice squad for Week 6’s contest against the Los Angeles Chargers . Armstrong, a 2025 Miami Dolphins undrafted signing out of Arkansas, caught one pass for 13 yards in his NFL debut. Armstrong finished the game with 42 offensive snaps played (while on the field for nine more plays on special teams). With starting wideout Rashee Rice set to miss his second consecutive game due to a hamstring, it was widely expected that Armstrong would again get the nod against the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football.” It turns out that won’t come via a second practice squad elevation. According to Friday’s NFL transactions report, Kansas City has signed Armstrong to the 53-man roster. Armstrong saw extensive action in Kansas City’s preseason and seemed a strong candidate to make the final roster. However, he was waived at the roster cut deadline and signed to the Chiefs’ practice squad the next day. An unexpected running back injury may have put some urgency on the roster shuffling. Third-string runner Brashard Smith reportedly injured his hamstring in Thursday’s practice. According to head coach Andy Reid, Smith will be ruled out for Sunday. Reid also confirmed that rookie running back Jadyn Ott will be elevated from the practice squad to be available on Sunday night. Ott joined the Chiefs as an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma following April’s NFL Draft. He played for current Chiefs running backs coach DeMarco Murray with the Sooners. Sunday will mark Ott’s NFL debut. Taking Armstrong’s place on the practice squad will be a running back reinforcement in Nate Carter. Carter had been on Kansas City’s practice squad all season, but he was cut on Wednesday when linebacker Aiden Fisher was added. Carter recorded nine carries for 60 yards in 2025 with the Atlanta Falcons . After cutting linebacker Cam Jones this week and officially placing tackle Josh Simmons on the Reserve/Injured (IR) list Thursday, the Chiefs technically have an open spot on the 53-man roster even after promoting Armstrong. However, linebacker Cooper McDonald is widely expected to be activated from IR on Saturday to allow him to suit up in Seattle. McDonald suffered a knee injury in the Chiefs’ Week 1 contest against the Denver Broncos and was designated to return earlier this week.

title: Chiefs Madden Simulation Week 7: Sunday Night vs. the defending champions

full_text: On Sunday, the (5-0) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road to play the Seattle Seahawks to take on the reigning Super Bowl Champions, the (3-3) Seattle Seahawks. Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. Note: The Chiefs Madden Simulation has predicted five correct Chiefs victories. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here. First quarter The Kansas City Chiefs’ offense started hot as Patrick Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce on a 41-yard post route that flipped the field and put the Chiefs at the Seattle Seahawks’ 34-yard line. Mahomes then found Jalen Royals on a drag route for another first down. The drive would stall out, but Harrison Butker gave the Chiefs the first lead of the game with a field goal. Sam Darnold tried to replicate what Mahomes did on the opening drive, throwing a deep ball to Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 37-yard gain before the receiver was forced out of bounds. The Seahawks’ drive would also stall out, giving Jason Myers a field goal attempt. The attempt was no good. Kenneth Walker got revenge on his former team by finding the end zone for the first touchdown of the game. End of first quarter: Chiefs 10, Seahawks 0 Second quarter The Seahawks opened the quarter with a punt. Mahomes found Xavier Worthy for an 18-yard gain on third down to keep the drive alive and move the ball to the Chiefs’ 41-yard line. Walker put the Chiefs across midfield with a screen pass to the Seahawks’ 45-yard line. Kelce then picked up a third-down conversion to move the ball to the 29-yard line. On the next play, Kelce surpassed the 100-yard mark and brought the Chiefs to the 8-yard line. Noah Gray capped off the drive with an 8-yard touchdown reception on a hard flat route into the end zone. A.J. Barner helped the Seahawks cross midfield as the two-minute warning approached. Smith-Njigba recorded his third catch of the game and picked up a first down. Rasheed Shaheed then caught a deep crossing route in stride before being tackled at the 1-yard line. The Chiefs’ defense stood tall with the Seahawks backed up near the end zone, holding them to a field goal and giving Mahomes 36 seconds to work with before halftime. End of second quarter: Chiefs 17, Seahawks 3 Third quarter The Seahawks opened the second half with a drive that reached the Chiefs’ 28-yard line before they settled for a field goal, cutting the deficit to 11 points. Mahomes did his best Michael Jordan impersonation, completing a pass to Xavier Worthy for a 15-yard gain. Worthy then caught a pass on a hard flat for 10 yards, converting a crucial fourth-and-2 at the Seahawks’ 40-yard line. Justin Watson capped off the 13-play drive with a touchdown, giving the Chiefs a commanding lead. End of third quarter: Chiefs 24, Seahawks 6 Fourth quarter Sam Darnold picked up a first down with his legs on fourth-and-3 to keep the Seahawks’ drive alive. Tory Horton then caught an 11-yard slant to move Seattle to the Chiefs’ 18-yard line with five minutes remaining. On their second attempt to convert a fourth-and-3, the Seahawks tried to connect with running back Emanuel Wilson on a Texas route. However, Nick Bolton blew up the play to force a turnover on downs and help seal the Chiefs’ victory. End of the fourth quarter: Chiefs 24, Seahawks 6 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 25 for 35 passing, 295 yards, 2 touchdowns, 2 rushing attempts, 14 yards. Kenneth Walker: 7 rushing attempts, 21 yards, 1 touchdown, 2 receptions. 14 yards Emmett Johnson: 3 rushing attempts, 15 yards; 2 receptions, 8 yards. Travis Kelce: 8 receptions, 135 yards. Xavier Worthy: 7 receptions, 85 yards. Cyrus Allen: 3 receptions, 30 yards. Chris Jones: 2 tackles for loss. Nick Bolton: 7 tackles, 1 tackle for loss. Sam Darnold: 17 for 32 passing, 200 yards. Emanuel Wilson: 7 rushing attempts, 26 yards. Jaxon Smith-Njigba: 6 receptions, 82 yards. A.J. Barner: 3 receptions, 33 yards. Rashid Shaheed: 3 receptions, 55 yards. Next week, the Chiefs travel to Mile High to take on the Denver Broncos, whom they beat back in Week 1. Until then, we will see how it is played out inside the EA Universe.

title: Chiefs-Seahawks Week 7 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
summary: It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Seattle Seahawks, our writers predicted the final score and result. The 3-3 Seahawks have not found an easy time defending their Super Bowl title and will be coming off of consecutive losses. […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Seattle Seahawks , our writers predicted the final score and result. The 3-3 Seahawks have not found an easy time defending their Super Bowl title and will be coming off of consecutive losses. Because their 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 6 came on “Thursday Night Football,” Seattle will have a rest advantage in the contest. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists Seattle as 2.5-point home favorites. When last on the field, the Chiefs defeated the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6 by a 22-6 margin that felt much less satisfying than the score should indicate. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) When the schedule was released, I was very confident I would be predicting a Chiefs loss in Seattle. However, the Seahawks have not exactly looked dominant past the first two weeks of the season. I believe in the Kenneth Walker revenge factor. I also trust Steve Spagnuolo to have a defensive plan to stop an offense that increasingly depends only on one player — even if Jaxon Smith-Njigba may currently be the league’s best wide receiver. Seattle’s modest rest advantage could easily be a factor, and I am expecting a close, somewhat ugly game no matter who comes on top. Chiefs 20, Seahawks 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) In this heavyweight matchup, the Chiefs will face their first true test of the season on the road against the defending champion Seahawks. The Seahawks offense may have taken a step back with Kenneth Walker now on the Chiefs, but the Chiefs will still have to account for Jaxon Smith-Njigba, which should set up for an entertaining matchup. Chiefs corners Nohl Williams and Mansoor Delane have sparkled so far, but Smith-Njigba will be their toughest test yet. It will be interesting to see if Steve Spagnuolo allows his young corners to play one-on-one or if they choose to bracket and double-cover him. If the Chiefs can stop him, they will take away the rest of the Seahawks’ offense. The Seattle defense is still formidable, and it has been well publicized this week about Walker’s 100-yard streak and the Seahawks’ streak of not allowing 100 yards rushing. That being said, this feels like a week when the Chiefs’ screen game and running backs in the passing game could be a factor due to offensive line issues headed into the game. Chiefs 20, Seahawks 17 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I think Seattle has a legitimate chance to knock off Kansas City because of how physical they are on both sides of the ball. The Seahawks have the type of defense that can make life difficult for Patrick Mahomes, especially if they’re able to generate pressure without having to blitz. I also think Seattle can control the tempo offensively and keep Mahomes on the sideline by establishing the run. Ultimately, I expect a close game, but I like Seattle to make a few more plays down the stretch and pull off the win. Seahawks 23, Chiefs 20 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The defending Super Bowl champions have dropped three of their last four games, with Sam Darnold throwing seven interceptions since returning from injury. But Seattle’s defense leads the NFL in yards allowed, making this a serious test for Kansas City. Defensively, the Chiefs’ priority should be containing Jaxon Smith-Njigba and forcing Darnold to look elsewhere. I trust Kansas City’s outside cornerbacks to compete, but Smith-Njigba’s opportunities from the slot concern me. Giving him extra attention while collapsing the pocket around Darnold could create the turnovers the Chiefs need to swing this game. Seattle’s defense presents its own problems, especially if Jaylon Moore’s concussion leaves Kansas City shorthanded at tackle. Thankfully, Kenneth Walker III is on the Chiefs’ side this time. Kansas City needs to stay committed to him, even if the yards come hard early. If Seattle loads up to stop its former running back, Patrick Mahomes must capitalize on the opportunities that creates through play-action. I expect a physical, close game, but I trust Mahomes to make the decisive plays and the Chiefs’ defense to force a costly mistake. Chiefs 24, Seahawks 17. Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Could this be the biggest challenge of the young season? The reigning champs vs the interrupted dynasty. Ken Walker vs the team that let him go. JSN vs the Chiefs young secondary. I believe in the balance of this Kansas City squad– they can run, stop the run, and frustrate an opponent’s passing game. Patrick Mahomes has the best opportunity in years not only to win, but to prove he can elevate the play of his receivers. They’re unlikely to go undefeated, but I don’t think I can pick against Andy and Patrick this week. Chiefs 31, Seahawks 27 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) This one is tough. I could see this one being the Chiefs’ first loss. Seattle has the best defense in the league, and they’ll be motivated against their former teammate (and league MVP) Kenneth Walker. Seattle is a tough place to play and the Seahawks are more rested as they’re coming off their mini bye. I think the Chiefs lack of a pass rush will also be a problem and JSN could continue his consecutive OPOY campaign. I don’t see the Chiefs going into the Thanksgiving game against the Bills with a 10-0 record. I think this is our one slip-up before that game. It doesn’t feel good, but I’ll take the Seahawks in a close one this week. Seahawks 28, Chiefs 24 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) This game is Kansas City’s chance to show the world they are capable of beating a legitimately good team. The problem is, the Seahawks offense has not been good this year. They basically have wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba — and that’s it. This will, however, be the biggest test the Chiefs’ offensive line has faced all year. Whether KC wins or loses will depend on how well the Chiefs’ line holds up. Look for Andy Reid to mix in a lot of the run and chip blocks to help out his big guys up front. This game will be labeled the Kenneth Walker III revenge game, but that’s only because they are going to feed him the rock out of necessity. Chiefs 24, Seahawks 17 Nate Christensen This is a fascinating test for the Chiefs on both sides of the ball. The Chiefs’ run game has powered them all year, but now they are going up against a dominant run defense. It’s a good test to see if the Chiefs run game holds up against elite competition. On defense, it’s a good test for the Chiefs pass rush. Denver got to Sam Darnold often and affected his internal clock. Can the Chiefs do the same? I’m expecting a low-scoring game with both defenses controlling the game. Seattle has the better defense and are at home after a mini bye, so I give them a slight advantage. Seahawks 17, Chiefs 13 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) This feels like the perfect recipe for the Chiefs’ first loss of the season. Even if the offense wasn’t down its No. 1 wide receiver and starting right tackle, it feels like a good spot for the defending Super Bowl champions to get right in front of the home fans. Running back Kenneth Walker is returning to Seattle, and I’m not sure which side that benefits more. There’s reason to believe the offense’s limitations will allow the defense to feel comfortable keying on him and letting Kansas City’s pass catchers beat them. I’m not sure the current version of the Chiefs’ offense is ready for this matchup. They’ll have growing pains to learn from on Sunday night. Linebackers Chazz Surratt (calf) and Drake Thomas (ankle) will not play ; Surratt has mainly been a special-teams player this year, but Thomas has the third-most tackles on the team and was impactful alongside middle linebacker Ernest Jones. Starting outside linebacker Uchenne Nwosu (hip) is questionable after popping up on Thursday’s injury report as a limited participant after not appearing on Wednesday’s list. full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs will face their toughest test of the young season as they travel for a Sunday night matchup against the defending Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks . Kansas City remains undefeated at 5-0, while Seattle is 3-3 after two straight losses, but the record doesn’t tell the whole story. The Seahawks possess the NFL’s top-ranked defense and remain especially difficult to beat at Lumen Field. The game will also mark Kenneth Walker III’s first return to Seattle after helping the Seahawks win last season’s Super Bowl. Walker now leads the league in rushing and has transformed a Chiefs offense that struggled to run the ball consistently a year ago. Here are three keys to a Chiefs victory in Week 7. Offensive key: Stay committed to Kenneth Walker III Seattle enters the matchup ranked first in total defense, allowing only 237.3 yards per game. The Seahawks are particularly dominant against the pass, surrendering a league-low 141.3 passing yards per game. They also allow only 96 rushing yards per game and haven’t allowed a 100-yard rusher since October 2024. Those numbers make this a strength-on-strength matchup. Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, 6.3 yards per attempt and 133 rushing yards per game. He also leads the league with 52 broken tackles and has produced seven runs of at least 20 yards. He continued his outstanding start against the Chargers, rushing for 128 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries. Now he returns to face the team he won a championship against less than a year ago. The Chiefs cannot let Seattle’s early success on the run push them away from Walker. Some carries may produce only two or three yards, but Andy Reid must remain patient. Keeping Walker involved will prevent Seattle from making Kansas City one-dimensional. It can also slow the pass rush, create manageable third downs and open opportunities for Patrick Mahomes in the play-action passing game. Establishing the run will be particularly important at Lumen Field. Long, sustained drives can quiet the crowd and keep Seattle’s defense from attacking Kansas City’s offensive line in obvious passing situations. The Chiefs do not necessarily need Walker to extend his streak of 100-yard performances. Seattle has not allowed an individual runner to reach that mark in two years. However, Kansas City should aim to finish with at least 100 rushing yards. Even if explosive runs aren’t immediately available, Walker must remain central to the offensive plan. Defensive key: Contain Jaxon Smith-Njigba The Seahawks have several capable offensive players, but it all starts with Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Through six games, Smith-Njigba is averaging approximately 11 targets, 8.2 receptions and 120 receiving yards per game. His estimated 35.6% target share leads the NFL, demonstrating how heavily Seattle’s passing attack depends on him. The Chiefs are unlikely to completely stop Smith-Njigba. The objective should be to contain him, prevent explosive receptions and force Sam Darnold to consistently find his secondary options. Kansas City should feel comfortable allowing its outside cornerbacks to challenge Smith-Njigba when he lines up on the perimeter. The more difficult assignment will come when Seattle moves him into the slot, where he can avoid press coverage and find favorable matchups against safeties and linebackers. Steve Spagnuolo will need to vary his coverages. That could mean bracketing Smith-Njigba on important downs, rotating a safety toward him after the snap, or using zone coverage to keep multiple defenders between him and the end zone. The priority is preventing one reception from changing the game. Smith-Njigba has the speed and route-running ability to turn a small opening into an explosive play. Kansas City should force Seattle to sustain long drives instead. The defensive benchmark should be to keep Smith-Njigba under 100 receiving yards and prevent him from catching a 30-yard or longer pass. If the Chiefs can accomplish that, Darnold will have to prove he can patiently work through his progressions and win by distributing the ball elsewhere. X-factor: Win the turnover battle Darnold helped lead Seattle to a championship last season, but he has struggled since returning to the starting lineup. He enters Sunday night with 60.4% completion, 1,033 yards, seven touchdowns, and seven interceptions. His 77.4 passer rating reflects an offense that has become inconsistent and far too dependent on Smith-Njigba. Darnold has also been sacked 14 times. He threw two interceptions during Seattle’s overtime loss to Denver, including mistakes on two of the Seahawks’ final three possessions. When pressured or forced to play from behind, Darnold has given opposing defenses opportunities. Kansas City’s pass rush finally converted its pressure into production against Los Angeles. The Chiefs recorded four sacks after going three consecutive games without one. Chris Jones, George Karlaftis, Ashton Gillotte, Peter Woods, and Chamarri Conner all helped bring down Justin Herbert. Karlaftis has been especially disruptive, generating 19 pressures across his last two games. The Chiefs should not have to blitz Darnold on every passing down. Spagnuolo can use simulated pressure and late coverage rotations to make Darnold believe pressure is coming before dropping defenders into his passing lanes. Kansas City must also protect the football on offense. Mahomes threw an interception against the Chargers, giving him three this season. Seattle’s defense is too talented for the Chiefs to give it short fields and extra possessions. The goal should be to force at least two takeaways while committing no more than one turnover. Winning that margin would prevent Seattle’s defense and home crowd from controlling the game. The bottom line The Chiefs don’t need to abandon the identity that has carried them to an undefeated start just because they are facing the NFL’s top-ranked defense. Kansas City must remain committed to Kenneth Walker, even if Seattle limits him early. Defensively, the Chiefs need to contain Jaxon Smith-Njigba, prevent explosive plays and force Sam Darnold to rely on his other weapons. Most importantly, they must pressure Darnold into mistakes without giving Seattle similar opportunities on the other side. If the Chiefs reach 100 rushing yards, keep Smith-Njigba under 100 receiving yards, and win the turnover battle, they will have an excellent chance to defeat the defending champions, remain undefeated, and leave Seattle with their most impressive win of the season.
author: Maurice Elston

title: Dave Merritt sees Nohl Williams as one of the NFL’s top corners
summary: One of the biggest reasons the Kansas City Chiefs have gotten off to a 5-0 start to the season is that they boast the ninth-ranked pass defense in the NFL. Arguably the biggest contributor to the secondary’s impressive start has been second-year cornerback Nohl Williams, one of the best cornerbacks in man coverage this season. […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the biggest reasons the Kansas City Chiefs have gotten off to a 5-0 start to the season is that they boast the ninth-ranked pass defense in the NFL. Arguably the biggest contributor to the secondary’s impressive start has been second-year cornerback Nohl Williams, one of the best cornerbacks in man coverage this season. Lowest comp pct allowed in man coverage this season among CB (min 5 targets) Nohl Williams 0.0% Josh Wallace 16.7% Travis Hunter 25.0% Pat Surtain 25.0% Christian Gonzalez 27.3% pic.twitter.com/CGdDhZhEub — PFF (@PFF) October 14, 2026 The former third-round pick was a standout defender at California before the Chiefs selected him in the 2025 draft, where he led the nation with seven interceptions . Williams had a solid rookie campaign for Kansas City in 2025, but he’s taken his game to another level in 2026.` Speaking to the media on Thursday, Chiefs defensive backs coach Dave Merritt praised his second-year defensive back, saying Williams is becoming one of the best cornerbacks in the league. “I think where he’s trending to is, in my opinion, he’s one of the better corners in the league right now.” It’s not just the Chiefs coaching staff who have taken notice of Williams’ coming-out party; the other players in the secondary have too, including veteran L’Jarius Sneed. “That young man, we were just praising him yesterday,” explained Merritt. “And he doesn’t receive that too well in the sense that LJ, myself, and a couple other guys were just saying, ‘Boy, you’re really playing really good football,’ and Nohl kind of always just shut that down because he remembers his M.E.s (mental errors). He remembers some bad plays, but we’re saying you’ve made enough good plays that have helped us win.” Merritt didn’t stop the praise for Williams there. “I think that he’s playing at a high, high level,” Merritt continued. “I think they did away with the Pro Bowl, but still, I think he’s playing at an All-Star level right now. So, if he can continue to do that and come up with some more plays for us that can excite and wow the crowd, I think it’s going to be good for his future.” #Chiefs DBs Coach Dave Merritt describes how he's seen CB Nohl Williams improve. pic.twitter.com/S6P1SrYx6M — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) October 22, 2026 Williams’ next test comes this Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks . It will be interesting to see how much the Chiefs line up Williams against Seattle’s star wide receiver Jackson Smith-Njigba, who already has 717 receiving yards on the season . Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo said JSN was “elite, really elite” during his press conference on Thursday. Seattle’s next two receiving options, Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed, haven’t matched Njigba’s statistical success, but both can break off a big play at any time. But something tells me Williams will be up to the job.

title: The Josh Simmons saga is a really big deal for the Chiefs
summary: I don’t know what’s going on. That’s my take. It’s bad for this format, but sometimes it’s okay to acknowledge the truth: I. Don’t. Know. Maybe it’s as simple as Josh Simmons’ back isn’t responding to treatment as well as the Kansas City Chiefs had hoped. Maybe it’s something more. I don’t know. We might […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) I don’t know what’s going on. That’s my take. It’s bad for this format, but sometimes it’s okay to acknowledge the truth: I. Don’t. Know. Maybe it’s as simple as Josh Simmons’ back isn’t responding to treatment as well as the Kansas City Chiefs had hoped. Maybe it’s something more. I don’t know. We might never know. Rick Burkholder full statement today: "Alright, I want to talk about Josh Simmons & give you a little timeline here. On August 17, Josh came to me with calf discomfort and feeling that he couldn't post on a single leg in training camp practices. This was the same leg he had… — Brandon Kiley (@BKSportsTalk) October 22, 2026 Can we set the off-field drama and speculation aside for a moment and discuss this from a pure football perspective? I think the on-field ramifications have been lost in the discussion. This is a really big deal for the Chiefs. A year ago, it felt like the Chiefs had finally solved the left tackle position for the next decade. That was no small feat, given the revolving door of players they’ve tried at the position since 2021. That date matters because it marks the year the Chiefs moved on from longtime starter Eric Fisher. The following players have taken snaps at left tackle for the Chiefs in the five-plus years since Fisher’s release: Orlando Brown Jr., Joe Thuney, Prince Tega Wanogho, Wanya Morris, Jawaan Taylor, Kingsley Suamataia, D.J. Humphries, Josh Simmons, Jaylon Moore, Esa Pole and Kahlil Benson. That’s 11 different players taking snaps over a 5+ year stretch. It’s not what you want. Simmons was supposed to end this cycle, which felt endless. He was a ‘set it and forget it’ type of player. His talent was so immense and obvious that even an old-school Andy Reid didn’t try to manufacture a position battle between Simmons and a veteran at training camp. It was Simmons’ job, and there would be no looking back. That is, until everything changed. You’re familiar with the story, but just to rehash some of the specifics: Simmons reportedly left the team the night before the Detroit Lions game last season, ultimately missing the next four games. The absence has been often discussed among Chiefs fans, but it could have been an afterthought in his career if all went according to plan in years to come. It very much has not. We now know Simmons reported calf discomfort to the training staff on August 17. He was evaluated, and the medical staff was able to diagnose him with a herniated, bulging disc in his back. It’s never great to hear that a big guy has a back issue, but the team seemed to believe he could play sooner rather than later with treatment. Simmons tried treatment, attempted to ramp back up with a return-to-play protocol, and, according to the team, plateaued in his progress. This whole thing doesn’t pass the smell test, yet again. You don’t do that on a Wednesday coming off a “ramp up” week where you practice every day and the wording has been that he’s going to continue that process. I do not know anything but this screams of the team expecting him… — Mitchell Schwartz (@MitchSchwartz71) October 22, 2026 He’s now on injured reserve. It’s hard to say with any level of confidence he’ll play again this season. I can’t say with any level of confidence that I think he’ll play again for the Chiefs. That’s veering into speculation. Back to what we know. This sucks. It’s unfortunate, because the Chiefs felt they had an answer at one of the most valuable positions on the offense. Simmons was expected to be a building block for years to come. That position is once again in flux. For those who take the team at their word, the franchise left tackle now has a back issue which could keep him out for months. For those that don’t, well, this is now the second unexplained absence for the franchise left tackle. No matter your view, it’s a problem. The Chiefs are rolling with Kahlil Benson. He’s been better than anyone could have reasonably expected. He’ll be put to the test this weekend against Mike MacDonald and the Seattle Seahawks ’ defense in a night game on the road. Maybe he can be the long-term answer at the position. Maybe not. He’s at least capable of solidifying the position for the here and now, which is more than the Chiefs have been able to say in quite some time. I pray we’ll soon be able to talk about Josh Simmons the football player again and not Josh Simmons the enigma. Today is not that day. The saga rolls on. Next man up.
author: Brandon Kiley

full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs defense has been a sound unit, whether you look at the top-5 mark in points allowed or the reliable tackling it shows every week. Six players are tied for the team lead in sacks with one. However, defensive end George Karlaftis (13) has more than 3x the quarterback hits of the second-place defender, Felix Anudike-Uzomah (4). He has been one of the unit’s most valuable players this year. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news How George Karlaftis leads the Chiefs’ defense — even without racking up sacks | The Athletic “He’s making plays — really smart plays, too — all across the field,” Gillotte told The Athletic . In this instance, Gillotte said, Karlaftis read his keys correctly. He trusted his film study during the week and leaned on coaching pointers he’d received from defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo and defensive line coach Joe Cullen. “You know what you’re going to get on pass rush. He’s relentless,” Gillotte said. “And he wins. You can rally around people like that.” Kenneth Walker III is thriving with Chiefs. Why did the Seahawks let him go? | ESPN “I’ll just say, I love Ken,” Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Wednesday when asked if he has any second thoughts about Seattle letting Walker leave. “I thoroughly enjoyed him being on our football team. We’ve had some great one-on-one conversations. I thought we had a great relationship. I respect the heck out of him. … But I think there’s mixed emotions in terms of, you’re happy for him, but also, we’re trying to figure out ways to stop this guy, too, because he’s playing at a really high level.” Even some clarity about Chiefs’ Josh Simmons punctuates the enigma that he is | The Kansas City Star As much as player safety and health has to be a prime directive, the Chiefs, of course, also would like to return to full function with the help of Simmons — a player whose talents are such that he could be not just a pillar of their line, but of their future. Yes, they’re 5-0 entering their Sunday night contest at reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle (3-3), a game that represents the start of a scheduling, well, ramp-up. With Simmons still back on the ramp, largely remaining — to borrow from Winston Churchill — a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside an enigma. Kansas City Chiefs have a 53-man roster spot to fill after latest Josh Simmons news, and a move to reward a player makes the most sense | A to Z Sports Chiefs wide receiver Andrew Armstrong is the player deserving of a spot on the 53-man roster After Week 6’s win over the Los Angeles Chargers, it became clear that wide receiver Andrew Armstrong deserves a larger role. Armstrong entered that game as a practice squad player who hadn’t appeared in a regular season game. He left it with his first career catch, a 13-yard reception, and the third-most offensive snaps among Kansas City’s wide receivers. Only starting wide receiver Xavier Worthy and second-year wide receiver Jalen Royals played more offensive snaps at the position. Chiefs DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones take on different kind of ‘line’ duty | KSHB 41 Kansas City Chiefs defensive end George Karlaftis and defensive tackle Chris Jones traded their defensive line responsibilities for a different kind of “line” work when they served as line judges at a recent Shawnee Mission East volleyball match against rival Shawnee Mission South. Jones said he was happy to support the event’s cause despite not being aware of his line-judging duties. “I didn’t know I was gonna be a line judge, so that was a curveball,” Jones joked. “But it’s pretty exciting.” Around the NFL Baker Mayfield says thumb ‘strong enough to be able to play’ for Buccaneers vs. Panthers | NFL.com “Feel good. Just improving,” Mayfield said. “It’s been a process for me. Never really missed time cause of injury. Not fun. You always want to be out there with the guys. … It’s been feeling slowly better and better. That’s the frustrating part, it just takes time for an injury like that.” Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles hasn’t yet confirmed Mayfield will play against the Panthers, and offensive coordinator Zac Robinson told reporters they’re prepared for Mayfield or backup Jalon Daniels to fill the job Sunday, but it seems as if Mayfield is trending toward being available. He was a full participant in practice for the second straight day on Thursday. Ben Johnson originally called a punt, but Cairo Santos asked to try a 58-yard field goal | Pro Football Talk “I was right next to HT and Ben originally called a punt, and then the injury allowed us to talk about it. I was talking to HT that I felt good about it,” Santos said. “Ben asked, ‘Does he want it?’ And I heard it and I told HT I want it and he said, ‘Ben, Cairo says he wants it.’ Thankful that Ben trusted me on that, and I delivered a great kick right down the middle.” Rare NFL penalty: Bears become first team in 16 years to get flagged for illegal forward handoff | CBS Sports On the play, Caleb Williams took the snap and immediately handed the ball off to guard Joe Thuney. This was a trick play by the Bears and not only did it NOT work, but they lost five yards after the officiating crew threw a flag. The reason you don’t see offensive linemen get more handoffs is because in most instances, it’s against the rules. As the NFL rule book clearly states, “except where permitted by rule, handing the ball forward to a teammate is illegal.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Patrick Mahomes praises rookie Cyrus Allen’s contested catches “And then the one down the middle was a big time catch in between a lot of traffic.“ “So that’s stuff we saw from him in training camp,” Mahomes continued. “I think now that he’s getting more and more comfortable within the offense, we’ll continue to give him more and more of a role within the offense.” Mahomes threw a third pass Allen’s way against the Chargers, and it helped move the chains. On second-and-6, a downfield, back-shoulder fade attempt to the rookie drew a defensive pass interference flag. full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 11: Offensive Coordinator Mike McDaniel of the Los Angeles Chargers looks on prior to the game against the Denver Broncos at SoFi Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 going into the bye week. While they haven’t made any changes to the coaching staff yet, it’s possible something is brewing down the line if the losses continue to pile up. In this week’s Reacts poll, I asked you all to vote for who has the hottest seat in the organization. With a runaway victory, it was offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who has failed to generate a group that can get on the same page when it comes to scoring points. He received 68 percent of the vote while general manager Joe Hortiz was next with a distant 17 percent. Head coach Jim Harbaugh clocked in at 15 percent, while strength coach Ben Herbert did not receive any votes. Last week, the confidence meter to determine whether the team is heading in the right direction, was at 10 percent. This week, that number has been chopped in half to 5 percent.

title: Chargers schedule doesn’t get much easier after the bye week
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are breathing a sigh of relief in Week 7 as they face their annual bye. The Chargers have struggled mightily this season, losing their first six games, but things don’t get much easier when they come back to the facility. Here’s a look at their first three games coming up after […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Chargers are breathing a sigh of relief in Week 7 as they face their annual bye. The Chargers have struggled mightily this season, losing their first six games, but things don’t get much easier when they come back to the facility. Here’s a look at their first three games coming up after the bye. Week 8 at Los Angeles Rams The Chargers won’t have to move very far for their next road game, as they visit the crosstown rival Rams at SoFi Stadium. The Rams have also dealt with their fair share of troubles this season, as they are off to a 2-4 start despite having high hopes of reaching the Super Bowl in their home stadium. That being said, the Rams still pose a massive threat, even with injuries across the board, thanks to high-level players like Myles Garrett and Davante Adams. The Rams should be favored in this one, and the Chargers will have to pull out all the stops to try and grab their first win. Week 9 vs. Houston Texans The Texans are another team that has struggled at the start of the season, but they have picked things up in recent weeks. Following a 0-4 start, they have won back-to-back games against the Tennessee Titans and Jacksonville Jaguars to climb back into a chance to reach the playoffs. The Texans have beaten the Chargers in four of their last five meetings, including last season in Week 17 at SoFi Stadium. This is a chance for revenge, but Houston will be ready to give them another test. Week 10 at Baltimore Ravens The Chargers will head back out on the road to face off against their former defensive coordinator, Jesse Minter, on Monday Night Football. The league probably didn’t expect the Chargers to be winless this close to the game. Otherwise, they might not have put it on Monday Night Football, but that’s the nature of the schedule. Facing off against Lamar Jackson on the road is never easy, but the Chargers will have to do their best to contain him in hopes of grabbing a win on the road. BFTB community, can the Chargers win any of these games? If so, which ones? Let us know in the comment section below.

full_text: After losing two consecutive home games in heart-breaking fashion, the 2-4 Los Angeles Rams head back on the road for Week 7. In a bit of relief from their wearisome early season travel schedule, L.A. will jaunt across the desert on Interstate 15 North into Nevada for a Sunday October 25 matinee matchup with the 3-3 Las Vegas Raiders. The Allegiant Stadium kickoff is set for 1:25 p.m. PDT. One of the two participants will get off the schneid this Sunday. The Rams are still stinging from their aforementioned losses, 18-16 to the Arizona Cardinals and 37-34 to the Buffalo Bills. The Raiders are themselves on a three week run of bad cards. Las Vegas rolled to three straight wins to open the season, but have since crapped out to the Bills 33-30, New England Patriots 45-17, and Kansas City Chiefs 30-27. If hung with another loss, either team could be at a crossroad. While both veteran quarterbacks, Matthew Stafford (Rams) and Kirk Cousins (Raiders), are off to good statistical starts, after a loss this Sunday there won’t be enough hot seats to go around. Each team has in place their heir apparent QB, Ty Simpson in L.A. and Fernando Mendoza in Las Vegas . Negative circumstances could demand a changing of the guard. Considering that the two teams have shared a coast, and even a metropolitan area, there isn’t a long history of head-to-head matchups. The series began in 1972 and is dead even at 8-8. Since Sean McVay took the Rams over in 2017, he has not lost took to the Raiders, boasting a 3-0 slate. Here’s how to follow the game! Location: Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nv. title: Nate Landman out for Rams vs. Raiders
summary: Nate Landman went on the injury report this week and now he’s officially out. It’s another blow to the Rams who seem to have their 2026 season falling apart. As the injuries and losses mount up, how can this team stay positive? A win on Sunday would go a long way, but with all the […]
full_text: Nate Landman went on the injury report this week and now he’s officially out. It’s another blow to the Rams who seem to have their 2026 season falling apart. As the injuries and losses mount up, how can this team stay positive? A win on Sunday would go a long way, but with all the injuries, a win may be a long shot. Puka Nacua’s status is up in the air. It was no sure thing that the Rams would play the playoffs this year, but it seems very likely, and now? It seems like a stretch as L.A. seems more likely to fall to 2-5 than 3-4. Injury Report, Week 7 at Raiders: Puka Nacua and Trent McDuffie questionable, Nate Landman ruled out (therams) “Nacua left Thursday’s practice early with the aforementioned calf injury. Head coach Sean McVay on Friday said Nacua “took part in a majority of the practice, left, (and then) got it checked out.” McVay also said that “I don’t think he (Nacua) knows exactly when it occurred.” However, McVay did characterize the injury as “minor.” “You look at it, and there’s just a little minor thing in there, and felt it where he wasn’t able to have some of the power and full explosion, and just kind of noticed it,” McVay said. “But I don’t think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it.” Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) is also listed as questionable. McDuffie did not practice all week. Meanwhile, inside linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) was ruled out, but is “making good progress,” McVay said. With Landman out, McVay confirmed Los Angeles will elevate inside linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad.“ Puka Nacua, Trent McDuffie questionable, Nate Landman ruled out for Week 7 (nbcsports) “McDuffie has registered seven passes defensed with an interception. The Rams will be without linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) on Sunday, as he’s been ruled out. The team will elevate veteran linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad to play in the game.“ Latest updates on Rams WR Puka Nacua’s calf injury (ramswire) “Already without Davante Adams for the next 6-10 weeks , losing Nacua for any amount of time will be a huge blow to the Rams offense. Terrance Ferguson is also on IR with an ankle injury, while the defense has lost plenty of playmakers, too. All eyes will be on Nacua’s status heading into Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders , as the Rams attempt to snap a two-game losing streak and avoid a dreaded 2-5 start to the season. We’ll be providing the latest updates on Nacua’s status below.“ Raiders vs. Rams Betting Pick: Back the Home Underdog (sp0rtsgrid) “The 2-4 Los Angeles Rams visit a Las Vegas Raiders team that has been a bettor’s delight. The Raiders covered against the Buffalo Bills last week after entering as 4.5-point underdogs. They trailed by 10 before scoring a late touchdown and losing by three. title: Rams could be reason Raiders turn to Fernando Mendoza
summary: Kirk Cousins leads the NFL in touchdown passes with 14, and started his career with the Las Vegas Raiders at 3-0, but the veteran signal caller is playing with fire amid a three-game losing streak. If the Raiders lose to the spiraling Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, the fans begging to see number one pick […]
full_text: Kirk Cousins leads the NFL in touchdown passes with 14, and started his career with the Las Vegas Raiders at 3-0, but the veteran signal caller is playing with fire amid a three-game losing streak. If the Raiders lose to the spiraling Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, the fans begging to see number one pick Fernando Mendoza take the reins could finally get their wish. It’s not necessarily because Cousins lost the job, but that he was always just keeping it warm for Mendoza. In fact, Cousins has played so well this season that Las Vegas should be able to flip him before the trade deadline for a draft pick. Perhaps on his way back to the Minnesota Vikings? The Las Vegas Raiders might have to make a tough decision heading into Week 7. https://t.co/LjdhJRguey — Raider Nation (@RaidersNationCP) October 21, 2026 That was one of the topics that came up in this weeks 5 Qs with Silver and Black Pride’s Matt Holder. I asked about the season that Cousins is having and what it means for Mendoza, and his answer pulled no punches: “At that point, it might be time to start thinking about 2027 and beyond because the team isn’t winning despite the 38-year-old quarterback playing well.” Under any other circumstances, the Raiders would be thanking their lucky stars for Cousins. The carousel has been a nightmare since Derek Carr was cut and went to the Saints. But despite his 14 touchdowns, Cousins is starting to just get in the way, it seems. Q: Is Kirk Cousins all the way back to being Kirk Cousins, or do you think he’s just had a nice setup so far and Fernando Mendoza will take over this season? A: Cousins has definitely played a lot better than I (and most people) expected. It helps that he has experience working with Klint Kubiak, since they spent three years together in Minnesota when Gary Kubiak was the Vikings offensive coordinator (2019-2020), and Klint was the quarterbacks coach (2019-2020) and took over as OC in 2021. During the preseason, it was clear that Cousins has command of the offense/system, and that has continued over the last six weeks. The Raiders come into this game ranking sixth in points per game (27.0) and seventh in passing yards per game (263.5). However, as you alluded to, the veteran signal caller is keeping the seat warm for Mendoza. Cousins has played well enough to make the Raiders a surprise playoff contender in the first half of the campaign, likely extending his time as the starter. And even during the three-game losing streak, he’s far from the team’s biggest problem and is a big reason they’ve been competitive in two out of the three losses. But the fact of the matter is that Las Vegas hasn’t beaten a quality opponent, and the October losses have made September feel like more of a fluke. If the Raiders lose this week, that’ll be four in a row and their record will dip below .500 for the first time this year. At that point, it might be time to start thinking about 2027 and beyond because the team isn’t winning despite the 38-year-old quarterback playing well. So, even though the decision would have nothing to do with Cousins’ performance, turning to the rookie to give him experience and start building for the future will likely become Kubiak’s and the organization’s priority. Q: Tre Tucker could be one of the more shocking fourth-year breakout receivers of recent memory. What makes him so good and do you expect his production to continue long-term? A: The 2023 third-round pick has been getting better and more productive every year despite working with subpar quarterbacks. For example, Tucker was the Raiders’ leading receiver with 57 catches, 696 yards and five touchdowns last year, all of which were career highs. He came into the league as a deep threat, and that’s still his bread and butter, but he’s grown tremendously as a route runner to be a threat in the intermediate areas of the field as well. So, I’m not surprised that Tucker is starting to climb up the receiver charts and get more recognition this season, ranking 20th in the NFL with 371 receiving yards through six weeks. He’s a good second option behind Brock Bowers in the passing game and has been the only wide receiver on the roster who has been productive this year. That being said, the long-term production question is tough to answer because the fourth-year pro is in a contract year. It will be interesting to see what his market looks like because his production has typically come in spurts rather than being consistent game-by-game, making it difficult to determine if he’s a go-to target moving forward. Q: I don’t know anything about defensive coordinator Rob Leonard. Tell me about him. A: Leonard was hired as the Raiders’ defensive line coach during Josh McDaniels’ second and final season as head coach. He had worked with defensive coordinator Patrick Graham — who he replaced this past offseason — for several years prior to landing in Las Vegas. Last year, Leonard’s role expanded by adding defensive run game coordinator to his title, and the defense showed a few impressive run blitzes and stunts that helped create negative plays in the running game throughout the season. When Klint Kubiak took over, what likely helped the former defensive line coach stay with the Raiders and receive a promotion is that he spent one year under current Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald when Macdonald was the Baltimore Ravens’ defensive coordinator. Obviously, Kubiak is tied to the Seahawks’ head coach too, having won a Super Bowl together last February. It seems pretty clear that Kubiak wanted to run a variation of Macdonald’s defense in Vegas, which is what Leonard is doing. The first-time coordinator has continued to develop the blitzes and stunts that he used in the run game last year, expanding them with simulated pressures, creeper blitzes and safety rotations to defend against the passing attack. Vegas’ defense has a lot of moving parts that can create confusion for quarterbacks and lead to turnovers — they had nine in the first three games — but that also can be a determinant. Leonard’s tendacies have been exposed during the three-game losing streak, as the Chiefs and Patriots routinely had the perfect play call for the Raiders’ defense. That was a little better last week, but the unit is very reliant on taking the ball away, and getting just one turnover in the last three weeks has led to them allowing 108 points during that time frame. At the end of the day, Leonard is still learning how to be an effective play-caller, and it doesn’t help that he doesn’t have that much talent to work with. Q: Who is one player on the Raiders defense that’s an absolute baller but the majority of NFL fans haven’t heard of him before? As mentioned above, Vegas’ defense doesn’t have enough talent outside of Maxx Crosby, who everyone has heard of at this point. So, this is a tough question to answer, but the first name that comes to mind is linebacker Nakobe Dean. Granted, Dean was fairly well-known as a draft prospect coming out of Georgia and spent the last four seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles, meaning he’s far from a “no-name”. But he fits the criteria the best because he hasn’t received any Pro Bowls or postseason recognition and is all of the field on the Raiders’ defense. The former Eagle has made several impact plays against the run, routinely coming up with big third-down stops in key moments of the game. Within that, he’s tied for the NFL lead with three forced fumbles, all of which have come in the fourth quarter with less than four minutes left on the clock. Q: Give the Offensive Line a letter grade and tell me if you think they’re trending up or down this week. C-. Tyler Linderbaum signed a historic contract in free agency that makes him the highest-paid center by $9 million per year, but he has only been above-average and not the Top 5 player at the position the Raiders thought they were getting. Left Tackle Kolton Miller has been solid but isn’t nearly the pass protector he…

title: Why a reset year would be different this time for the Rams
summary: The 2026 season for the Los Angeles Rams is starting to feel a lot like the outcomes we saw in 2020 and 2022. The collapses in these respective years brought significant change to the organization. With the offense struggling in 2020, the Rams decided that they had reached the end of the runway with Jared […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 12: Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 season for the Los Angeles Rams is starting to feel a lot like the outcomes we saw in 2020 and 2022. The collapses in these respective years brought significant change to the organization. With the offense struggling in 2020, the Rams decided that they had reached the end of the runway with Jared Goff. They traded Goff plus multiple first-round picks to the Detroit Lions in order to acquire Matthew Stafford. Stafford brought a renewed passing game to Los Angeles, and this allowed Sean McVay to reach deeper into his bag of tricks. Then came 2022. The offensive line was in shambles to start the year. It only got worse. Stafford was poorly protected and he ultimately succumbed to injury himself. Cooper Kupp and Aaron Donald were soon to follow. The change coming out of the 2022 season was a little more abstract than a sea change at quarterback. The front office realigned expectations with cornerstone piece Aaron Donald and refocused how they approach the draft. The Rams knew it was time for a roster reset. Donald was willing to return to help build the next era of the team as long as he was surrounded by players who loved the game and played for the right reasons. That led to an injection of home grown talent like Steve Avila, Kobie Turner, Byron Young, Puka Nacua, Braden Fiske, Jared Verse, Kamren Kinchens, and others. We don’t yet know whether 2026 is a lost season, although things certainly seem to be trending in that direction. But if the Rams find themselves out of contention soon, this collapse would be different. LA has already taken steps to build the future. There would be more sizeable moves to follow, of course, but the framework is at least already in place this time. The difference this time around is Ty Simpson . A losing season would likely mean the end of the run for Stafford, whose individual performance has significantly declined from his MVP year . Whether the Rams find a new home for Stafford remains uncertain, but a logical first step in a roster reset would be moving on from a quarterback in his late 30’s and the twilight of his career. The Rams need to at least win eight of their remaining 11 games in order to keep pace for a wildcard spot in 2026. That is a high bar to clear. Dropping games the team should win over the next month only accelerates the timeline for a quarterback change. Losing and lost seasons often bring uncertainty. That wouldn’t be the case for the 2026 and 2027 Rams. The future is already on their roster. This time around is different.
author: JB Scott

title: NFL predictions: Rams’ Tutu Atwell will be weapon vs. Raiders
summary: The Los Angeles Rams need a wide receiver to step up, and it has to be five-year veteran Tutu Atwell. With Davante Adams sidelined by injury and Puka Nacua suffering a calf injury during Thursday’s practice, the Rams could be running dangerously thin at wide receiver. If Sean McVay wants his offense to remain productive […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Tutu Atwell #8 of the Los Angeles Rams walks off the field after an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams need a wide receiver to step up, and it has to be five-year veteran Tutu Atwell . With Davante Adams sidelined by injury and Puka Nacua suffering a calf injury during Thursday’s practice, the Rams could be running dangerously thin at wide receiver. If Sean McVay wants his offense to remain productive against the Las Vegas Raiders, Atwell must become a much bigger part of the game plan. And I believe Sean McVay finally course corrects with his usage of Tutu Atwell; leading to Atwell’s biggest game as a Ram. Here are my five predictions for Sunday’s game. 1. Tutu Atwell becomes Stafford’s No. 1 target With Davante Adams and maybe Puka Nacua, you may think the Rams lean more into 13 personnel, and maybe so. But the Rams will have to throw the ball. Stafford needs someone that can create separation consistently. Tutu is the guy. And Atwell offers a lot of explosive play ability with it. McVay just has to dial it up. Do you not remember the start of the 2023 season? Tutu’s first three games: 26 targets, 17 receptions, 246 receiving yards, and 1 receiving touchdown. Tutu will receiving double digit targets for the first time in his career. And finishes the day with 12 targets, 8 receptions and 143 receiving yards. 2. Kyren Williams rushes for 180 yards Kyren Williams made waves in his postgame comments after Week 6 citing that the offense is struggling to find consistency because he is not out there. With the Rams needing to find their identity on offense, I think Sean McVay leans into run game for the first time all season. With that being said, Kyren gets 25 touches on the ground in a must win game for Los Angeles. Las Vegas does not have a strong run defense; having surrendered 134.3 rushing yards/game and 152.3 rushing yards/game over their last three games. 3. Rams defense pitches shutout in 2nd half The Raiders have struggled in the 2nd half of games. In the 3rd quarter, they have been outscored by 26 points through six games (the worst mark in the NFL). LA must capitalize on this. The Rams have a reputation of posting shutouts in the 2nd half of games over the last 3 years. They could use one this week. 4. Wesley Bailey notches multi-sack game I have liked what Wesley Bailey has to offer off the edge for the Rams. His size and length provide something that Byron Young and Josiah Stewart lack. With the help of Aaron Donald, Bailey grabs not just one but two sacks in Week 7. 5. Rams do not punt until 4th quarter Seeking rhythm on offense, the Rams commit to going for it in 4th & short situations rather than opting to send the special teams out and risking a disaster waiting to happen. The Rams don’t send Ethan Evans and the punt unit out until the 4th quarter; acknowledging that this is a must win game and the offense will need to execute in order to secure a win on the road.

title: Unknown rookie could be key to the Rams’ ailing defensive line
summary: As the Los Angeles Rams scramble to assemble a new defensive line in the wake of injuries to both Kobie Turner and Poona Ford, undrafted rookie Bill Norton could be the answer that Chris Shula is looking for. Although Norton is on the practice squad and yet to be called up for an NFL game, […]
full_text: As the Los Angeles Rams scramble to assemble a new defensive line in the wake of injuries to both Kobie Turner and Poona Ford, undrafted rookie Bill Norton could be the answer that Chris Shula is looking for. Although Norton is on the practice squad and yet to be called up for an NFL game, there are components to his player profile that make him a more intriguing option moving forward than L.A.’s current stable of backups. Rams fans just want something to be excited about right now, and an underdog story like Norton’s fits the bill. What went wrong this season? Injury attrition continues to take its toll on the Rams defensive line with this weeks news that Poona Ford (torn tricep) is lost for the season and Kobie Turner faces extended time, a minimum of four weeks, on the the Injured Reserve List. Both L.A.’s coaching and front office braintrust are left scrambling to fill the void. The Rams just happen to have a prospect on their practice squad that is certainly big enough to take up some of that space: 6’ 5” 330 lb. defensive tackle Bill Norton. In the recent past, the Rams have been trending towards smaller, speaking relatively when it’s 300 lb. men, defensive interior players that can be moved freely across the front line. Norton’s thick and wide frame breaks that mold. Now in the midst of his second season, he signed with the Rams as an undrafted free agent in the spring of 2025. At that time, his addition appeared to be another piece of L.A.’s big picture plan to improve a run defense that had a Bottom 10 NFL ranking in 2024. Norton has not seen any time on the 53-man roster and has been biding his time toiling on the L.A. practice squad Norton boasts a good pedigree. Originally recruited and signed by the Georgia Bulldogs as a four-star high school recruit. Played basketball, as well. Spent four seasons with the “Dawgs and was part of two National Championship teams. He never was able to break through in Athens, playing in 26 games and accumulating modest stats (12 tackles, 3.5 for loss) on special teams and in a reserve role. Rode the portal west to Arizona for 2023 and had his best college season, starting 12 of 13 games and charting 32 tackles, 2.5 for loss, three batted down passes and two forced fumbles. Norton stepped in class for his final season in 2024 with the Texas Longhorns. He saw action in 14 games and claimed 14 tackles, 1.5 for loss, and one sack. New #Texas DT commit Bill Norton (#45) against an SEC offensive line. Durable with play strength and size. 88 overall grade in the portal #HookEm pic.twitter.com/2lZL54EnMk — Clint Brewster (@clintbrew247) April 22, 2024 Finding a role that fits Gone are are the days when L.A. made due with a predominant five-man front base. Sub packages are now the rule, based mostly on four man defensive fronts. Last year, according to Sharp Football Analysis , the Rams used sub defensive packages at a 75 percent rate. In the past two seasons they have moved towards a deep rotation on the defensive interior, at times using as many as seven different players in a game, and moving them interchangeably. Norton will find his fit as one of those pieces, Norton projects best into the Poona Ford role, as the dirty work guy tasked with clogging the inside gaps, disrupting run lanes and absorbing double team blocks to open things up for others. Not glamorous, the job is for lunch pail-type players that don’t need glossy stat counts to keep them pounding away. There might also be place for him on special teams, he was a regular performer on those units in college. Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart said of his special teams efforts, “What a great kid man, this guy worked his tail off here, worked really hard. One of his key roles was with special teams, he played on our field goal protection unit and was the best at doing it.” What does the film say? With the Rams strategy of all roster contributors sitting out the preseason, it creates the opportunity to see a lot of Norton on film. L.A. did not limit him to nose tackle or shading the center in the A gaps, he was employed up and down the front line. On field goal/extra point protection, he displayed a low pad level and wide base and staying connected (no open lanes) to the players on his flanks. He’s not an explosive gap shooter/penetrator that will create pass rush pressure. Nor does he have a toolbox full of moves that he can combine to wreak havoc. Norton is going to use linear push as his predominant move. If he gets stymied, he’s aware of getting into passing lanes and stretching out his frame to tighten passing lanes. He had three batted passes in preseason. Not often, but he had a few reps from outside on the edge, and the short runway allowed him to do a pretty good job using a direct speed to power attack. Inside, taking on blockers is where he’ll have the best chance for success. While arm length is just adequate (32 1/4”) and his punch isn’t of stun grade, he does a good job of landing first and is quite accurate. It enables him to keep good control tostack/shed blockers. When you combine the extension with a wide base, he was able to hold ground against double teams at the preseason level of competition. Not gifted with plus agility or change of direction skills, but he moves laterally pretty well for his girth. More importantly, Norton is a hustler, navigates well in traffic, and takes good angles in pursuit. Although he’ll likely struggle in the open field, expect him get his share of hustle stops from behind, even across the field. Bill Norton ( @billlnorton ) had 2 tackles, 1 of them solo and a PD for the Rams. pic.twitter.com/bjKHZaBjcX — NFL Longhorns (@NFL_Longhorns) August 28, 2026 Does Bill Norton offer any value? The Rams put a lot of weight on the shoulders of the defensive line. In the past, along with run-stopping responsibilities, the front (including edges in this case) has been expected to provide pass rush pressure without a lot of blitz calls. Although the Rams are blitzing at a 10% higher rate this year than last (27.5% to 17.7%), it’s not identity of the defense. Norton shouldn’t be expected to upgrade the pass rush, maybe clean up and/or back door hustle pursuit Fans have to be realistic about the value Norton can offer. He is not an All-Pro waiting for his big chance and bringing a polished game up with him from the practice squad. What he can offer is rotational snaps, particularly working in running situations. Providing a big body to help improve L.A.’s between the tackles run defense. Every double team he can draw and engage will keep a linebacker/safety clean to fill a lane or give one of the better-equipped pass rushers a 1on1. On the defensive interior, big problems demand big answers. Bill Norton certainly offers the size, will the Rams apply it?

title: Analyst: Rams should trade for Chris Godwin
summary: Should the Los Angeles Rams make a move for Chris Godwin? The Rams have lost Davante Adams due to injury for an extended period of time and besides Puka Nacua, the receiver room for the Rams is a question mark. Could Godwin help stabilize the room? Godwin is a veteran of the NFL, he’s won […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 26: Chris Godwin #14 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrates in the endzone after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter in the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on September 26, 2021 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Should the Los Angeles Rams make a move for Chris Godwin? The Rams have lost Davante Adams due to injury for an extended period of time and besides Puka Nacua, the receiver room for the Rams is a question mark. Could Godwin help stabilize the room? Godwin is a veteran of the NFL, he’s won a Super Bowl, but he’s also had some serious injuries that have likely impacted his ability to play at his best. If the Rams could get a prime Godwin, then this trade would be beneficial, but a broken-down Godwin? How much does that help the Rams? So, L.A. will see in Week 7 if they have enough depth in their wide receiver and tight end group to make up for Adams going down, and if not, then the Rams may want to make a trade. Or if the Rams fall to 2-5, they may want to sell. Variables aplenty. Trade rumors aplenty. Rams Trade Pitch Lands $102 Million Super Bowl Champion (heavy.com) “The Rams lost Davante Adams for six to 10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring. Godwin is among the slew of names floated as potential targets for the Rams before the trade deadline. “I wonder if they call for Chris Godwin,” NFL analyst Trevor Sikkema posted on X on October 21. “Godwin’s now 30 and 2027 is a club option in his contract. He’s the ideal Rams receiver with how much he does as a blocker. If Tampa loses to Carolina this weekend I could see it.” Why the Rams should trade for this Pro Bowl TE instead of a WR “On Wednesday, Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta told “Pardon My Take” that he’s not thrilled about how the organization has treated his contract situation, and he’s OK if he hits free agency this coming offseason. His words sparked the idea that he could be on the trade block. “It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and bear the risk of getting hurt,” said LaPorta. “Like last year, I broke my (expletive) back for the team. And then I’m going out there this year, and I’m balling, and maybe they’re just not showing the love.” NFL trade rumors: 5 receivers the Rams should target in a deal, including Cowboys’ George Pickens (cbssports) “The veteran receiver is expected to miss six to 10 weeks after rupturing his hamstring in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals . Under the best-case scenario, Adams isn’t expected to be back until December, which means the Rams now have a gaping hole at receiver. title: Las Vegas Raiders-Los Angeles Rams FEED Topic: Which team will win special teams battle?
summary: Heading into the Week 7 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders, the 2026 Los Angeles Rams have drawn comparisons to the 2010 then-San Diego Chargers. That year, the Chargers had the No. 1-ranked offense and No. 1-ranked defense in terms of yards per game, but finished with a 9-7 record and failed to make the […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Heading into the Week 7 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders, the 2026 Los Angeles Rams have drawn comparisons to the 2010 then-San Diego Chargers. That year, the Chargers had the No. 1-ranked offense and No. 1-ranked defense in terms of yards per game, but finished with a 9-7 record and failed to make the playoffs. How did that happen? San Diego’s special teams ranked dead last in the NFL and cost the team several games. Sixteen years later, the franchise the Bolts currently share a city and stadium with is following a similar trend. The Rams “won the offseason” by swinging big and making trades for All-Pros like Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie, while luring future Hall of Famer Aaron Donald out of retirement. They already had a potent offense with reigning MVP Matthew Stafford at quarterback, seemingly setting themselves up to host Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium. To Los Angeles’ credit, the team does have the third-ranked offense and third-ranked defense in total yards through the first six weeks of the season. But the 2-4 club is clearly falling short of the preseason expectations. How? Injuries have certainly been a factor since Garrett has only played in the season opener, while McDuffie and Donald have combined to miss three games. But the biggest aspect of the Rams’ lack of success is that they rank dead last in total special teams EPA (-21.35) and EPA per play (-0.309), according to Sumer Sports . Figuring out the kicker situation has been a big part of the issue. Harrison Mevis was L.A.’s kicker for the first five games of the campaign but made just five of his nine attempts (55.6%), missing both tries in a 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills. That was the final straw for Mevis, who was released and replaced by Blake Grupe last week, only for Grupe to tear an ACL in his Rams debut last Sunday. Brandon McManus, who made 24 of 30 attempts ( 80.0% ) with the Green Bay Packers a year ago, will be Los Angeles’ third kicker in seven games this season. However, putting the ball between the uprights has been the Rams’ biggest issue on special teams, but not the only one. Sumer Sports has their punt coverage costing the team about 0.43 EPA per punt, while having a neutral punt return game. Additionally, Pro Football Focus has Los Angeles graded as the seventh-worst special teams unit in the NFL with a 66.5 mark. This phase of the game was a sticking point in Turf Show Times’ Kenny Arthur’s response when Silver and Black Pride asked Arthur how the “Super Team” has fallen apart . Meanwhile, the Raiders’ special teams have had issues under coordinator Joe DeCamillis — who held the same position with the Rams in 2021 and 2022 — so far this season, too. Vegas has fared decently in total EPA, ranking ninth at 7.65, primarily due to Matt Gay making 14 of his 15 field goals (93.3%). However, the Silver and Black have struggled to cover punts, ranking 26th in the NFL by allowing 13.44 yards per punt return, according to Sumer. Also, the punt returners have had issues with both when to and when not to field punts, while kick returners Dylan Laube and Dareke Young have each had costly fumbles. As a result, Vegas has a slightly worse PFF special teams grade than L.A. does, ranking as the fifth-worst with a 65.2 mark . Plenty of focus will be on each team’s offense and defense this Sunday, but it could be the third/often forgotten phase of the game that ends up being the biggest difference or factor on the scoreboard. So, for this week’s game day discussion on The FEED , we’ll be keeping tabs on the special teams battle. The game kicks off at 1:25 p.m. PST and will air on FOX (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!
