title: Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing set for golden opportunity they might not get again
summary: If the 49ers take the sensible, long-term approach, then they will not have Mike Evans available for their Week 7 matchup with the Atlanta Falcons after his Achilles issue flared up in their Monday Night Football win over the Washington Commanders. San Francisco is shorn of wide receiver depth due to a remarkable cluster of […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 27: Jordan Watkins #17 of the San Francisco 49ers runs with the ball during an NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals on September 27, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If the 49ers take the sensible, long-term approach, then they will not have Mike Evans available for their Week 7 matchup with the Atlanta Falcons after his Achilles issue flared up in their Monday Night Football win over the Washington Commanders. San Francisco is shorn of wide receiver depth due to a remarkable cluster of injuries at the position, and the 49er passing game was ineffective without Evans after he left the game against the Commanders. Evans has developed a superb rapport with Brock Purdy, serving as a devastatingly effective easy button for the San Francisco quarterback. The future Hall of Famer’s connection with Purdy is likely to be critical down the stretch and in the postseason as the 49ers aim to realize their Super Bowl aspirations and, as such, there is little reason for San Francisco to risk a serious injury to Evans by pushing him to play against the Falcons when they are 6-0 with a three-game lead in the NFC West. Though the 49ers look likely to be without Evans, they could get a boost with the return of Christian Kirk from the calf issue that has kept him out for the entire season to this point. But it is perhaps a tad ambitious to expert Kirk to hit the ground running right off the bat and, in Evans’ potential absence, the passing game will most likely predominantly go through tight end George Kittle. Yet the dearth of other options would also leave the Falcons game as a golden opportunity for Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing to impress and stake a claim for a larger amount of offensive snaps going forward. Both Cowing (2024) and Watkins (2025) came into the league as fourth-round picks with skill sets that suggested they could be dynamic options in the Kyle Shanahan offense. Yet their potential in that regard has remained largely untapped. Cowing and Watkins each displayed speed and route-running craft in college that figured to translate well to the NFL level. However, they have each seen injuries check their progress. After playing only a peripheral role in 2024, Cowing lost an entire season to injury in 2025, when a preseason high-ankle sprain curtailed the ascent Watkins was seemingly enjoying as a rookie. Heading into Week 7, Cowing and Watkins each have just five catches each in their respective careers. Cowing has only 89 yards to his name, while Watkins has 108, with the former seemingly on thin ice in his role as a return man having muffed a punt in the win over the Seattle Seahawks before making an ill-advised decision to return one from the four-yard line in the defeat of the Commanders. After Evans again missed practice on Thursday, it seems highly likely Watkins and Cowing will have prominent roles to play regardless of Kirk’s involvement. Even with Christian Kirk probably returning on Sunday, Watkins should have a decent role to play. Nice work here recovering from the stumble on the incidental contact, working back to the ball and then managing to get upfield for YAC. pic.twitter.com/JqseP6Piwo — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 22, 2026 It is an opportunity neither can afford to waste, as they may not get another this season. While Evans’ Achilles issue will need to be managed throughout the year, he will be expected to return in Week 9 if he does indeed miss the Falcons game. Deebo Samuel is also expected back after the bye, though rookie De’Zhaun Stribling will have to wait a little longer to make his return from the ankle injury suffered in the season opener. In other words, they will each be down the pecking order again soon. From Watkins at least, there have been some encouraging flashes of promise this season, the former Ole Miss wideout making catches of 34 and 26 yards in the Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals and doing an excellent job overcoming physical coverage to make a 22-yard reception against the Commanders. Nothing spectacular here, but Jordan Watkins has played 45% of the offensive snaps this season. Injuries aside, some of that will be tied to the fact that he's shown buy-in as a run-blocker, including on the weird inadvertent Kaelon Black direct snap play. pic.twitter.com/LSeeyvhr5y — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 22, 2026 Watkins has also displayed admirable commitment as a run blocker this season, with his effort in that area of the game likely a reason why he has been trusted to play 45 percent of the offensive snaps so far in 2026. Asked why Watkins hasn’t had more targets, quarterback Brock Purdy replied on Thursday: “Honestly, it has nothing to do with not trying to get him the ball or anything. I think that’s just sort of how the game’s gone. He’s definitely a playmaker. He’s done that since he’s got here. And it’s just been tough with him getting opportunities when we have like [WR] Mike Evans, [WR] Demarcus Robinson, [TE] George [Kittle], [RB] Christian [McCaffrey], like other guys too and he’s trying to get in that mix. But, he’s been consistent. He’s been a guy that has stayed faithful to this whole process. And now he’s getting a shot and opportunity. So, I feel like we will over time. Hopefully this game too, I can get him the ball. Watching the film, that’s definitely a guy that I’m like, ‘Yeah, I’d love to get the ball to him.’ He’s shown flashes and glimpses of not even just catching the ball, but making plays after the catch too or getting YAC after the catch. So, I feel you on that and that’s something that I watch and I want to have our connection get better and better, but has nothing to do with not trying to give him the ball or anything like that.” Of the two, Watkins seems the more likely to have success in carving out a long-term role in the offense. Cowing was put the behind the 8-ball by his lost 2025 and has not caught up, with his stock at a low ebb amid his questionable performance as a returner. But if either is going to have a compelling case for being involved in the offense once the likes of Evans and Samuel return, then they need to make the most of the chance that looks set to come their way on Sunday. There is concern about how the 49er passing game will look without Evans in Atlanta. If either Cowing or Watkins can ensure it still succeeds, then it would serve as a great boost to their long-term prospects and the depth of the 49er receiving corps.

title: 49ers OC on second year WR: ‘The ball is going to find him’
summary: The San Francisco 49ers will likely have a whole different look in the passing game this week, as they’re expected to be without star wide receiver Mike Evans, general manager John Lynch said on the radio. San Francisco’s wide receiver core was already banged up heading into the game, and now, the team will rely […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Jordan Watkins #17 of the San Francisco 49ers catches a pass against the Washington Commanders in the second quarter of an NFL football game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers will likely have a whole different look in the passing game this week, as they’re expected to be without star wide receiver Mike Evans, general manager John Lynch said on the radio. San Francisco’s wide receiver core was already banged up heading into the game, and now, the team will rely on Brandin Cooks, Christian Kirk, Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, Malik Turner, and potentially a wide receiver from the practice squad. With Evans out for the second half this past week, the 49ers had a big shift in their wide receiver snaps. Jordan Watkins, who got the start over Cooks and Cowing, played 47 snaps, leading all wideouts. Cooks was behind him at 32 snaps, while Cowing got just 15. The week prior, it was Cowing who lapped both Cooks and Watkins in snaps. Now, despite the 47 snaps, Watkins saw just one target, making the catch for 22 yards. With Evans now out, that figure will potentially have to rise, as the 49ers need to throw the ball somewhere. Do they anticipate giving their second-year wideout a bigger role? “[The lack of targets and opportunities], it’s nothing to do with him,” offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said of Watkins. “He’s doing a heck of a job, and Jordan’s playing the right way down in and down out. We’ve been really happy with him. Sometimes it’s just circumstances and where the ball goes. There were things in the game we were trying to get to him and the ball ended up going the other way, so it’s not really amount of targets. “He’s doing everything right and the ball is going to find him because he’s playing the right way. Jordan’s just got to keep going and the ball’s going to go where it goes, just like every down. The way Jordan’s approaching every play and playing the right way and doing his assignment the right way, fortunate things are going to keep happening for him, so just keep him going.” Watkins had struggled to stay healthy as a rookie, playing in only four games, but he also wasn’t involved much, catching just three passes for 26 yards. Now, it seems like he’ll be stepping into a bigger role as another receiver, Jacob Cowing, is trending downwards. Is the coaching staff seeing what they want from Watkins from a route-running and separation perspective? “100%. He’s doing a great job. He’s practicing really well too,” Kubiak added. “He’s gotten better as a player. That’s what we’ve asked him to do is keep working, keep pushing himself. He’s grown a lot as he stepped up more and been more involved in our offense and I expect that to continue to happen. Jordan’s doing everything right and, like I said, when guys approach things that way, good things tend to happen so we’re just going to keep going with him.” If things hold similarly to last week, it looks like Watkins should be in line for his second start, and could lead the wide receivers in snaps again. Brock Purdy is going to need this group to make plays, so it’ll be up to Watkins and the other wideouts to get open. But after a week with just one target, it feels like more are coming Watkins’s way in Week 7.

summary: This matchup between the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans looks to be the most boring game of the week. The total in this game currently sits at 37.5 over at FanDuel Sportsbook. That is the lowest total of the week, and the under might be the smart bet. The Titans are last in the league […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Chimere Dike #17 of the Tennessee Titans avoids a tackle by Rigoberto Sanchez #8 of the Indianapolis Colts during the fourth quarter at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images This matchup between the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans looks to be the most boring game of the week. The total in this game currently sits at 37.5 over at FanDuel Sportsbook . That is the lowest total of the week, and the under might be the smart bet. The Titans are last in the league in yards per game at 236.3. The Browns are 29th at 267.5. Get ready for a lot of punts. The key for the Titans in this game will be taking care of the ball. Last week, the Titans forced three turnovers against the Indianapolis Colts. That, and a couple of key special teams plays, were the difference in the game. This game will likely play out in a similar way. Speaking of special teams plays, it was really good to see Chimere Dike break off a 58-yard punt return against the Colts. Dike was the biggest weapon the Titans had last season, but he had struggled this season before last week. Hopefully, that was the start of his return to the All-Pro returner he was last season. This game does feature two good rookie wide receivers. Denzel Boston leads all rookie receivers with 345 yards and is averaging over 20 yards per catch. Carnell Tate is right behind him with 344 yards. If one of those guys can break a big play, it could be the difference in this game. Don’t expect a thrilling game when you sit down to watch this one on Sunday, but if the Titans can play a game similar to the one they did last week, they might have a chance at back-to-back wins for the first time since 2022.

title: 5 Titans players need to show up vs. Browns in Week 7
summary: The Tennessee Titans have a difficult showdown versus the surging 4-2 Cleveland Browns in Week 7. We’ve identified five players who need to thrive for Robert Saleh’s squad to execute an upset victory. […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jeffery Simmons #98 of the Tennessee Titans warms up prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. Despite the record, the Browns have been rather average, and the Titans should appreciate their chances to play a close, competitive contest. We’ve identified five players who need to thrive for Robert Saleh’s squad to execute an upset victory. DT Jeffery Simmons Jeffery Simmons was outstanding versus the Colts, registering two sacks. He also forced a fumble that he recovered; it kickstarted the comeback. Now, Simmons gets another quarterback in Deshaun Watson who is mistake-prone and likes holding onto the football instead of throwing it in efficient fashion. WR Carnell Tate Carnell Tate was excellent in Week 6, recording six receptions for 70 yards and a touchdown. The rookie fourth overall selection also drew a significant pass interference penalty that flipped the field (roughly 35 yards). The last time Tate broke out (Ravens, Week 4), the Titans failed to build on his momentum. They can’t repeat that mistake versus the Browns. S Amani Hooker Veteran safety Amani Hooker leads the Titans in interceptions with two. HIs takeaway versus the Colts showcased some savvy footwork and hand-eye coordination on a tipped Daniel Jones pass near the sideline. Hooker nearly had three INTs against the Browns. His ballhawking ways could generate another turnover against Watson. QB Cam Ward Quarterback Cam Ward was carried by the defense and special teams throughout the Colts win. The sophomore No. 1 overall pick was just 11-of-22 for 102 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. The Browns have an excellent defense, so Ward and the below-average passing attack will be tested. LB Anthony Hill Jr. Titans rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. has been a complete revelation this season. While Cody Barton and Cedric Gray continue competing for reps opposite him, Hill has been the Titans’ only constant at linebacker. He continues showcasing sideline-to-sideline ability while being an asset both versus the pass and run.

summary: The Daily Slop – 24 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles scores a touchdown against Mike Sainristil #0 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 24 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Sports Illustrated Where Does Mike Sainristil Fit in the Washington Commanders Defense Now? Mike Sainristil played seven defensive snaps against San Francisco; with Trey Amos back, earning more work will take more than a change in position [After playing] 54 of 55 defensive snaps against Philadelphia [in Week 1], six games into the season, finding a place for him has become a much different conversation. Sainristil played seven defensive snaps against San Francisco . Robertson played all 62, while Rasul Douglas and Trey Amos played 36 apiece. That leaves Washington entering its bye with three corners getting considerably more work than [the] player it drafted in the second round just two years ago. The coverage has been a problem. Entering Washington’s bye, Pro Football Focus gave Sainristil a 29.4 overall defensive grade and a 28.5 coverage grade, both ranking 102nd among 102 qualifying cornerbacks. When asked about Amos’ return and whether he had considered Sainristil at safety, [defensive coordinator Daronte] Jones pointed to the deep-zone assignments Sainristil had handled against New York . “The depth chart that we had in that game and who was available definitely had something to do with that,” Jones said. He was explaining how the team could use him in different assignments, without announcing a permanent position change. That’s where I would keep Sainristil for now: situational nickel work and reserve duties that allow Washington to use that flexibility when needed. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Rasul Douglas is turning a late Commanders signing into an offseason steal The Commanders needed more from Douglas than they originally anticipated. Trey Amos spent the first four games on injured reserve and missed five contests before returning on Monday Night Football against the San Francisco 49ers. Mike Sainristil’s freefall has seen him become an afterthought, which was the only sensible call left. That meant Douglas had to step up and he’s coped with the challenge superbly. Douglas has been a tremendous addition. His coverage is an outstanding feature of his production, giving Washington the assurance it desperately needed. The 2017 third-round pick out of West Virginia is giving up just 54.5 percent of targets thrown in his direction. Douglas has five pass breakups and one interception. He is also allowing a measly 63.8 passer rating when targeted, which fairly reflects his outstanding consistency. That’s not all. Douglas is also making a considerable impression against the run. His physicality closer to the line of scrimmage goes overlooked, but it’s nonetheless impressive. Douglas has been credited with eight run stops through six games. And even with the Commanders’ defense struggling to maintain high performance for four quarters , almost nobody is gaining big yards on the ground. Other factors are in play. However, Douglas is one reason for this turnaround. Douglas only signed a one-year deal. He’s still performing at a high level, but he also recently turned 31. That’s not ancient, but it is the stage where corners tend to regress. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Washington Has Allowed Twice as Many Red-Zone Touchdowns as It Has Scored The Washington Commanders entered their bye week with a red-zone issue: opponents scored 18 red-zone touchdowns, while Washington scored 9. That’s a problem on both sides of the ball for a team that has already seen close games slip away. The Commanders have scored nine touchdowns on 17 red-zone trips, or 52.9%, tied for 21st-best with the Bengals. Opposing teams have had five more trips (22 total) but scored nine more touchdowns (81.8%), which ranks Washington 31st in red-zone touchdown rate allowed through Week 6. Commanders Roundtable Three trade targets for the Washington Commanders [Tthe Commanders…sit two games back in an NFC East race that resembles 2020. With embattled head coach Dan Quinn and general manager Adam Peters potentially facing scrutiny for the roster construction, the pressure is on to make the right roster upgrades to give the team a chance to make a run in a suddenly compromised division. But who are trade targets? Amani Hooker, safety, Tennessee Titans Hooker, 28, has been the most underrated safety in the NFL because he is stuck on a struggling Titans team that’s winless this season and went 3-19 in the last two seasons. Hooker is a piece teams would like, as a productive player with one 92-yard interception and 28 tackles so far in 2026. His run defense grade per PFF is 86.5, the seventh among safeties, and his coverage grade is 62.1, the 37th among safeties, for a combined grade of 73.0, good for 21st out of 96 qualified safeties. Quan Martin and Jeremy Reeves haven’t shown they’re starting-quality safeties, and Hooker and Nick Cross would be a beneficial safety tandem for the next few seasons. Hooker is under contract through 2028 after signing a three-year extension before the 2025 season. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders’ Drew Stevens Owns Two Franchise Rookie Records After Just Six Games Washington Commanders rookie Drew Stevens already held the franchise’s rookie record for the longest field goal before Monday night against San Francisco. His 51-yarder in the first quarter brought him to three makes from 50-plus yards , extending the franchise rookie record he already held. The 57-yarder against Seattle set the distance record in Week 3, after Stevens had connected from 55 yards against Philadelphia in the opener. Both rookie marks are now his with 11 games still left to play. Stevens was 3-for-5 on field goals after the first two games, and he hasn’t missed one since. He made two apiece against Seattle, Indianapolis, and New York, then his lone attempt against San Francisco. That puts him at seven straight makes and 10-for-12 overall, or 83.3%, entering the bye. Both misses came from 50-plus yards during those opening two games. He’s also 7-for-7 inside 50 yards and 3-for-5 from 50 or longer. The long kicks are getting the records, but Stevens has taken care of the shorter field goals, too. title: Commanders survey results: Fans refuse to punt on 2026 season
summary: In this week’s Reacts survey, we asked Hogs Haven readers two questions regarding the state of the Washington Commanders as the team enters its Week 7 bye. A question of confidence The first question was our standard pulse check: Are you confident in the team’s direction? Interestingly, that 26% positive mark represents an 8-point jump […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - DECEMBER 30: Washington Redskins punter Tress Way (5) throws a completed pass on a fake punt in the third quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles at FedEx Field. (Photo by Jonathan Newton / The Washington Post via Getty Images) In this week’s Reacts survey, we asked Hogs Haven readers two questions regarding the state of the Washington Commanders as the team enters its Week 7 bye. A question of confidence The first question was our standard pulse check: Are you confident in the team’s direction? No: 74% Yes: 26% Interestingly, that 26% positive mark represents an 8-point jump from the 18% registered after Week 6 despite the Commanders suffering a second consecutive loss. While nearly three-quarters of the fanbase remains skeptical—understandably so after a grueling 1-4-1 start—the modest uptick suggests that a few days of distance from game action have allowed a little bit of perspective to seep back in. What Hogs Haven readers want to see from the team after the bye Our second question tackled the immediate road ahead: What do you want to see from the Commanders after the bye week? Rally around Dan Quinn, fight to win games, and reach the postseason: 64% An interim head coach to replace Dan Quinn and a shift in focus to the 2027 season: 36% Taken together, the results of the two survey questions tell a revealing story about where this fanbase stands at the mid-autumn break. While 3 out of 4 fans remain uneasy with the broader direction after six weeks of frustration, nearly two-thirds flatly reject the idea of waving a white flag on the 2026 campaign. There is a tangible difference between acknowledging a disappointing start and surrendering to it, and Hogs Haven readers clearly believe that letting Dan Quinn and this squad fight through the storm offers a far better path forward than triggering an organizational fire drill in late October. The case for measured optimism in the “second season” that starts after the bye To anyone staring strictly at the standings, talking about a postseason push might sound borderline delusional. The bad news from the first 6 weeks is well known, painful to recount, and needs little rehash here: missed opportunities, fourth-quarter breakdowns, and an offense that was severely hindered when quarterback injuries disrupted Weeks 2, 3, and 4. Yet, nearly two-thirds of our readers voted against pulling the rip cord. As Alex Rowsey aptly put it in the comments, it is hard to stomach punting on an NFL season when the NFC East remains completely up for grabs. Look around the neighborhood. The Philadelphia Eagles have lost Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season , have dropped 4 straight games, and look vulnerable heading into the Week 8 road game against Washington. The Dallas Cowboys , despite avoiding the quarterback injuries that partly-derailed Washington’s early slate, have also dropped 4 of their first 6 games and look just as out of sorts . Meanwhile, the New York Giants sit just 2 games ahead of Washington and enter this weekend as double-digit underdogs against the Houston Texans. Nobody is running away with this division. In fact, Washington’s remaining strength of schedule over the final 11 games is among the easiest in the NFL, which seems to open up a world of opportunity – if the team can make some meaningful improvements during this week’s lull in the action. FWIW via @tankathon only three teams have an easier remaining strength of schedule than the Commanders … unfortunately the Cowboys are one of em pic.twitter.com/9tfl8uZJhk — Mitchell Tischler (@Mitch_Tischler) October 20, 2026 The secret ingredient to success Most importantly, Jayden Daniels has played high-caliber football behind center and continues to display significant upside. As offensive coordinator David Blough and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones gain comfort and rhythm in their play-calling duties, the units around Daniels should improve steadily. If the coaching staff utilizes the bye week to incorporate more quick reads, rhythmic RPOs, and enhanced and aggressive defensive looks—points raised repeatedly by commenters and media—this team has plenty of room for meaningful growth. Dan Quinn, Josh Harris, and the executive reality In addition to the Reacts surveys we carry out on Hogs Haven, SB Nation conducts regular weekly national (even international) polling of fans across the fanbases of all 32 teams via email. This week, one of the national survey questions asked which coach would be the first to be fired this season. Visit our partners at FanDuel I think the national press and most NFL fans are reading the situation in Washington all wrong. It seems to me that a hell of a lot more would have to go wrong for the Washington ownership group to consider parting ways with DQ in the midst of his 3rd season. It’s true that a sizable 36% contingent voted for an interim coach to replace Quinn in our Reacts survey this week, and several commenters made thoughtful arguments about clock management and late-game execution. But owner Josh Harris is an experienced professional sports owner who understands the value of organizational stability. Harris knows all too well the damage caused by knee-jerk, emotional reactions to early-season adversity. There is an old, reliable axiom in professional management that applies to both business and sports: a good executive supports his guy 100% right up until the exact moment he doesn’t. That is not an empty cliché; it is how professional organizations operate — and Josh Harris knows how to run a professional organization. As long as Dan Quinn is the head coach of the Washington Commanders, he holds the complete, undivided support of ownership. Harris has shown throughout his ownership career that he prefers to evaluate a full body of work across an entire 17-game campaign rather than pulling the plug mid-stream. Quinn will be given every opportunity to navigate through these waters, and I would hope that fans will be pulling for him to succeed — our survey results indicate that most Hogs Haven readers will absolutely continue to root for the team to win games and earn a playoff spot. Personally, I expect Quinn to succeed in turning the 2026 season around, and I expect him to remain the head coach into 2027 after doing so. Consistent leadership and direction over a period of years has been proven to be more effective in the NFL than constantly lurching from one vision of leadership to another based on short term results. With 11 games left to play in the 2026 season, there’s a lot of time left to right the ship, but that opportunity would be lost if the mob mentality of “fire everyone” were to be adopted by Harris because of a tough few weeks to open the season. Charting the path back to relevance If you are looking for a reasonable roadmap to a season turnaround, consider how the next month sets up. Coming out of the bye, the Commanders face a wounded Philadelphia team, followed by the 2-4 Rams , and then a rematch with the Giants (who’ve just made the QB switch to JJ McCarthy). Winning those 3 games is entirely within reach, and doing so would vault Washington to 4-4-1, putting them right back at the .500 mark with 8 games to play. From there, the schedule remains exceptionally favorable. Winning 4 of the 6 winnable games between Weeks 11 and 16 (Bengals, Cardinals, Titans, Texans, Falcons, Vikings) would have Washington sitting two games above .500 heading into a pivotal Week 17 clash in Jacksonville. With one of the easiest remaining schedules in football ahead of them, the Commanders could put together a string of victories reminiscent of the 2012 Redskins ( from 3-6, 7 straight wins to close out the season ) or the 2015 team ( from 2-4, 6 wins in the final 8 games; 7 wins in the final 10 ). Heck, even the 2020 Football Team won a division title in a weak NFC East by going 5-2 in the final 7 games after a 2-7 start. We’ve seen the burgundy & gold turn mid-season losing teams into division…

summary: The NFL trade deadline is coming up in the relatively near future, with the last day to deal on Nov. 10. That comes right after a Week 9 contest with the L.A. full_text: The NFL trade deadline is coming up in the relatively near future, with the last day to deal on Nov. 10. That comes right after a Week 9 contest with the L.A. Rams, after which we should have a great idea about this Commanders season. Washington must surge and stack some wins right away, lest the season go south. Will the Commander be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline? That will depend on what happens next. We’ll see tons of projected trades in the coming weeks, and ESPN believes Washington general manager Adam Peters could make a minor move to add an asset. Bill Barnwell has the Commanders dealing from their offensive line depth, parting with a versatile chess piece with some serious experience for a Day 3 pick. The deal: Andrew Wylie gets sent to the Patriots for a 2027 sixth-round pick. Here’s Barnwell’s explanation for why this deal works for both sides: “It’s rare to see a team nearly run out of linemen in an NFL game, but the Patriots came close last week. With Mike Onwenu already sidelined and Will Campbell playing despite a knee injury , New England lost Alijah Vera-Tucker , Morgan Moses and Ben Brown during a win over the Jets , leaving the defending AFC champs with a mere five healthy offensive linemen. The line made it through the rest of the contest, and Moses could be back this week, but the Patriots are remarkably thin up front. Adding a versatile lineman to the mix makes a lot of sense. Wylie can play right tackle or either guard spot, allowing him to fill in across the lineup with relative ease. He’s buried on the Commanders’ depth chart and has played just 15 snaps this season despite the absence of left tackle Laremy Tunsil , which caused Brandon Coleman to move to the left side. With multiple sixth-round picks, the Patriots can afford to ship one off to add a veteran. And the Commanders could turn to practice-squaders Trent Scott or Esa Pole , who filled in for the Chiefs at left tackle last season, as their swing tackle after Wylie’s departure.” This isn’t a major deal, but would you make it? Also, do you think the Commanders should add talent or sell off even more pieces of this roster? Let us know in the article comments below.

title: Commanders at the bye: Sonny Styles provides hope for better defense
summary: The Commanders invested a ton in their defense, with money spent on younger players perceived to be on the ascent. Odafe Oweh came with a huge price tag. Nick Cross was supposed to lock down the secondary. Leo Chenal was to help anchor the linebacker corps with No. 7 overall NFL draft pick Sonny Styles. […]
full_text: The Commanders invested a ton in their defense, with money spent on younger players perceived to be on the ascent. Odafe Oweh came with a huge price tag . Nick Cross was supposed to lock down the secondary. Leo Chenal was to help anchor the linebacker corps with No. 7 overall NFL draft pick Sonny Styles. Amik Robertson was signed to fortify a young cornerback corps ready for better. This group, including K’Lavon Chaisson and Charles Omenihu, was supposed to help a previously old and slow unit get younger, faster and prove to be a better fit for Daronte Jones’ attacking scheme. Our John Portis did a great job breaking down why this scheme isn’t quite hitting like it should, so we won’t rehash all that here. Let’s focus instead on the personnel and the hits the depth chart has taken while allowing at least 23 points in every game this season and 30-plus in three straight . Those totals are surely a negative as the Commanders try to emerge from a rough start. There was great hope that the defense would be better. To this point, that has not been the case. The Numbers Total defense : 354.5 ypg (No. 26 overall) Scoring defense: 28.7 ppg (No. 29 overall) Rushing defense: 100.5 ypg (No. 11 overall) Passing defense: 254 ypg (No. 29 overall) Third down%: 44.4 (No. 25 overall) Red zone% : 81.8 (No. 32 overall) Takeaways: 8 (3 INT/5 FF) (No. 13 overall) Biggest weakness This Commanders secondary was always thought to be an issue. Then injuries hit, starting in the summer when Trey Amos’ balky ankle never got right in its recovery from a fractured fibula, landing him on injured reserve when the season started. Mike Sainristil simply couldn’t be trusted and has now essentially been benched, leaving smart signing and street free agent Rasul Douglas to take tons of unexpected snaps. Nick Cross missed significant time with an undisclosed issue stemming from a Week 2 hospitalization, depleting an already weak group of safeties that Jones expects so much from. All that has left the Commanders vulnerable in the back, especially when the team’s blitzes don’t get home. Cross and Amos are back now and Amik Robertson is playing like a No. 1 cover corner, providing some hope that the Commanders will be better down the line. Greatest strength The Commanders are allowing roughly 100 rushing yards per game, by far their best defensive metric within a group that doesn’t have much to brag about. That’s largely due to a defensive line that is stout and fairly deep. Charles Omenihu has been a pleasant addition , with Deatrich Wise adding heft to the group after being activated off the physically unable to perform list. While Daron Payne isn’t the pass rusher he once was, he’s still tough against the run. The defensive line funnels ball carriers to Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu, who have been good cleaning things up. Problem that must be solved The Commanders employ some creative blitzes and pressure schemes designed to put the opposing quarterback under duress. Washington is doing all that but not getting home enough or on a regular basis. They’re therefore left vulnerable and exposed to explosive plays that have proven to be back breakers. Outside of that Week 6 loss to the 49ers, Washington has generally been worse in the second half of games as teams adapt and adjust to what they’re doing. As Portis outlines, it sure seems like Washington gets in trouble when it’s not set or still changing strategy when the ball is snapped. Jones scheme seems solid, but it doesn’t seem like the Commanders are comfortable operating it yet. They need to figure that out in a hurry and get right or the season will get away from them. How would you categorize the Commanders’ biggest weakness, greatest strength and the problem that must be solved? Let us know in the comments below.

We wanted to cast as wide a net as possible. Activity around the NFL trade deadline has increased in recent seasons. Still, most of the players on our board will not be traded. The fun is in considering all the options. Contracts and the salary cap are important factors in facilitating trades. The Texans announced Tuesday that Tank Dell will return to action for the first time since Dec. 21, 2024, when he suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap against the Kansas City Chiefs. He’ll likely be on a snap count, but the standout receiver will join a room that also now includes Marvin Harrison, Jr., who had three catches for 34 yards in his debut. Cowboys & Eagles The Eagles are riding a four-game losing streak — their longest streak since Doug Peterson’s 4-11-1 season in 2020 and the first in the Nick Sirianni era. Both Philadelphia and Dallas enter the matchup with the same 2-4 record, so a victory would push the [the winner] to 3-4 overall [record]. Commanders What worked: The Commanders almost rallied back from a 23-3 deficit to upset the unbeaten 49ers in the second half. They fell by just one score, 23-17, and the comeback was a valiant effort from Jayden Daniels leading two touchdown drives and a defense that forced three consecutive three-and-outs. Washington contained San Francisco’s offensive weapons in the second half, namely by bringing Brock Purdy to the ground three times for a total loss of 15 yards and limiting him to just four passes in the final 30 minutes. The defense stepped up in critical moments; Jeremy Reaves recorded an important pass breakup in the secondary that prevented George Kittle from converting on third-and-11, and he also brought Christian McCaffrey down short on a third-and-8. Although they are tied for No. 1 in the NFL in turnover differential at +6, the Commanders still have a point differential of -40. Washington is generating takeaways and putting pressure on offenses, yet the turnovers aren’t solving its problems on offense and generating points to win games. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Review: Defense vs 49ers In the first half, the 49ers offense dominated, scoring touchdowns on three of their first five possessions and were well on their way to another score on the fourth possession before K’Lavon Chaisson punched the ball out and the Commanders got a turnover. In the second half, the 49ers scored a field goal on their first possession and then went three and out on three consecutive drives to end the game. That makes it sound like the Commanders came out with a terrible game plan and then switched at half time and it all worked perfectly. I don’t think that was the case. But there was a noticeable change in approach early on which didn’t work for Washington at all. That change lines up interestingly with the news that the Commanders have hired Steve Wilks to help with game planning on the defensive side of the ball. Wilks apparently started last week prior to the 49ers game and on the opening drives for the 49ers, we saw a big shift in philosophy from the Commanders defense. Under Daronte Jones, the Commanders defense are running their interpretation of Brian Flores’ scheme in Minnesota. It’s an ultra aggressive, blitz heavy scheme. But on the 49ers opening possession, the Commanders went away from that philosophy entirely and played a lot more basic zone coverage with just four man rushes up front. It didn’t work for them… What was new was the continued theme of dropping seven into zone coverage and rushing just four. We’ve seen already this season that the Commanders don’t have the defensive line capable of generating a consistent pass rush with just the front four. So to come into this game with the game plan of rushing four and dropping seven into coverage, rather than persisting with the blitzing style that has been the only form of pressure so far this year, is questionable. title: NFL Week 7 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
summary: Touchdowns for Tucker Kraft and Germie Bernard? Cardinals pull another upset? Revenge game for Trey Hendrickson? Let's predict 15 things for Week 7.
full_text:
Week 7 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Bears beat the Patriots 30-24 on  Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Can the Cardinals pull off an upset for the second straight week? What could Packers tight end Tucker Kraft 's stat line look like against the Lions? Is Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee a sneaky play in fantasy? And how many sacks will Ravens edge rusher Trey Hendrickson have against his former team?

 Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Arizona Cardinals +4.5 (+195 moneyline) vs. Denver Broncos 

 The Broncos haven't shown they can pull away when ahead this season. Denver is averaging only 3.4 yards per carry (third lowest in the league), and quarterback Bo Nix has thrown for just 230 yards over the past two games combined. Despite a strong showing against the Rams , Arizona's pass defense has given up plenty of explosive plays in 2026. But Denver rarely throws downfield to take advantage.

 The Broncos' defense should be a tough matchup for Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett , so I'm not expecting a big offensive day from the Cardinals. But this matchup looks like it will be decided by a field goal, and Arizona could come out on top.

 
 

 

 Kansas City Chiefs +2.5 (+120 moneyline) at Seattle Seahawks 

 Kansas City has the defense to keep this close even if Seattle slows down QB Patrick Mahomes . The Chiefs create pressure on nearly 39% of dropbacks, and QB Sam Darnold has completed only 38% of his throws under pressure this season. Seattle's struggles with run blocking could leave him handling too many difficult passing downs.

 Offensively, running back  Kenneth Walker III faces a tough rushing matchup against his former team, but Seattle has had issues covering RBs as receivers. That gives Kansas City another way to move the ball and win this outright.

 

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 Tucker Kraft , TE, Green Bay Packers : 9 targets, 7 receptions, 87 receiving yards, 1 TD 

 Kraft has the benefit of going against a Lions defense that has allowed 27% of its targets to opposing tight ends, the second-highest rate in the league. But it gets better. Based on player tracking data from NFL Next Gen Stats, Detroit linebackers Malcolm Rodriguez , Derrick Barnes and Jack Campbell all bite on play-action more than average . The Packers haven't used play-action a ton this season, but Kraft could be the beneficiary whenever they do Sunday.

 
 

 Ted Hurst III , WR, Tampa Bay Buccaneers : 6 targets, 4 receptions, 79 yards, 1 TD 

 I've had my eye on predicting a breakout game by Hurst for a few weeks now, and I think it will finally happen  against the Panthers . Hurst has a vertical route profile, running either a go route or deep fade on 21% of his routes -- 11th-highest rate among wide receivers with at least 60 routes this season. That means high variance and high upside in any given week.

 So why a big game this Sunday? Well for starters, there seems to be a good chance quarterback Baker Mayfield will be back from his thumb injury . Emeka Egbuka is also out, which should lead to even more targets for Hurst. The Panthers also have backup cornerbacks in both outside spots. And on top of all that, Carolina plays an above-average amount of single-high coverage, which helps with deep outside shots.

 
 

 Zach Allen , DL, Denver Broncos : 2.0 sacks, 7 pressures, 25% pass rush win rate 

 Allen is off to a hot start this season with 4.5 sacks and a 19.6% pass rush win rate that's tied for sixth best among interior rushers. Now, he gets a perfect matchup against the Cardinals ' interior offensive line.

 Allen figures to face right guard Jon Gaines II more than anyone else, and Gaines ranks last in pass block win rate out of 71 qualifying guards. The rest of the interior isn't much better: Left guard Isaac Seumalo and center Hjalte Froholdt have 12th-percentile and sixth-percentile pass block win rates, respectively, at their positions.

 

 

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Keenan Allen , WR, Indianapolis Colts (rostered in 42.4% of ESPN leagues) 

 Allen is worth considering for fantasy managers navigating bye weeks. He has averaged 9.6 targets and 14.7 fantasy points over the past three games, becoming one of Daniel Jones ' most reliable targets with Alec Pierce on IR ( heel ). The Vikings are a tough matchup , but their aggressive blitzing could lead to more quick throws, which suits Allen's game. His touchdown upside is limited, though the consistent targets make him a viable flex option.

 
 

 Malik Washington , WR, Miami Dolphins (36.6%) 

 Washington has seen at least five targets in every game this season, including eight or more in three contests. He has also scored at least 11 fantasy points in three straight games. Miami hasn't been able to do much downfield, but Washington showcases reliability on shorter throws. That should help him against a Jets defense that plays a lot of Cover 2 to limit big plays.

 Washington should see enough targets to provide a decent fantasy floor, with more upside if he scores his first touchdown of the season.

 
 

 Tanner McKee , QB, Philadelphia Eagles (4.6%) 

 McKee is an intriguing sleeper with quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season ( blood clots ). He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers last week and now faces a Cowboys defense that has allowed 21.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks (fifth most in the league). Dallas has also given up 11 passing touchdowns this season.

 McKee attempted 45 passes last week, and he has the targets to reach the end zone with DeVonta Smith  and Dallas Goedert  (both questionable to play). He's worth considering in deeper single-QB leagues and as a QB2 in superflex formats.

 

 

 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers

 After scoring at least one touchdown in his first three games, St. Brown hasn't reached the end zone in his past two. However, he is still averaging 11.4 targets per game. The throwbacks were well-represented in Week 6 of the NFL slate. While that's still the case this week, it's the alternates that lead the way -- including two monochromatic looks from the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions .

 

 Houston will be wearing its "battle red" combination, which the team first unveiled in 2024. It's all red from head to toe complete with a similarly colored matte lid that includes a new bullhorn logo. The numbers are deep steel blue with a liberty white trim, while the red pants boast blue and white stripes. The  New York Giants will counter with all-white. 

 Also unveiled in 2024, the Lions are rocking their all-black threads against the Green Bay Packers . The black jersey and pants include a Honolulu Blue matte helmet with leaping Lions logo in silver. There's also a black stripe across the middle. Detroit first wore black uniforms in 1948 before bringing it back in 2005 as an alternate. The team stopped wearing them after the 2007 season before returning it in 2024. 

 The Dallas Cowboys will don their color rush look against the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football." Dallas unveiled these threads in 2015 with a silver helmet before an arctic white one debuted in 2022. The all-white combination has navy blue numbers and on the shoulder for a neat look.

 Though alternates are the headliners, fans of the classics aren't leaving empty handed either in Week 7.

 The Seattle Seahawks are wearing their throwbacks from the 1990s, complete with royal blue jerseys and silver pants and helmet. Seattle wore them last week on "Thursday Night Football." For the first time this season, the Atlanta Falcons and New York Jets are rocking classic uniforms. New York's is appropriately named "The Classic," and the all-white look pays homage to the 1968 championship season. It also includes uniform details from 1998 to 2018. title: Betting buzz: Sportsbooks, bettors join the National Tight Ends Day frenzy
summary: On the fourth Sunday of every October since 2018, bettors and books alike celebrate National Tight Ends Day.
full_text:
Everything that happens in sports has additional context when viewed from a sports betting perspective. From season-changing injuries to record-setting moments and so much more, the sports news cycle will constantly and significantly affect the sports betting industry. 

 Our NFL betting buzz file, with contributions from David Purdum, Doug Greenberg and others, aims to provide fans a look at the sports betting stories that are driving the conversation throughout each week of the season.  

 Key links: NFL futures | Awards odds |  Sports betting home  |  DraftKings   

 
 Oct. 23: Sportsbooks, bettors join the National Tight Ends Day frenzy 
 By Doug Greenberg 

 In 2018, the Supreme Court struck down the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act, clearing the way for states to legalize sports betting nationwide. That same year marked the beginning of another momentous occasion that has become a stalwart of NFL betting every season.

 On the fourth Sunday in October -- Oct. 25 in 2026 -- the NFL celebrates National Tight Ends Day, a tongue-in-cheek commemoration of football's most underappreciated skill position. Since San Francisco 49ers tight ends Garrett Celek and George Kittle helped bring the honorary day to life eight years ago, it has become a staple of the betting world, with bookmakers taking extra notice and bettors staking extra cash backing players of the position.

 

 "National Tight Ends Day has become a fun day for football fans, and we've seen the excitement around it grow each year," DraftKings director of sports operation Johnny Avello told ESPN via email. "This is a prime example of a way to have fun with the content on our platform."

 The sportsbook noted that it sees more engagement on tight end player props on National Tight Ends Day than in any other week of a given season. On the day last season (Oct. 28), Hard Rock Bet says it saw tight ends account for 25% of all player prop selections compared to 11% the Sunday before and 9% the Sunday after. For touchdown scorer markets, that number jumped to 42% against 16% and 10% on the surrounding Sundays.

 BetMGM specifically points out that its five most-bet players for props by tickets on the day in 2025 were all tight ends: Dallas Goedert , Tyler Warren , Tucker Kraft , Travis Kelce and Kittle.

 Kraft celebrated by putting up a monster stat line of seven catches for 143 yards and two touchdowns in the Green Bay Packers ' Week 8 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers . Caesars Sportsbook head of football Joey Feazel said that "bettors certainly prospered" by backing Kraft and that the book has had to be more aware of bettor activity during this particular Sunday.

 "This week certainly will increase the amount of action on tight ends in all facets of the games, which in turn has the ability to shorten touchdown prices when the amount of action is significantly increased," Feazel said via email. "But at the end of the day it will simply be the implied probability of each TE to score a touchdown."

 Even with all the hype surrounding tight ends for the day, there are only four players with anytime touchdown odds shorter than +200, according to DraftKings odds as of Thursday evening: Brock Bowers (+110), Trey McBride (+130), Sam LaPorta (+170) and Kraft (+175). Those could -- and probably will -- change closer to kickoff as bettors pile on their favorite TEs and take advantage of the many promotions sportsbooks will be running for the occasion.

 Sportsbooks, like Caesars, also plan to offer special markets, such as most tight end receiving yards, tight end touchdown combos and other milestone props. Last year, Hard Rock offered leaguewide touchdown ladders and a tight end to score in every Sunday 1 p.m. ET game (+1750), among other specialties.

 You can find our bets for National Tight Ends Day here .

 

 Oct. 18: Cardinals pulls biggest upset of season, add to Rams' struggles 
 

 By David Purdum 

 The Los Angeles Rams won over the betting public in the offseason and kicked off the regular season as the clear-cut Super Bowl favorites. They haven't lived up to that billing so far, suffering a new low Sunday.

 The Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals as 13.5-point home favorites in the biggest upset of the season based on point spread. They are only the second double-digit favorite to lose outright in the past two seasons, joining the Green Bay Packers , who lost to the Carolina Panthers in Week 9 last November as 13.5-point favorites.

 

 Arizona's upset shredded survivor pool entries around the nation.

 The Rams were picked by the most contestants in ESPN Survivor contests and in the high-stakes contests Circa Survivor and Circa Grandissimo in Las Vegas. Throw in the  Indianapolis Colts ' loss to the underdog and previously winless Tennessee Titans , and the Circa contests lost greater than 50% of the remaining entries.

 The loss drops the Rams to 2-4 on the season, the same record as the Cardinals. The Rams are the second preseason Super Bowl favorite in the past 20 years to lose four of their first six games, per SportsOddsHistory.com. (The 2015 Seattle Seahawks  started 2-4 and went on to lose in the divisional round of the playoffs.)

 Los Angeles was favored to win the Super Bowl at 5-1 ahead of Week 1. No other team had Super Bowl odds shorter than 10-1. The Rams were +950 to win the Super Bowl on Sunday night at DraftKings, behind four teams.

 More bets were placed and more money was wagered on the Rams to win the Super Bowl than any other team in the offseason at most sportsbooks.

 

 Oct. 11: Who wants to win the NFC East? 
 

 By Doug Greenberg 

 Week 5 was one to forget for the NFC East, to say the least.

 It started Thursday night when the Dallas Cowboys lost outright to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after closing as 8.5-point favorites, tied with four other games as the biggest upset of the season, according to DraftKings odds.

 Not only were the Cowboys heavily backed on the spread and in moneyline parlays at multiple sportsbooks, they were also the most popular pick in both ESPN Survivor (40% of the remaining field) and the $1,000-per-entry Circa Survivor (2,554 entries, 42.8% of the remaining field). It's the third time in the season's first five weeks that ESPN Survivor's most popular pick lost.

 But the misery didn't end there for the division. The Philadelphia Eagles led off the day in London by seemingly notching a winning field goal with eight seconds left against the Jacksonville Jaguars , giving them a 99.5% chance to win the game, per ESPN Analytics.

 Jacksonville returned the ensuing kickoff to the Philadelphia 35-yard line with one second left, allowing the Jags to kick a winning field goal as time expired. It was the first game in the Super Bowl era that featured two go-ahead field goals in the final 10 seconds of the fourth quarter, according to ESPN Research.

 Then, there was the most bizarre result of the week, possibly the season. The New York Giants and Washington Commanders played a mistake-ridden game into an overtime where neither team scored, including in the matchup's final moments when the Commanders somehow ran out the clock while in field goal range.

 "In the closing minutes and overtime, the live moneyline market was in complete chaos," Joey Feazel, Caesars Sportsbook head of football, told ESPN via email. "Every big play looked like it might decide the game and the book's fate, only for the final whistle to leave everyone staring at the screen wondering what had just happened. It was 90-plus minutes of drama, countless swings in perceived win probability, and in the end, nobody got the outcome they were expecting."

 That's right: None of the NFC East teams recorded a win in Week 5 ... despite two of the teams playing each other.

 Going into "Thursday Night Football," the Cowboys had been the +105 favorites to win the division and immediately dropped to +164 following their upset loss, tying them with the Eagles. After Week 5,…

title: Will Niners have edge with ex-Falcons coach facing Penix?
summary: With all of the familiarity between Morris and the Falcons, Sunday's game should come down to execution.
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Bijan Robinson has maintained a close relationship with Raheem Morris. It makes sense. Morris was the Atlanta Falcons ' head coach for two of the first three seasons of Robinson's career.

 On Sunday, the two men will meet again under different circumstances.

 Robinson will be helping to lead the Falcons' offense as one of the top running backs in the league. Morris, who has called Robinson the best player in the NFL multiple times, will be back in Atlanta as the San Francisco 49ers ' defensive coordinator. Morris was fired as Atlanta's coach in January after back-to-back eight-win campaigns.

 Robinson said he spoke to Morris just a few weeks ago, and he's relishing the chance to face off against a man he calls a "father figure" to him.

 "He's always going to be family to me no matter if we compete or not," Robinson said. "But yeah, man, he still talks to all of his players, because that's just who he is."

 Morris is glad Penix has recovered from the torn left ACL that ended his season last year on Nov. 16.

 "He's back healthy and he's probably everything that you thought and hoped for as far as being a play-action passer, a guy that can push the ball down the field, can make all the throws, go through the whole process," Morris said. "Just one of those guys that I have a lot of appreciation for and love for."

 The Falcons players on offense who have been here the past several years will be going up against a defense run by a man who knows them all too well.  And that 49ers defense has been potent regardless of opponent familiarity. San Francisco is allowing the fourth-fewest points per game (18.3) and the fifth-fewest yards per game (300).

 Atlanta (2-4) must perform against Morris and the undefeated Niners or risk losing three straight games and moving to 0-4 at home. A fifth loss in the first seven games is not how the Falcons wanted to start off under new head coach Kevin Stefanski.

 The Falcons' biggest issue on offense is one the Chicago Bears exploited last week in a 31-23 Falcons loss. The Bears pressured quarterback Michael Penix Jr . 46.2% of the time, the highest rate Penix has faced this season. Chicago sacked Penix five times and blitzed on more than half of his dropbacks.

 The results were not good. For the season, Penix has the worst EPA per dropback under quick pressure in the NFL (-1.17). He is 3-of-15 for 17 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions in those scenarios.

 With no pressure at all, Penix has the fourth-best EPA per dropback in the league (0.40). So, it is imperative that the Falcons figure out how to better protect him.

 "Any game you go into, you want to protect your quarterback," Stefanski said. "And I think you protect your quarterback literally with the protection, but also you protect the quarterback with how guys get open, how we get the ball out of our hands, how we run the ball, all those type of things."

 

 No defensive coordinator knows Penix better than Morris. He was part of the regime that drafted Penix and was a major proponent of the QB for two years. How much does that come into play during the week? A little bit.

 Falcons defense coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, who has a long history with Morris, said he will speak with offensive coordinator Tommy Rees about Morris and his scheme. Stefanski calls situations like this "overblown."

 "Of course, Raheem has great insight into our personnel, and our coaches have great insight into Raheem and he knows that," Stefanski said. "So, I think you can get into, 'Well, he knows that we know that they know,' and I don't think it's as useful as it may seem. Now having said that, of course, anytime we're playing against a coach or a player that someone has knowledge on, you sit and you talk to your players, and you talk to your coaches and you try to get as much insight on people as possible."

 Penix, for his part, said he is looking forward to the chess match with his former head coach.

 "It's going to be exciting," Penix said. "It's going to be good to be able to see him again, but we got to find a way to obviously put points on the board against the defense."

 Contributing: Nick Wagoner

title: Fantasy's greatest tight end enshrined in ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame

full_text:
Fantasy football is all about fun, competition and camaraderie, but it's also another way to appreciate the best of the best in the NFL. For more than three decades, ESPN Fantasy has been here with you, celebrating peak performers and magical moments.

 Presenting the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame   , which honors the best players and acknowledges the most memorable moments since the advent of our game in 1995, the first year that fantasy football was available on ESPN.com. 

 Take me to the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame 

 Class of 2026 Week 7 Inductee: Tony Gonzalez 

 3,510.7 fantasy points 
1,325 receptions, 15,127 receiving yards, 111 total TDs 

 The highest-scoring tight end in fantasy football history and one who helped set the template for the modern tight end, Gonzalez's 3,510.7 career points give him a lead of more than 500 over the next-best at the position, Jason Witten. Over a 17-year career, he paced his position in fantasy points six times (1999-2001, '03-04, '08), matching Travis Kelce for the most ever by a tight end, and he finished second an additional five times (2002, '06-07, '12-13). Gonzalez was as safe a fantasy starter as there was, missing only two of 272 possible games in his career, and scoring 15 or more fantasy points 99 times, also the most by any tight end.

Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights  for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder give us  final-score picks for every game.

 What we're hearing on the Steelers:  Despite the return of running back Rico Dowdle from a toe injury, Jaylen Warren will remain a major factor in the Steelers' offense. Players are sold on him as the alpha, and, as tight end Pat Freiermuth recently told me, great things happen when Warren gets the ball -- and he's going to get the ball a lot. The Steelers want to use two backs, though, because it's a long season and Dowdle complements Warren's burst with a bruising style. Expect that to continue, with a slant toward Warren.  -- Jeremy Fowler 

 What we're hearing on the Saints: The Saints spent the entire week practicing in Paris leading up to the game, and they're thankful for it. Several Saints players said it took them several days to acclimate to the six-hour time change after the plane ride from New York -- where they played the Giants -- to their practice facility in Versailles. "That's a great part of how we do it here, by today I felt normal," LB Kaden Elliss said Thursday afternoon in France. -- Katherine Terrell 

 Stat to know: The Saints have made the most of their red zone trips, scoring a touchdown on 84% of their red zone drives, the second-highest rate in the NFL (49ers: 85%). -- ESPN Research 

 

 Bold prediction: Steelers LB Payton Wilson will record 12 or more tackles. Wilson ranks second in vertical distance traveled in the first second after the snap on a run play, and that has helped him accrue a strong 16% tackle rate this season (ninth best in the NFL among players with at least 150 defensive snaps). -- Walder 

 Injuries: Saints | Steelers 

 Fantasy nugget: Steelers WR Germie Bernard has seen at least nine targets and scored 14 or more fantasy points in each of his past two games. With Roman Wilson ( finger ) on injured reserve, Bernard should continue seeing a ton of targets. He also has a favorable matchup against a Saints defense that has allowed the sixth-most passing yards per game over the past three weeks. See Week 7 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: The Steelers have hit the over in four straight games, and New Orleans gives them ways to keep scoring. The Saints allow 4.8 yards per carry and struggle to pressure QBs, which should give Warren running room and Aaron Rodgers time to throw. Meanwhile, Saints WR Chris Olave matches up well against Pittsburgh's zone coverages, giving New Orleans a way to answer offensively. Read more . -- Maldonado

title: Inside the silent messages Boye Mafe sends every game day
summary: The Bengals defensive end uses sign language to say "I love you" to his mother, Bola, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2018.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Before the chaos of each game unfolds, Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Boye Mafe has a conversation that centers him in a special place.

 He closes his eyes and starts talking to his mother, Bola, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2018. And in those moments, Mafe lays out his vision for what's about to unfold.

 I know you're watching over me. I want to put on a show for you. I love you and this is what I'm going to do for you. 

 Then he'll wrap up the message by using American Sign Language to say "I love you" before he continues the rest of his pregame routine. Mafe does the same after each sack.

 But it's about more than signs. Everything Mafe does is about what he signals. From those messages to Bola, to his pregame outfits, to how he plays, it's all about honoring the systems and structures that built him into one of the NFL's leading pass rushers and a Super Bowl champion.

 

 "I try not to let circumstances dictate who I am," Mafe told ESPN. "At the end of the day, I am who I am and I want to be true to who I am."

 That doesn't come easily. Mafe, the son of proud Nigerians, grapples with a phenomenon that is common among those with generational ties to other places -- the more time passes, the harder it is to stay connected to those roots.

 But all it takes is one glance on game day to see just how strong those ties are.

 How Boye Mafe's mother impacted her community 
 To fully understand why Mafe signs to his late mother requires understanding his upbringing in the western suburbs of Minneapolis.

 Mafe and his siblings often communicate via American Sign Language. Starting with his older sister, Tayo, they all decided to study it in high school as their alternative language. And over the years the practice has stuck, even during games. Once, Tayo recalled signing to Mafe when he suffered an injury at Minnesota. He quickly signaled back that it wasn't anything serious.

 Of all Mafe's six siblings, he is the one who spent the most time in their mother's seamstress shop on 1110 Lowery Avenue in North Minneapolis. There, Bola did more than mend clothes. She served as a cultural hub for many, not just Nigerians or those with Yoruba roots.

 And she invested in the community. She volunteered at a battered women's shelter, made vests for Mafe's entire church choir and often let her customers have some extended credit.

 

 "She had a lot of patience because sometimes people couldn't pay and she was like, 'Oh, pay me later,'" said Angie Onayiga, one of Bola's longtime friends. "She still gave them the clothes, sold things for them."

 When Bola was diagnosed with cancer while Boye was in high school, the bond between mother and son deepened. Boye and his brother Domi did everything they could to make sure Bola was as comfortable as possible as the disease progressed.

 How she fought the disease made a lasting impact on Boye.

 "Not one day I see her cry or one day I see her down sad or [say] woe is me," Boye said. "She always found the light and made joy in any moment she could.

 "I try to bring that into my life."

 And he needed those lessons as he got deeper into his NFL career.

 Why Boye Mafe was a better fit for the Bengals 
 Those who have spent time around Mafe know where his temperament comes from.

 "My mom didn't waste words," Tayo said. "He's like that. He just has this quieter confidence. When he walks in a room, you just know it. And my mom had that."

 But that confidence was tested during the end of his run with the Seattle Seahawks , who selected him in the second round of the 2022 draft out of Minnesota.

 In Seattle, there was a consensus about what Mafe brought to the Seahawks -- a high-motor player, an energetic pass rusher and someone who could develop into a hybrid edge player who could also drop into pass coverage when needed.

 

 In 2023, his second season in the NFL, Mafe started in all 16 of his appearances and totaled a career-high nine sacks. But over the next two seasons, those numbers dwindled, as did the amount of time he spent on the field.

 He recalled a particular three-game stretch during one of those seasons when he was "in the dumps" about not playing well. Then he remembered what he learned from his mom.

 "I had to remind myself I am who I am," Mafe said. "And I thought about how she would do it and what she would do in those situations. And you always got to look at the glass half full.

 "And when I started looking at the glass half full in a lot of situations, it makes getting through tough times happen, and tough times also will pass."

 This offseason, the Bengals had a glaring need at edge rusher. Trey Hendrickson , an All-Pro defensive end who totaled 61 sacks in five seasons with Cincinnati, left in free agency and signed with the Baltimore Ravens . Joseph Ossai landed a big contract with the New York Jets , making pass rush an even bigger need.

 Mafe fit exactly what the Bengals were looking for.

 

 "The talent was always there," said Bengals assistant Sean Desai, who was in Seattle when the Seahawks drafted Mafe. "And it was an opportunity for him, I feel like, to come to a place and get a fresh start in terms of being a full-time player."

 Through five games this season, Mafe is playing a career-high 74% of his team's defensive snaps. He is one of three Bengals players who each have a team-high three sacks and is seventh in the NFL in pass rush win rate, per ESPN Analytics and NFL Next Gen Stats.

 "He seems to me like a guy that's free-spirited, in terms of just enjoying the journey, and he plays with great energy on game day," Bengals defensive coordinator Al Golden said. "He's getting better technically at all the things that we're asking him to do, which is awesome to see. And we just need him to keep growing."

 How Boye Mafe stays true to his family's heritage 

 Every time Mafe takes the field, he carries a piece of his family's culture. His father, Adewale, is in Nigeria and recently celebrated his 70th birthday with a gathering of roughly 500 friends and family, including Boye.

 Mafe sports a decal of the Nigerian flag -- next to a U.S. flag -- on the back of his helmet, honoring a place he knows firsthand.

 Like four of his siblings, Mafe -- who was born in Minnesota -- spent eighth grade at a boarding school in Nigeria, a move that Bola and Adewale Mafe made to immerse their children in their culture and give them a true feel of where they came from.

 His mother shaped how Mafe represented that, too. Growing up, he had several pieces of traditional Nigerian garb made by Bola.

 

 On certain game days this season, Mafe will wear an agbada, the long, flowing robe predominantly worn by Yoruba people. Mafe still has some of the fabrics that were in Bola's shop on Lowery Avenue and will sometimes have his current tailor use them in new designs.

 Instilling that sense of culture has been paramount to their family dynamic, even as the generations grow older.

 "[Their parents have] always been involved in organizations that maintain the culture," said Tayo, who also started a Nigerian organization of her own. "They've always put us around [it] and made sure that we knew their culture.

 "But they're also very open, knowing that we are here in the diaspora and that it's like you are living in two cultures."

 Mafe has remained true to those principles and to the people who raised him. With each sign to his mother during game days and so many other aspects of his life, he is determined to signal to the world why he is who he is.

 "At the end of the day, it's something that's demonstrative and you can see," Mafe said. "It's one thing for me to say and talk to her, but it's another thing for me to show."
